description: The molecule is a beta-D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphinganine in which the acyl group specified is tetracosanoyl. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and an allergen. It derives from a tetracosanoic acid.
The molecule is the hydrochloride salt of doxapram. It has a role as an antispasmodic drug, a muscle relaxant and a cholinergic antagonist. It contains a doxapram.

The molecule is a steroid glucosiduronic acid that is 5alpha-dihydrotestosterone having a single beta-D-glucuronic acid residue attached at position 17. It has a role as a human urinary metabolite and a rat metabolite. It is a beta-D-glucosiduronic acid, an 11beta-hydroxy steroid, a 3-hydroxy steroid and a steroid glucosiduronic acid. It derives from a 17beta-hydroxy-5alpha-androstan-3-one.

The molecule is a hydroxy fatty acid ascaroside anion that is the conjugate base of oscr#27, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of an oscr#27.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid in which all three methyl hydrogens are replaced by chlorines. It has a role as an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic metabolite. It is a conjugate acid of a trichloroacetate.

The molecule is an amino tetrasaccharide that consists of 2-acetamido-beta-D-galactopyranose, beta-D-glucopyranosyl and 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-6-O-sulfo-D-glucopyranose residues joined in sequence by (1->4) glycosidic bonds. It is a member of acetamides, an oligosaccharide sulfate and an amino tetrasaccharide.

The molecule is a hexonic acid that is 2-ketohexanoic acid carrying six hydroxy substituents at positions 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite. It derives from a D-glucaric acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 2-dehydro-D-glucarate(1-).

The molecule is a homodetic cyclic peptide that consists of L-valine as the amino acid residue cyclised by amide bonds between positions 2 and 3, position 6 and 7 and position 9 and 10. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antineoplastic agent, an antiviral agent, a bacterial metabolite, an antiprotozoal drug, an EC 5.99.1.3 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor, an apoptosis inducer, an antibacterial agent and an antifungal agent. It is a homodetic cyclic peptide, a macrocycle, a member of 1,3-oxazoles, a furanone, a sulfonamide and a dipeptide.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that consists of propionic acid bearing two methoxy substituents at position 3 and 4 respectively. It has a role as an EC 6.4.1.2 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase) inhibitor, a plant metabolite, a human blood serum metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a propionic acid.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the secondary amino group of validoxylamine A; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a valiaminium(1+). It is a conjugate acid of a validoxylamine A.

The molecule is a tricyclic diterpenoid that is ent-cassa-12,15-diene in which the hydrogen at position 3 has been replaced by an alpha-methyl group. It derives from a hydride of an ent-cassa-12,15-diene.
The molecule is a dipeptide formed from L-valine and L-proline residues. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-valine and a L-proline.

The molecule is a tetrahydroxyflavanone that is (2S)-flavanone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 5, 7, 3' and 4' and a prenyl group at position 5'. Isolated from Macaranga tanarius, it exhibits radical scavenging activity. It has a role as a metabolite and an antioxidant. It is a tetrahydroxyflavanone and a member of 4'-hydroxyflavanones.

The molecule is a dihydroxydocosahexaenoate that is the conjugate base of (4Z,7Z,10Z,12E,16Z,19Z)-14,22-dihydroxydocosahexaenoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an all-cis-docosa-4,7,10,13,16,19-hexaenoate. It is a conjugate base of a (4Z,7Z,10Z,12E,16Z,19Z)-14,22-dihydroxyicosapentaenoic acid.

The molecule is a pseudoguaianolide with anti-inflammatory activity isolated from the aerial parts of Inula hupehensis. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a plant metabolite. It is a gamma-lactone, an acetate ester, a cyclic ketone, an organic heterotricyclic compound and a pseudoguaianolide.
The molecule is a primary alcohol that is ethanol substituted by an ethoxy group at position 2. It has a role as a protic solvent and a metabolite.

The molecule is the hydrochloride salt of (S)-chlorfenac. It has a role as an antiglaucoma drug, an EC 1.8.1.3 [aldehyde reductase (NADPH)] inhibitor and an antihypertensive agent. It contains a (S)-chlorfenac.

The molecule is a triply-charged monocarboxylic acid anion arising from deprotonation of the carboxy and phosphate OH groups of phosphonopyruvic acid; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from pyruvate(2-). It is a conjugate base of an O-phosphonatopyruvate(1-).

The molecule is a 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-1D-myo-inositol(1-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH group of 1-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-D-myo-inositol; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an oleate. It is a conjugate base of a 1-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-D-myo-inositol.

The molecule is a diterpenoid isolated from Ajuga bracteosa and has been shown to exhibit antifeedant activity. It has a role as an antifeedant, a plant metabolite and an EC 3.6.3.9 (Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase) inhibitor. It is a furofuran, an acetate ester, a diterpenoid, a spiro-epoxide and a cyclic acetal.

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (10Z,13Z,16Z)-docosatrienoic acid. It is a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA and an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (10Z,13Z,16Z)-docosa-10,13,16-trienoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (10Z,13Z,16Z)-docosatrienoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is a pyrrolizine alkaloid that is jacoline in which the tertiary amino function has been oxidised to the corresponding N-oxide. It has a role as a Jacobaea metabolite and an insecticide. It is a macrocyclic lactone, an organic heterotricyclic compound, a pyrrolizine alkaloid, a tertiary amine oxide and a spiro-epoxide.
The molecule is the tetracation of 3,6-bis(dimethylamino)acridine. It has a role as an antiseptic drug and a fluorochrome.
The molecule is N-Acetylneuraminic acid in which the anomeric centre has alpha configuration. It has a role as an epitope and a mouse metabolite.
The molecule is a dipeptide formed from L-leucine and L-alanine residues. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-leucine and a L-alanine.

The molecule is a steroid saponin that consists of (3beta,5alpha,6beta)-17-hydroxyestra-2,4-diene substituted by an amino group at position 3 and a beta-D-xylopyranosyl-(1->2)-[beta-D-glucopyranosyl-(1->4)]-beta-D-fucopyranosyloxy residue at position 17. Isolated from Ornithogalum thyrsoides and Galtonia candicans, it exhibits antineoplastic activity. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a steroid alkaloid, a deoxy hexoside, a monosaccharide derivative, a steroid saponin and a tertiary amino compound.

The molecule is a hydrochloride obtained by reaction of (S)-ethcathinone with one equivalent of hydrochloric acid. It has a role as an opioid analgesic, a mu-opioid receptor agonist and a dopamine uptake inhibitor. It contains a (S)-ethcathinone(1+). It is an enantiomer of a (R)-ethcathinone hydrochloride.

The molecule is a chloropyridine that consists of picolinic acid bearing two chloro substituents at positions 3 and 5. It has a role as an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a herbicide. It derives from a picolinic acid.
The molecule is a dipeptide composed of L-lysine and D-glutamic acid joined by a peptide linkage. It has a role as a metabolite.

The molecule is a 1-(alk-1-enyl)-2-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine in which the alkenyl and acyl groups are specified as (Z)-hexadec-1-enyl and hexadecanoyl respectively. It has a role as a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hexadecanoic acid.

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as palmitoyl and 8Z,11Z,14Z-eicosatrienoyl respectively. It has a role as a mouse metabolite. It derives from an all-cis-icosa-8,11,14-trienoic acid and a hexadecanoic acid.

The molecule is a ketohexose monophosphate that is 3-deoxy-D-threo-hex-2-ulopyranosonic acid carrying an additional phospho substituent at position 6. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a D-threo-hex-2-ulosonic acid.

The molecule is an O-acyl-L-serine that is L-serine in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by a 3-acetamido-2,6-dideoxy-beta-D-xylo-hexopyranos-4-yl group. It derives from a N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosamine and a D-glucopyranosamine.

The molecule is an amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of N(6)-hydroxylysine; major species at pH 7.3 It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a L-lysinium(1+). It is a tautomer of a N(6)-hydroxylysine.
The molecule is a carbohydrate ester formed between 2,3-dihydroxyoctadecanoic acid and alpha,alpha-trehalose. It derives from an alpha,alpha-trehalose and a 2,3-dihydroxyoctadecanoic acid.

The molecule is a pyrimidine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate having (2S)-4-oxo-3,4-dihydrouracil as the nucleobase. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a uridine 5'-monophosphate.
The molecule is an organic anion obtained by deprotonation of the tetrazole nitrogen and one of the triazole nitrogens of rucaparib. It is a conjugate base of a rucaparib.

The molecule is a flavanone glycoside that is (+)-taxifolin substituted by an alpha-D-arabinopyranosyl residue at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite and an antioxidant. It is an alpha-D-arabinopyranoside, a member of 3'-hydroxyflavanones, a flavanone glycoside, a monosaccharide derivative, a tetrahydroxyflavanone and a member of 4'-hydroxyflavanones. It derives from an alpha-D-arabinopyranose and a (+)-taxifolin.

The molecule is a monoterpenoid that is cyclohex-2-en-1-ol substituted by an isopropylidene group at position 4. It has been isolated from the essential oils of Lippia citriodora and Ocimum canum. It has a role as a plant metabolite, a volatile oil component and an antileishmanial agent. It is a primary alcohol and a monoterpenoid.
The molecule is a tartrate(3-) that is the conjugate base of L-tartaric acid. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a human metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a L-tartaric acid.

The molecule is an abietane diterpenoid isolated from the stem bark of Fraxinus sieboldiana. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a tetracyclic diterpenoid, an abietane diterpenoid and a cyclic ether.

The molecule is a steroid alkaloid that consists of 4-methylidenecycloartanol having an N,N-dimethylamino substituent at the 2beta-position and an oxo group at position 3. It has been isolated from the roots of Scorzonera judaica. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a member of cyclopropanes, a tertiary amino compound, a steroid alkaloid and a monocarboxylic acid amide.

The molecule is a monomethoxyflavone that is the 3-methoxy derivative of scutellarein. It has been isolated from the roots of Rubia yunnanensis. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, a plant metabolite and an EC 1.8.1.4 (trypanothione-disulfide reductase) inhibitor. It is a dihydroxyflavone and a monomethoxyflavone. It derives from a scutellarein.

The molecule is a diterpene lactone isolated from the whole plants of Ajuga ciliata. It has a role as an antifeedant and a plant metabolite. It is a gamma-lactone, an acetate ester, a butenolide, a diterpene lactone and an epoxide.

The molecule is a member of the class of pyrazoles that is 1H-pyrazole carrying an additional phenyl substituent at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite and an EC 2.7.10.2 (non-specific serine/threonine protein kinase) inhibitor.
The molecule is a guanidine derivative that is agmatine in which one of the hydrogens attached to N-1 has been replaced by an 8-aminooctyl group. It derives from an agmatine.
The molecule is a myo-inositol tetrakisphosphate having the four phosphate groups located at positions 1, 2, 4 and 6. It derives from a myo-inositol.
The molecule is a diterpenoid that is (+)-kolavenol in which the hydroxy group at position 19 has been oxidised to give the corresponding ketone. It derives from a hydride of an isopimarane.

The molecule is a (5Z,8Z,14Z)-13,14-dihydroxyicosatrienoate obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group of (5Z,8Z,13R,14Z)-13,14-dihydroxyicosa-5,8,14-trienoic acid; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of a (5Z,8Z,13R,14Z)-13,14-dihydroxyicosatrienoic acid. It is an enantiomer of a (5Z,8Z,13S,14Z)-13,14-dihydroxyicosatrienoate.

The molecule is a benzamide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoic acid with the amino group of p-[2-(dimethylamino)ethyl]benzene-1-amine. It has a role as an anti-arrhythmia drug and a beta-adrenergic antagonist.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the tertiary amino function of nicotine. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a norbelladine(1+).

The molecule is a non-proteinogenic alpha-amino acid that is 2,3-diaminopentanoic acid in which both hydrogens at position 5 are replaced by fluoro groups. It has a role as an EC 6.1.1.14 (methionine gamma-lyase) inhibitor and a human metabolite. It is an organofluorine compound, a non-proteinogenic alpha-amino acid and a diamine.

The molecule is a member of the class of bianthracenes that is 1,9-dihydrobianthracene-4,5-dione substituted by geminal methyl groups at position 2 and hydroxy group at position 3, an isoprenyl group at position 6 and indol-3-ylmethyl groups at positions 1 and 8. Isolated from Chaetomium globosum, it exhibits cytotoxic activity against human cancer cell lines. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a member of bianthracenes, a member of phenols, an enone, an olefinic compound and a member of indole alkaloids.
The molecule is a C-nitro compound that is toluene in which one of the meta hydrogens has been replaced by a nitro group. It derives from a hydride of a toluene.

The molecule is zwitterionic form of gamma-aminobutyric acid having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Daphnia magna metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a tautomer of a gamma-aminobutyric acid.

The molecule is a mannooligosaccharide derivative consisting of an alpha-D-mannosyl residue beta-linked to a 3-aminopropyloxy group and which carries an alpha-D-mannosyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannosyl-(1->2)-[alpha-L-fucosyl-(1->3)]-beta-D-mannosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-glucosyl unit linked (1->3) and an alpha-D-mannosyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannosyl-(1->6)-beta-D-mannosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-glucosyl unit linked (1->6). It contains an alpha-D-Manp-(1->2)-alpha-D-Manp-(1->2)-[alpha-L-Fucp-(1->3)]-beta-D-Manp-(1->4)-beta-D-GlcpNAc-(1->3)-alpha-D-Manp-(1

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (15Z,18Z,21Z,24Z)-triacontatetraenoic acid. It is a member of the n-3 PUFA and is the product of alpha-linolenic acid metabolism. It has a role as a mouse metabolite. It is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA and an ultra-long-chain fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (15Z,18Z,21Z,24Z)-triacontatetraenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (15Z,18Z,21Z,24Z)-triacontatetraenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid anion that results from the removal of a proton from the carboxy group of 3-(indol-3-yl)lanthranilic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from a lanthaninate. It is a conjugate base of a 3-(indol-3-yl)lanthranilic acid.

The molecule is a 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoserine in which the acyl group is specified as oleoyl. It derives from an oleic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 1-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-L-serine(1-).
The molecule is an amino disaccharide consisting of two N-acetyl-alpha-D-galactosaminyl residues linked (1->3). It has a role as an epitope and an antigen.

The molecule is a leukotriene that is (7E,9E,11Z,14Z)-icosa-7,9,11,14-tetraenoic acid substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 5 and 6 as well as an L-cysteinylglycinyl group at position 8. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from an icosa-7,9,11,14-tetraenoic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of aminonaphthalenes that is 1-aminonaphthalene substituted by methyl groups at positions 2 and 6 and nitro groups at positions 3 and 4. It has a role as an epitope, a carcinogenic agent and a mutagen. It is a C-nitro compound and a member of amino-1-naphthols.

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 2,3-bis-O-phytanyl-sn-glycerol 1-phosphate; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a (2R,3S)-2,3-dihydroxybacillosyl-sn-glycerol(1-).

The molecule is an organic cation that is 1,3-dioxo-2H-benzo[de]isoquinoline substituted at positions 5 and 6 by hydroxy and carboxymethyl groups respectively and at position 4 by a dimethylamino group. The chloride salt is the histological dye 'acid red 7'.
The molecule is a beta-D-galactosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphinganine in which the acyl group specified is docosanoyl. It has a role as an epitope and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a docosanoic acid.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid anion that is the conjugate base of methionine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a propionate. It is a conjugate base of a methionine.

The molecule is an androstanoid that is testosterone substituted by a beta-hydroxy group at position 17. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite, a marine xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid, a fluorinated steroid, an androstanoid and a secondary alcohol. It derives from a testosterone.

The molecule is a single-stranded DNA polynucleotide consisting of thymidine residues connected by 3'->5' phosphodiester linkages. It contains a dTMP 3'-end residue, a dTMP 5'-end residue and a dTMP 3'-end residue.

The molecule is an alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of alanine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group. It has a role as a fundamental metabolite. It derives from an octanoate. It is a conjugate base of an alanine and an alanine zwitterion.

The molecule is a hydrate that is the monohydrate form of dabigatran etexilate. Used for prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with atrial fibrillation. It has a role as an anticoagulant, an EC 3.4.21.6 (coagulation factor Xa) inhibitor and a platelet aggregation inhibitor. It contains a dabigatran etexilate.

The molecule is a member of the class of phenylureas that is urea in which one of the nitrogens has been substituted by an o-iodophenyl group and the other has been substituted by a cyclohexyl group. It has a role as a xenobiotic, an environmental contaminant and a herbicide. It is a member of styrenes, a member of iodobenzenes and a member of phenylureas.

The molecule is a branched amino hexasaccharide comprising an alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->3)-beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl chain, to the galactosyl residue at the non-reducing end of which are linked beta(1->2) and alpha(1->6) respectively an alpha-L-fucose residue and an L-fucosyl residue. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is an organic disodium salt having 3-(3-carboxypropyl)-2-{3-tert-butyl-7,8-dimethyl-5-oxo-5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobenzo[g]indol-4-yl}-3-methyl-1-(3-sulfonatopropyl)indoline-5-sulfonate as the counterion. It has a role as a fluorochrome and a histological dye.

The molecule is a tricarboxylic acid that consists of (1S,4R)-cyclohexa-2,5-diene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 6 as well as an oxo group at position 8 which in turn is substituted by a 1-carboxyvinyl group. It has been isolated from the bacterial strain Streptomyces sp.TC-0379. It exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 and also antifungal activity towards Candida albicans ATCC 10231. It has a role as a metabolite, an antimicrobial agent and an antifungal agent. It is a cyclic ketone, a secondary alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, a dicarboxylic acid, an enol ether and an olefinic compound.

The molecule is a nucleoside analogue in which guanosine has been modified by substitution at positions 1 and 5 on the purine ring by amino and hydroxy groups, respectively. It derives from a guanosine.

The molecule is a glycosylgalactose consisting of beta-D-glucopyranosyl and D-galactofuranose residues joined in sequence by a (1->4) glycosidic bond. It derives from a beta-D-glucose and a D-galactofuranose.

The molecule is an alkylglucosinolic acid that consists of 1-thio-beta-D-glucose attached to a 3-methyl-N-(sulfooxy)butanimidoyl group at the anomeric sulfur. It derives from a gluconapin and a 4-methylpentanethioic S-acid.

The molecule is an organic heteroheptacyclic compound isolated from the marine sponge Petrosia. It has a role as a metabolite and an animal metabolite. It is a cyclic ether, an organic heteropentacyclic compound, an enone, a tertiary alcohol and a secondary alcohol.
The molecule is an inorganic sodium salt having selenite as the counterion. It has a role as a reducing agent, a poison and a food antioxidant. It contains a selenite.
The molecule is a N-octadecenoylsphingosine-1-phosphocholine in which the acyl group specified is (9Z)-octadecenoyl. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and a rat metabolite.

The molecule is a phosphatidylcholine 34:0 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are palmitoyl and myristoyl respectively. It derives from a hexadecanoic acid and an octadecanoic acid.
The molecule is a xanthene dye anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy and 5-hydroxy groups of bromosulfophthalein. It is a conjugate base of a bromosulfophthalein free acid.
The molecule is an organic sodium salt having (S)-haloxyfop-P(1-) as the counterion. It has a role as a proherbicide and an agrochemical. It contains a haloxyfop-P(1-).

The molecule is a thromboxane A that consists of prostaglandin H2 bearing an additional hydroxy substituent at position 18. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a prostaglandin H2.

The molecule is a member of the class of 1,3-oxazoles that is 4,5-dihydro-1,2-oxazole-3-carboxamide substituted by a phenyl group at position 5. It has a role as an EC 1.14.99.1 (prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase) inhibitor and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug.

The molecule is an alpha-D-glucoside that is the 2''-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl derivative of validoxylamine A. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and an antimicrobial agent. It derives from a validoxylamine A.

The molecule is a hydrate that is the monohydrate form of iron(3+) citrate. It has a role as an antidote to cyanide poisoning, a food acidity regulator and a reducing agent. It contains an iron(3+) citrate (anhydrous).

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 3-oxodecanoic acid with the amino group of oxirane-2,3-dione. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite and a marine metabolite. It derives from a dodecanoic acid and an oxirane-2,3-dione.

The molecule is a member of the class of bianthracenes that is 1,4-dihydro-2H-3,6'-bichromene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 5 and 7, an oxo group at position 2' and a ({[(E)-deca-2,4,6,8-tetraenoyl]amino}methyl)(4-hydroxyphenyl)methylidene moiety at position 1'. Isolated from Chaetomium globosum it exhibits cytotoxic activity against human tumour cell lines. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a member of phenols, a secondary carboxamide, an enone, a member of bianthracenes and a cyclic ketone.
The molecule is the dihydrochloride salt of (R,S)-nebivolol. It has a role as an antihypertensive agent and a beta-adrenergic antagonist. It contains a (R,S)-nebivolol.
The molecule is an L-cysteine thioether that is the S-(2E,6E)-farnesyl derivative of L-cysteine. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a phytotoxin.

The molecule is a phosphatidylethanolamine 38:4 zwitterion in which the acyl substituents at positions 1 and 2 are specified as octadecanoyl and arachidonoyl respectively. It derives from an arachidonic acid and an octadecanoic acid. It is a tautomer of a 1-octadecanoyl-2-arachidonoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine.

The molecule is a quaternary ammonium salt that has 1-hydroxydiphenylacetic acid as the counterion. It has a role as an antiseptic drug, an EC 3.5.1.98 (histone deacetylase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent.

The molecule is a sesquiterpene that consists of 1,2,3a,4,5,6,7-octahydroazulene bearing five methyl substituents at positions 1, 1, 3a and 8 as well as an ethyl substituent at position 4. It has a role as a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a labdane diterpenoid in which the labdane skeleton has double bonds at positions 8(17) and 14 and carries hydroxy groups at positions 9alpha and 13. It derives from a hydride of an oleanane.

The molecule is a twelve-membered branched glucosamine oligosaccharide made up from four glucose, two Kdo and two galactose residues with one phosphate group attached. Corresponds to the core oligosaccharide of Neisseria meningitidis. It is an amino octasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.
The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the tertiary amino group of (S)-glaucine. It is a conjugate acid of a (S)-glaucine.

The molecule is a steroid sulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of 17alpha-hydroxyprogesterone sulfonate, obtained by deprotonation of the sulfonic acid group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an EC 2.7.1.33 (pantothenate kinase) inhibitor and a human metabolite. It derives from a 17alpha-hydroxyprogesterone.

The molecule is a monounsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of trans-2-isopentadecenoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It is an 11,12-saturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) and a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a trans-2-isopentadecenoyl-CoA.

The molecule is an optically active form of phenylalaninate having L-configuration. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a L-phenylalanine. It is an enantiomer of a D-phenylalaninate(1-).

The molecule is a bile acid anion that is the conjugate base of 3alpha,7beta-dihydroxy-5beta-cholan-24-oic acid. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a cholate. It is a conjugate base of a 3alpha,7beta-dihydroxy-5beta-cholanic acid.
The molecule is a heme having an iron(III) central cluster. It has a role as a cofactor and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite.

The molecule is a 13-membered oligopeptide comprising D-Phe, L-Pro, L-Trp, L-Leu, L-Ser(D), Nle, L-Gln, L-Tyr, L-His, L-Val and L-Glu residues coupled in sequence. It has a role as an antihypertensive agent and a metabolite.
The molecule is the stable isotope of beryllium with relative atomic mass 7.014632, 8.5 atom percent natural abundance and nuclear spin 9/2.

The molecule is an N-glycosylated dialkylglycerophosphoethanolamine in which the alkyl groups are hexadecyl, the glycerol core has sn stereochemistry and the phosphoethanolamine unit is at position 3 and substituted on nitrogen with a branched octasaccharide derivative. It derives from a 1,2-dihexadecyl-sn-glycerol.

The molecule is an anthracycline that is 13-deoxydaunorubicin substituted at position 4 by a beta-L-rhamnosyl residue. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is an aminoglycoside, a deoxy hexoside, an anthracycline antibiotic, a monosaccharide derivative, a member of p-quinones, a tertiary alcohol and a monocarboxylic acid. It derives from a daunorubicin.

The molecule is a phosphatidylcholine 40:6 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are arachidonoyl and linoleoyl respectively. It derives from an arachidonic acid and a linoleic acid.

The molecule is a phenothiazine derivative in which the phenothiazine tricycle has 2-(4-piperazin-1-ylbutyl)ethyl and trifluoromethyl substituents at positions 2 and 5 respectively. It has a role as an antiemetic, a dopaminergic antagonist, a serotonergic antagonist, a second generation antipsychotic, an EC 3.4.21.26 (prolyl oligopeptidase) inhibitor and an anticoronaviral agent. It is a N-alkylpiperazine, a member of phenothiazines, an organofluorine compound and a tertiary amino compound.
The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-3-(beta-D-galactosyl)-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as linoleoyl. It derives from an oleic acid.

The molecule is a phosphocholine obtained by formal condensation of the hydroxy group at position 1 of hexanedioic acid with the primary amino group of phosphoric acid. It has a role as an animal metabolite, a plant metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a hexanedioic acid.

The molecule is a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate that is adenosine 5'-monophosphate in which one of the hydroxy groups of the phosphate has been condensed with the thiol group of mercaptoacetic acid. It derives from an adenosine 5'-monophosphate and a mercaptoacetic acid.

The molecule is an amino cyclitol glycoside that consists of neamine substituted at position 2 by a 6-O-carbamoyl-alpha-D-glucosaminyl residue. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antibacterial drug and a bacterial metabolite. It derives from a neamine.

The molecule is a resin glycoside that is the tetrasaccharide derivative of jalapinolic acid. Isolated from Ipomoea pes-caprae, it has been found to exhibit potential inhibitory effect against multidrug resistance in the human breast cancer cell line. It has a role as a metabolite. It is a cinnamate ester, a macrocyclic lactone, a resin glycoside and a tetrasaccharide derivative. It derives from an octadecanoic acid, a trans-cinnamic acid and a jalapinolic acid.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy groups of (7R)-1a,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undecin-7-yl acetate 6-carboxylate; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an azabicycloalkane and a pimelate(2-).
The molecule is a tetrapeptide composed of L-alanine, L-valine and two methyl L-aspartic acid units joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the two amino groups of 3,4-dichloroaniline. It has a role as a xenobiotic metabolite and a bacterial xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a phenolate anion.

The molecule is a member of the class of indoles that is 2-(1H-indol-3-yl)-4,4-dimethylpentanoic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 5 has been replaced by an alpha-D-glucopyranosyl group. It is found in Cinnamomum cassia and exhibits inhibitory activity against chymotrypsin. It has a role as a metabolite and an EC 3.4.21.1 (chymotrypsin) inhibitor. It is a tertiary alcohol, a ketone, an indole alkaloid and a monosaccharide derivative.
The molecule is an alkanesulfonic acid in which the alkyl group directly linked to the sulfo function is isopropyl. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite.
The molecule is a 7alpha-hydroxy steroid, a 26-oxo steroid and a 3-oxo-5beta-steroid. It has a role as a bile acid metabolite.
The molecule is a alkane that is heptane substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 6, 8 and 10. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism. It has a role as a human metabolite.

The molecule is a 7-oxo steroid that is lithocholic acid in which the hydroxy hydrogen at position 3 has been replaced by an oxo group. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a bile acid, a monohydroxy-5beta-cholanic acid, a 12alpha-hydroxy steroid, a 7-oxo steroid, a C24-steroid and a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid. It derives from a lithocholic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 7-oxolithocholate.

The molecule is a limonoid that consists of 13,20-epoxylimonoarborinane bearing two additional hydroxy substituents at positions 7 and 25. It has been isolated from Azadirachta indica. It has a role as an antifeedant and a plant metabolite. It is an acetate ester, a cyclic terpene ketone, a member of furans, a limonoid, a tetracyclic triterpenoid, a tertiary alcohol and a secondary alcohol.
The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that is nonanoic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens at position 4 has been replaced by a trimethylsilyl group. It derives from a nonanoic acid.

The molecule is a linear amino tetrasaccharide comprising an alpha-N-acetylneuraminyl residue (2->3)-linked to a beta-D-galactosyl residue, which in turn is linked (1->4) to N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine. It has a role as an epitope and an antigen. It is an amino tetrasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is an oxonium betaine obtained by deprotonation of the 5 and 7 positions of cyanidin 3-O-(2-O-beta-D-glucosyl-beta-D-glucoside). It derives from a cyanidin cation. It is a conjugate base of a cyanidin 3-O-(6''-O-beta-D-glucosyl-2'',4',5''-trihydroxybenzoyl)-beta-D-glucoside.

The molecule is a C-nitro compound that is imidazole in which the hydrogen attached to nitrogen has been replaced by a nitro group. It has a role as an EC 1.3.5.1 [succinate dehydrogenase (quinone)] inhibitor, an antidote and a metabolite. It is a member of imidazoles and a C-nitro compound.

The molecule is an S-substituted coenzyme M(4) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 5'-phosphopantetheine. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a D-pantetheine 4'-phosphate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a 5'-phosphonatopantoate(1-).
The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid that consists of glutaric acid bearing an additional phenyl substituent at position 2. It derives from a glutaric acid.

The molecule is an organic heterotetracyclic compound that is 3,4-dihydrotetraphene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1, 5, 6 and 8 as well as a oxo group at position 7. It has been isolated from Aspergillus taichungensis. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite. It is an organic heterotetracyclic compound, a cyclic ketone, a polyketide, a polyphenol and a bridged compound.

The molecule is an amino acid zwitterion resulting from a transfer of a proton from the carboxy group to the secondary amino group of (3R,5S)-3,4-dihydroxyproline; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from a trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline zwitterion. It is a tautomer of a (3R,5S)-3,4-dihydroxyproline.
The molecule is the stable isotope of zinc with relative atomic mass 65.908412, 73.2 atom percent natural abundance and nuclear spin +1/2.

The molecule is an androstanoid that consists of testosterone bearing a hydroxy substituent at the 1alpha-position. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Daphnia magna metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid, a 17beta-hydroxy steroid, an androstanoid and a secondary alpha-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid that is L-phenylalanine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the alpha-carbon is replaced by a hydrogen. It has a role as an EC 1.4.3.4 (monoamine oxidase) inhibitor, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of (9Z,12Z)-hexadecadienoyl-CoA. It is an (11Z)-Delta(11)-fatty acyl-CoA(4-) and a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a (9Z,12Z)-hexadecadienoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a member of morpholines and an aromatic ether. It has a role as an antiemetic, a dopaminergic antagonist, a serotonergic antagonist, a H1-receptor antagonist, an EC 3.4.21.26 (prolyl oligopeptidase) inhibitor and a first generation antipsychotic.

The molecule is a dTDP-4-acetamido-4,6-dideoxy-D-glucose in which the anomeric centre of the pyranose fragment has alpha-configuration. It derives from an alpha-L-idopyranuronic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a dTDP-4-acetamido-4,6-dideoxy-alpha-D-glucose(2-).

The molecule is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid that is 3-methylbutanoic acid which has been substituted at position 2 by hydroxy and oxo groups, respectively. It is an enol, a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of N-benzoylglycine, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human urinary metabolite and a human blood serum metabolite. It derives from an anthranilate. It is a conjugate base of a N-benzoylglycine.

The molecule is a dihydroxyflavanone that consists of (2S)-flavanone bearing two hydroxy substituents at positions 7 and 4'. It has a role as an antioxidant, an anti-inflammatory agent, an antineoplastic agent, a hepatoprotective agent, a plant metabolite, a food component and a human xenobiotic metabolite.

The molecule is an L-arginine derivative in which the omega-nitrogen atom carries a hydroxy group and one of the epsilon-nitrogen atoms carries a methyl group; major species at pH 7.3 It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid and a member of guanidines.
The molecule is a 1-(5-phospho-D-ribosyl)imidazolecarboxamide that has guanosine as the imidazopyrimidine moiety. It derives from an adenosine 5'-monophosphate and a guanosine 5'-monophosphate.

The molecule is a very long-chain omega-3 fatty acid that is tetratriacontapentaenoic acid having five double bonds located at positions 24, 27, 30, 33 and 36 (the 24Z,27Z,30Z,33Z,36Z-isomer). It is an omega-3 fatty acid and a tetratriacontahexaenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (24Z,27Z,30Z,33Z,36Z)-tetratriacontahexaenoate.

The molecule is an acyl-CoA(4-) oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of 3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy-5beta-cholest-24-en-26-oyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of a 3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy-5beta-cholest-24-en-26-oyl-CoA.
The molecule is an oligosaccharide derivative that is a tridecasaccharide derivative, the oligosaccharide portion of the Proteus penneri strain 14 lipopolysaccharide (LPS) core region.

The molecule is a cinnamate ester obtained by the formal condensation of hydroxy group at position 4' of (+)-quinic acid with trans-caffeic acid. Isolated from Piper sanguineispicum, it exhibits antileishmanial activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a metabolite. It is a member of phenols, a cyclic ketone, a cinnamate ester and a primary alcohol.

The molecule is a hydroxydocosahexaenoate that consists of (4Z,7Z,10Z,13Z,15E,19Z)-docosahexaenoic acid in which the hydroxy group is located at position 8. An intermediate of specialised proresolving mediators It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from an all-cis-docosa-4,7,10,13,16,19-hexaenoate.

The molecule is a tetracyclic triterpenoid that is 9beta,19-cyclolanostane substituted by an oxo group at position 3 and a beta-epoxy group across positions 8 and 24. It has been isolated from the stem bark of Fatsia polycarpa. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a cyclic terpene ketone, a diol, a member of epoxides and a tetracyclic triterpenoid.

The molecule is a member of the class of quinazolines that is 1,4-dihydroquinazoline which is substituted at positions 2 and 3 by pyridin-2-ylcarbonyl and [(2S)-piperidin-2-yl]methyl groups respectively. It has a role as an alpha-adrenergic antagonist, a serotonergic antagonist, a dopaminergic antagonist, a H1-receptor antagonist, a muscarinic antagonist, a second generation antipsychotic, an EC 3.4.21.26 (prolyl oligopeptidase) inhibitor and an anticoronaviral agent. It is a member of piperidines, a monocarboxylic acid amide, a member of quinazolines, a tertiary amino compound and a member of pyridines.
The molecule is a lipid A oxoanion obtained via deprotonation of the carboxy and phosphate OH groups of (KDO)2-(lauroyl)-lipid IVA; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a (Kdo)2-lipid IVA(6-).

The molecule is a triterpenoid obtained by epoxidation across the 2,3-double bond of squalene. It has a role as an EC 1.14.18.1 (aromatase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is an epoxide and a triterpenoid.
The molecule is a 1,3-diglyceride in which the acyl groups at positions 1 and 3 are specified as oleoyl. It derives from an oleic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of catechols that is catechol in which one of the hydrogens ortho- to both hydroxy groups has been replaced by a methyl group. It has a role as an antiinfective agent, a plant metabolite and a fungal xenobiotic metabolite.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid that consists of 1,2-dihydro-4H-benzo[g]isochromene bearing two carboxy substituents at positions C-3 and C-7. It has a role as an EC 6.4.1.2 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase) inhibitor, a plant metabolite, a human urinary metabolite and a marine xenobiotic metabolite. It is a benzoisochromanequinone, a member of isochromanes and a dicarboxylic acid.

The molecule is a diamino-1,3,5-triazine that is N',N'-diethyl-1,3,5-triazin-2-amine substituted by an amino group at position 4 and a chloro group at position 6. It has a role as a herbicide, an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic. It is a diamino-1,3,5-triazine and a member of monochlorobenzenes.

The molecule is a piperidinecarboxylate ester that is the methyl ester of (R)-2,5-dimethylpiperidine-4-carboxylic acid. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.8 (cholinesterase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is an organochlorine compound that is 2-chloroacetophenone in which the hydrogen at position 1 has been replaced by a N-ethoxypropanimidoyl group and in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen atom has been replaced by a methyl group. It is used as a herbicide for the control of broadleaf weeds in rice crops, but it can be harmful to humans who eat its food. It has a role as a herbicide, an agrochemical and an EC 1.3.3.4 (protoporphyrinogen oxidase) inhibitor. It is an organochlorine compound, an ethyl ester and an imidazolinylcarbamate strobilurin antifungal agent.

The molecule is an amino tetrasaccharide that is 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-beta-D-glucopyranose in which the hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 6 have been converted into the corresponding beta-D-galactopyranosyl and alpha-D-mannopyranosyl derivatives, respectively. It is a member of acetamides, an amino tetrasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is an amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of 5-methoxy-L-tryptophan; major species at pH 7.3 It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from a L-tryptophan zwitterion. It is a tautomer of a 5-methoxy-L-tryptophan.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzodioxoles that is 1,3-benzodioxole substituted by a heptadec-2-en-1-yl group at position 5. It has been isolated from Piper sanguineispicum and exhibits antileishmanial activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a member of benzodioxoles and an olefinic compound.
The molecule is the open-chain form of D-fructose. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a member of the class of quinolones that is 1-oxo-2,3-dihydroquinoline which is substituted at positions 4 and 6 by acetamido and N-acetyl-N-[(ethoxy-3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)methyl]sulfinyl groups respectively. It is an antibiotic fungicide used to control a wide range of diseases including downy mildew in cucumbers, potatoes, grapes, tomatoes and sugarbeet. It has a role as an EC 1.14.13.70 (sterol 14alpha-demethylase) inhibitor and an antifungal agrochemical. It is a sulfone, a secondary amino compound, a member of quinolines, a methyl ester, an aromatic ether, a carbamate ester, a tertiary carboxamide and an anilide fungicide.

The molecule is an inositol phosphomannosylinositol phosphophytoceramide(2-) having a tetracosanoyl group attached to the ceramide nitrogen, hydroxylation at C-4 of the long-chain base, and no additional hydroxylation of the very-long-chain fatty acid. Major species at pH 7.3 It is a conjugate base of an Ins-1-P-6-Man-beta1-2-Ins-1-P-Cer(t18:0/24:0).

The molecule is an organic heteropentacyclic compound that is 1,2,3,4-tetrahydrocyclopenta[b]indole substituted by a methoxy group at position 7, methyl groups at positions 1 and 6, an acetoxy group at position 8 and a N,N-diethylcarbamoyl group at position 3. It has been isolated from the bark of Cryptocarya chartacea. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an acetate ester, an aromatic ether, a carbamate ester, an organic heteropentacyclic compound and an indole alkaloid.
The molecule is a lathyrane diterpenoid isolated from the roots of Euphorbia micractina. It is a benzoate ester and a lathyrane diterpenoid.

The molecule is a scyllo-inositol phosphate that consists of 1D-myo-inositol having the hydroxy groups at positions 4 and 6 substituted by guanidino groups and a phospho group. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a mouse metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a myo-inositol.
The molecule is a pyrimidine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside having uracil as the nucleobase. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a hopanoid that consists of hopane substituted by an alpha-hydroxy group at position 3. It has been isolated from Hypocrella species and Aschersonia species. It has a role as a fungal metabolite, a bacterial metabolite and a marine metabolite.
The molecule is a hydrochloride obtained by combining (R)-tetrindole with one equivalent of hydrochloric acid. It contains a (R)-tetrindole(1+). It is an enantiomer of a (S)-tetrindole hydrochloride.

The molecule is a ferulic acid derivative obtained by the formal condensation of the carboxy group of trans-ferulic acid with methanol. It has a role as an antioxidant, a plant metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite.

The molecule is a phosphorodiamide that consists of 1,3,2-oxazaphosphinan-2-amine bearing two N-(2-chloroethyl) groups at positions 4 and 5 as well as a hydroxy substituent at position 2. A radiosensitising agent used in combination with radiation for the treatment of head and neck cancer. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a prodrug, a DNA synthesis inhibitor, a radiosensitizing agent and an EC 2.7.7.6 (RNA polymerase) inhibitor.

The molecule is a phosphatidylinositol 3-monophosphate(2-) that is the conjugate base of 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-1D-myo-inositol 3-phosphate; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a 1,2-ditetradecanoyl-sn-glycerol-3-phosphocholine(1-).

The molecule is an L-glutamic acid derivative having a phospho group attached to the gamma-nitrogen atom. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid, a L-glutamate derivative, an O(4)-phosphopantothenate and an aminoacyl phosphate. It derives from a pantoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 4'-phosphonato-L-pantoate(2-).

The molecule is a prostaglandin carboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 13,14-dihydroprostaglandin F2alpha, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an antiglaucoma drug and a vasodilator agent. It derives from a prostaglandin F2alpha(1-). It is a conjugate base of a 13,14-dihydroprostaglandin F2alpha.
The molecule is a sulfonic acid in which the sulfur atom has a methyl group attached to it. It derives from an acetic acid.

The molecule is a steroid sulfate that is 5alpha-pregnane-3beta,20alpha-diol in which the hydroxy hydrogen at position 17 has been replaced by a sulfo group. It derives from a 5alpha-pregnane-3beta,20alpha-diol.

The molecule is a member of the class of sulfamic acids that is sulfamic acid in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by a (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-yl group. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a kairomone.

The molecule is a member of the class of pyrroles that is 2-methylpyrrole which is substituted at positions 3, 4 and 5 by prop-1-en-1-yl, methylidene, and (E)-{[4-(p-sulfophenylazo)phenyl]diazenyl}ethyl groups, respectively. The monosodium salt is the biological stain 'azocarmine G'. It has a role as an acid-base indicator, a histological dye and a fluorochrome. It is a member of azobenzenes, a monocarboxylic acid, a member of pyrroles and an arenesulfonic acid.

The molecule is a sesquiterpenoid of the clerodane group isolated from the leaves and twigs of Casearia nigrescens. It exhibits cytotoxicity against human cancer cell lines, A-549 (nonsmall cell lung), SK-OV-3 (ovary), XF-498 (central nervous system), HCT116 (colon), MCF7 (breast) and PC-3 (prostate). It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a carbobicyclic compound, a monocarboxylic acid and a sesquiterpenoid.

The molecule is a member of the class of chromenes that is 2H-1-benzopyran substituted by an acetoxy group at position 4, methyl groups at positions 3 and 7, a p-fluorophenyl group at position 5 and geminal methyl groups at position 2 respectively. It has a role as a phytoalexin. It is a member of chromenes, an acetate ester and a member of monofluorobenzenes.

The molecule is a 1,4-benzodiazepinone compound having phenylmethyl and hexyl substituents at the 2- and 5-positions respectively. It has a role as an anxiolytic drug, a sedative and an anticonvulsant.

The molecule is a quassinoid isolated from Quassia indica and has been shown to exhibit antimalarial activity. It has a role as an antimalarial, an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a delta-lactone, a cyclic ether, an enone, an organic heteropentacyclic compound, a pentol, a secondary alcohol and a quassinoid.
The molecule is an N(2)-acetylornithine in which both amino nitrogens are acylated by acetyl groups. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite.

The molecule is a glycosylgalactose consisting of beta-D-glucopyranose and D-galactopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1->4) glycosidic bond. It derives from a beta-D-glucose and a D-galactopyranose.

The molecule is an amino trisaccharide consisting of alpha-L-fucopyranose, beta-D-galactopyranose and 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-D-glucopyranose residues joined in sequence by (1->3) glycosidic bonds. It is a member of acetamides, an amino sugar and an amino trisaccharide.

The molecule is a heterodetic cyclic peptide that is isolated from Streptomyces sp.MK95-23F1 and exhibits inhibitory activity against caspase 8, caspase 10 and caspase 1. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an apoptosis inducer, an EC 6.4.22.37 (caspase-8) inhibitor, an EC 6.4.22.36 (caspase-10) inhibitor and an EC 6.4.22.35 (caspase-1) inhibitor. It is an organochlorine compound, a polyphenol, a macrocycle, a heterodetic cyclic peptide and a member of phenols.

The molecule is a cyclic purine dinucleotide that consists of AMP and GMP units cyclised via 3',5'-linkages. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a cyclic purine dinucleotide and an organophosphate oxoanion.

The molecule is a medium-chain fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (3E)-nonenoic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a trans-non-2-enoyl-CoA and a cis-4-coumaric acid.

The molecule is a triterpenoid saponin that consists of urs-11-ene substituted by an epoxy group across positions 13 and 28, hydroxy groups at positions 16 and 21 and a beta-D-xylopyranosyl-(1->2)-beta-D-glucopyranosyl-(1->4)-[alpha-L-arabinopyranosyl-(1->5)]-beta-D-fucopyranosyloxy residue at position 3. Isolated from the whole plants of Gordonia chrysandra, it exhibits inhibitory activity against topoisomerase I. It has a role as a metabolite and an EC 5.99.1.3 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor. It is a bridged compound, a cyclic ether, a hexacyclic triterpenoid, a tetrasaccharide derivative, a triterpenoid saponin and a diol.

The molecule is a benzoate ester obtained by the formal condensation of 3-hydroxybenzoic acid with p-tert-butylcyclohexanecarboxylic acid. It has been isolated from Pisonia aculeata and exhibits antileishmanial activity. It has a role as an antileishmanial agent, a plant metabolite and a fungal metabolite.
The molecule is an O-acylcarnitine having 12-carboxytridecanoyl as the acyl substituent. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a dodecanedioic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of abietane diterpenes that is ferruginol in which the double bond at position 2-3 has undergone formal oxidation to give the corresponding epoxide. It has been isolated from the stem bark of Fraxinus sieboldiana and exhibits inhibitory activity against nitric oxide production. It has a role as a metabolite, an anti-inflammatory agent and an EC 1.14.13.39 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor. It is an oxaspiro compound, an olefinic compound, a tertiary alcohol, an abietane diterpenoid, a monocarboxylic acid and an epoxy monocarboxylic acid.

The molecule is a beta-D-glucoside that is luteolin attached to a beta-D-glucopyranosyl residue at position 7 via a glycosidic linkage. It has been isolated from the aerial parts of Vicia faba and Lotus edulis. It has a role as an antioxidant, a plant metabolite and a radical scavenger. It is a beta-D-glucoside, a monosaccharide derivative, a trihydroxyflavone and a member of flavonols. It derives from a luteolin.
The molecule is a 5-fluorotryptophan that has L configuration. It has a role as an EC 2.3.1.48 (tyrosine 3-monooxygenase) inhibitor, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a hydrate that is the dihydrate form of succinylcholine chloride. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, a muscle relaxant and a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist. It contains a succinylcholine chloride.

The molecule is a glycosyloxyflavone that consists of luteolin having a beta-D-glucosiduronic acid residue attached at the 7-position. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a metabolite. It is a glycosyloxyflavone, a dihydroxyflavone, a monosaccharide derivative and a glucosiduronic acid.

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the diphosphate OH groups of alpha-D-Man-(1->2)-alpha-D-Man-(1->3)-beta-D-Glc-(1->4)-alpha-D-GlcNAc-diphospho-ditrans,octacis-undecaprenol. It is a conjugate base of an alpha-D-Man-(1->2)-alpha-D-Man-(1->3)-beta-D-Glc-(1->4)-alpha-D-GlcNAc-diphospho-ditrans,octacis-undecaprenol.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of (2E,6Z)-10,11-epoxy-7-methyl-2,6-tridecadienoic acid arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid function; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an all-cis-geranylgeranate. It is a conjugate base of a (2E,6Z)-10,11-epoxy-7-methyl-2,6-tridecadienoic acid.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the secondary amino function of 1-(4-phenylbutyl)-2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-3-benzazepine. It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation.

The molecule is trication of spermidine arising from protonation at all three N-atoms; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a conjugate acid of a spermidine.

The molecule is a member of the class of 2,3-dihydro-1,4-benzoquinones that is 5-(propanoyloxy)cyclohexa-2,4-dienone which is substituted at position 6 by an oxo group and in which one of the hydrogens attached to the other carbonyl group has been replaced by a methoxycarbonyl group. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, an acaricide, an agrochemical, an avicide, a xenobiotic, an environmental contaminant and a plant metabolite. It is a methyl ester, an enoate ester, a cyclic ketone, a secondary alcohol and a member of 2,3-dihydro-1,4-benzoquinones.

The molecule is a carbohydrate acid derivative anion arising from deprotonation of the carboxy groups of beta-D-GlcA2S-(1->3)-beta-D-GalNAc-(1->4)-D-GlcNAc; major species at pH 7.3 It derives from a beta-D-GlcpA-(1->3)-[beta-D-GalpNAc-(1->4)]-D-GlcpNAc(1-).

The molecule is a member of the class of 1-benzothiophenes that is 2,3-dihydro-1-benzothiophene which is substituted at positions 2 and 5 by cyano and (4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzylidene)amino groups respectively. It has been isolated from Aspergillus taichungensis. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite. It is a nitrile, a monomethoxybenzene, a member of phenols, a secondary amino compound and a member of 1-benzothiophenes.

The molecule is a member of the class of depsidones that is 11H-dibenzo[b,e][1,4]dioxepine substituted by methoxy groups at positions 3, 6 and 9, methyl group at position 8 and an oxo group at position 11. It has been isolated from Chaetomium globosum. It has a role as a Chaetomium metabolite. It is a member of depsidones and an organic heterotricyclic compound.

The molecule is a synthetic RNA fragment comprised of six guanosine, seven adenosine and eight cytidine residues connected by 3'->5' phosphodiester linkages in the sequence G-A-C-G-A-U-C-A-A-C-C-G-A-C-A-C-C-G-A.

The molecule is a L-cysteine derivative in which the sulfur atom carries an allyl group. It has a role as a metabolite and a human urinary metabolite. It is a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid, a L-cysteine derivative and a sulfone.

The molecule is a phenolate anion that is the conjugate base of nogalonic acid, obtained by deprotonation of one of the two hydroxy groups at position 5. Major microspecies at pH 7.3 It derives from an anthrone. It is a conjugate base of a nogalonic acid.

The molecule is a 19-membered polypeptide comprising the sequence Lys-Gly-Lys-Asp-Phe-Val-His-Leu-Glu-Asn-Ile-Val-Thr-Pro-Arg. Corresponds to the sequence of the myelin basic protein 83-99 (MBP83-99) immunodominant epitope with the lysyl residue at position 91 replaced by phenylalanyl [MBP83-99(F(91))] and with an L-lysyl residue attached to the glutamine(83) (E(83)) residue via an amide bond.
The molecule is the hydrochloride salt of cyclizine. It has a role as an antiemetic, a H1-receptor antagonist and a serotonergic agonist. It contains a cyclizine.

The molecule is an aromatic amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 4-(aminomethyl)cyclohexanecarboxylic acid with the amino group of pyridine. It has a role as a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist, a muscarinic antagonist and a muscle relaxant. It is an aromatic amide and a member of pyridines.
The molecule is a (2R)-2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion. It derives from a propionate. It is a conjugate base of a (S)-lactic acid. It is an enantiomer of a (R)-lactate.

The molecule is an organic heteropentacyclic compound that is 1,2-dihydroanthra[2,3-b]furo[4,5-c]furan-7,9(6H)-dione substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 8 and 10, methyl groups at positions 2, 2, 5a and 9 and a methylenedioxy group across positions 4 and 5. Isolated from the culture broth of Chaetomium globosum, it exhibits cytotoxic activity against human cancer cell lines. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a member of phenols, a cyclic ketone, an enol ether, an organic heteropentacyclic compound and a beta-diketone.

The molecule is an N-acyl-L-alpha-amino acid anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy groups and protonation of the amino group of S-glutathionylglycinamide; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a cofactor. It derives from a glutathionate(1-).

The molecule is a 3-[(1S,5R)-2-oxoazetidin-1-yl]-4-chloro-2-methylbenzene-1-sulfonic acid that has R configuration. The active enantiomer of the racemic herbicide mecoprop. It has a role as an agrochemical and an EC 6.4.1.2 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase) inhibitor. It is an enantiomer of a (S)-mecoprop.

The molecule is a C7 cyanine dye having 1-ethyl-3,3-dimethylindoleinine units at each end. It has a role as a fluorochrome and an epitope. It is an organic iodide salt and a Cy5 dye. It contains a C7-indocyanine cation.

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of trans-2-undecenoic acid. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a medium-chain fatty acyl-CoA and a monounsaturated fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a trans-2-undecenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a trans-2-undecenoyl-CoA(4-).
The molecule is an acyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of 3-methylthioacryloyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a coenzyme A(4-).

The molecule is a mannosylinositol phosphorylceramide compound having a hexacosanoyl group amide-linked to a C18 phytosphingosine base, with no hydroxylation of the C26 very long chain fatty acid. It derives from an Ins-1-P-Cer(t18:0/26:0).
The molecule is a glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex. It has a role as an antigen.

The molecule is a sialopentaosylceramide consisting of the pentasaccharide beta-GalNAc-(1->4)-[alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->8)-alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->3)]-beta-Gal-(1->4)-beta-Glc attached to the primary hydroxy function of ceramide(d18:1/20:0). It has a role as a mouse metabolite and an epitope. It derives from a docosanoic acid.

The molecule is a glycosyloxyflavone that consists of kaempferol attached to a alpha-L-rhamnopyranosyl(1->2)-beta-D-glucopyranoside moiety at position 3 via a glycosidic linkage. Isolated from the aerial parts of Vicia faba and Lotus edulis, it exhibits inhibitory activity against topoisomerase I. It has a role as an EC 5.99.1.2 (DNA topoisomerase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a disaccharide derivative, a trihydroxyflavone and a glycosyloxyflavone. It derives from a kaempferol.

The molecule is an L-glutamine derivative that is the amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-2-aminoadipic acid with the amino group of 2-naphthylamine. It has a role as a chromogenic compound. It is a N-(2-naphthyl)carboxamide, an amino acid amide and a L-glutamine derivative.

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol 3-phosphate(3-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 1,2-dicapryl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate. It is a conjugate base of a 1,2-dicapryl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate.
The molecule is an organic thiophosphate, a phosphonic ester and an organochlorine compound. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, an acaricide and an agrochemical.

The molecule is an ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of the tertiary amino group of (-)-vincadifformine. The major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a conjugate acid of a (-)-vincadifformine.

The molecule is a trisaccharide consisting of two beta-D-galactopyranose residues and an L-arabinofuranose residue joined in sequence by (1->4) glycosidic bonds. It derives from a beta-D-Galp-(1->4)-beta-D-Galp and a L-arabinofuranose.

The molecule is a hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy-11-oxo-5beta-cholan-24-oic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a cholate. It is a conjugate base of a (3alpha,7alpha)-11-oxocholestanol-3,7-diol.

The molecule is an organic cation that is the conjugate acid of (1S,2R)-8,9-dihydroergoline; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation.

The molecule is a bianthracene that is 9,10-anthraquinone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 6, methyl group at position 2, chloro group at position 8 and oxo groups at positions 1 and 7. It has been isolated from Chaetomium globosum. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a Chaetomium metabolite. It is a member of phenols, a cyclic ketone, a polyphenol, a chlorinated compound and a member of bianthracenes.
The molecule is a gluconic acid derivative having an alpha-D-mannosyl residue attached at the 2-position and a phospho group at the 3-position. It derives from a D-mannitol.

The molecule is an N-carbamoyl-L-alpha-amino acid anion that is the conjugate base of N-carbamoyl-L-methionine, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a L-methioninate. It is a conjugate base of a N-carbamoyl-L-methionine.

The molecule is a member of the class of naphthoquinones that is 1-hydroxy-3,5-dimethyl-2-naphthoquinone bearing an additional (4E),7,10-trimethyldodeca-4,8-dien-1-yl substituent at position 4. It has been isolated from Chaetomium globosum and Aspergillus niger. It has a role as a metabolite and an Aspergillus metabolite.

The molecule is an organic phosphonate that consists of phenylphosphonic acid bearing a 4-nitrophenyl substituent at position P. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, an acaricide and an agrochemical.

The molecule is a dTDP-4-acetamido-2,3,4,6-tetradeoxy-alpha-D-glucose in which the anomeric centre of the pyranose fragment has alpha-configuration. It derives from an alpha-D-galactosamine. It is a conjugate acid of a dTDP-4-acetamido-2,3,4,6-tetradeoxy-alpha-D-glucose(1-).

The molecule is a linear amino tetrasaccharide comprising an alpha-N-acetylneuraminyl residue (2->3)-linked to the middle galactose of a trisaccharide chain consisting of N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine linked (1->4) to beta-D-galactose, which in turn is linked (1->6) to N-acetyl-alpha-D-galactosamine. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a heteropentacyclic compound that consists of 3beta,16alpha-epoxyazadiradione substituted by a beta-D-glucopyranosyl moiety at position 4 via a glycosidic linkage. It has been isolated from the roots and stems of Scorzonera judaica. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is an epoxide, a benzoate ester, a secondary alcohol, a bridged compound, a lactol and a heteropentacyclic compound. It derives from a 3beta,16alpha-epoxyazadiradione.

The molecule is a labdane diterpenoid in which the labdane skeleton has double bonds at positions 8(17) and 14, carries an alpha-hydroxy group at position 9 and contains an unsaturation at position 13. It derives from a hydride of a labdane.

The molecule is a 3-oxoacyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of 9alpha-hydroxy-3-oxochola-4,6-dien-24-oic acid. It derives from a (5beta)-cholestan-3beta-ol and an octanoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a 17-oxo steroid that consists of androstane bearing two oxo substituents at positions 3 and 17. It has a role as an androgen, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hydride of an androstane.

The molecule is a phosphosphingolipid that is sphingosine with the hydroxy group replaced by an amino group and the phosphate group replaced by a trimethylazaniumyl group. It has a role as a mouse metabolite, a rat metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a sphingosine.
The molecule is a cyclohexanecarboxylic acid carrying an oxo substituent at position 2. It has a role as a human metabolite and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a naphthochromene that is 3,4-dihydronaphtho[2,1-b]chromene which is substituted by oxo groups at positions 5 and 9, hydroxy groups at positions 3, 6, and 8, and by a methyl group at position 7. It has been isolated from Penicillium purpurogenum. It has a role as an EC 1.14.18.1 (tyrosinase) inhibitor and a Penicillium metabolite. It is a member of phenols, a cyclic ketone, a naphthochromene and a member of p-quinones.

The molecule is an ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of the amino group of 4-cyanobutanal. The major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a butan-4-aminium(1+).

The molecule is an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine compound having a (2-fluorophenyl)methylidene group at the 3-position, chloro and hydroxy substituents at positions 7 and 8 respectively and a (2-hydroxyethoxy)methyl substituent at position 5. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an EC 2.4.2.30 (mitogen-activated protein kinase) inhibitor and an apoptosis inducer.

The molecule is an apo carotenoid sesquiterpenoid that is 4,8-dihydronaphthalene substituted by a methyl group at position 1 and oxo groups at positions 2 and 7 respectively. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an enal, an apo carotenoid sesquiterpenoid and an enone.

The molecule is a proanthocyanidin consisting of two molecules of (-)-epicatechin joined by a bond between positions 4 and 8' in beta-configuration. It has a role as an antioxidant, an anti-inflammatory agent, an antineoplastic agent, a hepatoprotective agent, a hypoglycemic agent, a metabolite and an EC 3.2.1.95 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor. It is a hydroxyflavan, a proanthocyanidin, a biflavonoid and a polyphenol. It derives from a (-)-epicatechin.

The molecule is a member of the class of pyrazoles that is 1H-pyrazole which is substituted at positions 2, 3 and 5 by trifluoromethyl, carboxy, and [4'-({4-methyl-5-[p-(trifluoromethyl)phenoxy]phenyl}oxy)benzyl]oxy groups, respectively. It is an inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase activity. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It is a member of pyrazoles, a monocarboxylic acid, an aromatic ether, an organofluorine compound and an aromatic ketone.

The molecule is a C19-gibberellin, initially identified in Gibberella fujikuroi. It differs from gibberellin A1 in the absence of OH groups at C-2 and -7 as well as the presence of an alpha-OH group at C-3 (all gibbane numbering).

The molecule is a dicarboximide that consists of 2,3,4,5-tetrahydrophthalimide bearing piperidin-1-ylmethyl and pyrrolidin-1-yl substituents at position 6. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor. It is a member of pyrrolidines, a N-arylpiperazine, a tertiary amino compound, a member of phthalimides and an aromatic ketone.

The molecule is a heparin hexasaccharide consisting of 4-deoxy-2-O-sulfo-L-threo-hex-4-enopyranuronosyl, 2-deoxy-6-O-sulfo-2-(sulfoamino)-D-glucopyranosyl, L-idopyranuronosyl, 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-6-O-sulfo-D-glucopyranosyl, beta-D-glucopyranuronosyl and 2-deoxy-3,6-di-O-sulfo-2-(sulfoamino)-alpha-D-glucopyranose units joined in sequence by alpha-(1->4) linkages. Sequence: DUAp2S(1-4)-a-D-GlcNp2Sa(1-4)-IdoAp2S(1-4)-beta-D-GlcpA-(1-4)-D-GlcAp2S(1-4)-α-D-GlcNp2S. It is a heparin hexasaccharide, an amino hexasaccharide and an oligosaccharide sulfate.

The molecule is a benzoate ester that results from the formal condensation of one of the carboxy groups of terephthalic acid with methanol. It has a role as an allergen and a hapten. It derives from a methyl 4-carboxybenzoate.

The molecule is a pyrimidone that is uracil which is substituted at positions 1, 5 and 6 by acetylenecyclopropyl)methyl group. It has a role as an antimetabolite, an antineoplastic agent, an EC 2.4.2.30 (thymidylate synthase) inhibitor, an alkylating agent, an immunosuppressive agent, an apoptosis inducer, an antibacterial drug, an antirheumatic drug, a metabolite, an antimicrobial agent, a DNA synthesis inhibitor, an antiviral drug, a radiosensitizing agent, an antimitotic, a protein kinase C agonist, a prodrug, a radical scavenger, an angiogenesis modulating agent, an immunomodulator, an antioxidant, a hepatoprotective agent, a neuroprotective agent, an anticancer agent, a cardioprotectant, an anti-inflammatory agent, a xenobiotic, an environmental contaminant, a genotoxin, a mouse metabolite and a rat metabolite. It derives from a uracil.

The molecule is a pentacarboxylic acid that consists of 1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane bearing six carboxy substituents located at positions 1, 4, 7 and 10. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hydride of a 1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane.
The molecule is a menaquinol whose structure comprises a 2-methylbenzohydroquinone nucleus and an all-trans-decaprenyl chain. It has a role as an electron donor.

The molecule is a carboxylic ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of (2-amino-1,3-diphenylpropyl)malonic acid with one of the hydroxy groups of glyoxylic acid. It has a role as an EC 6.4.1.2 [succinate dehydrogenase (quinone)] inhibitor and a herbicide. It is a dichlorobenzene, a monocarboxylic acid, an aromatic amine, a secondary amino compound and a carboxylic ester. It derives from a glyoxylic acid and a (2-amino-1,3-diphenylpropyl)malonic acid.

The molecule is dianion of 5-formyltetrahydrofolic acid arising from deprotonation of both carboxylic acid functions. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a tetrahydrofolate(2-).
The molecule is the stable isotope of tin with relative atomic mass 104.923758, 60.4 atom percent natural abundance and nuclear spin (1)/2.

The molecule is a retinoid glucosiduronic acid anion that is the conjugate base of all-trans-16-hydroxyretinoic acid 3-O-(beta-D-glucuronide) arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid function; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an all-trans-16-hydroxyretinoate. It is a conjugate base of an all-trans-16-hydroxyretinoic acid 3-O-(beta-D-glucuronide).

The molecule is a glucotriose consisting of two alpha-D-glucopyranosyl residues and an alpha-D-glucopyranosyl residue joined in sequence by (1->6) glycosidic bonds. It derives from an alpha,alpha-trehalose and an alpha-maltose.
The molecule is a pyrimidine ribonucleoside 5'-diphosphate having cytosine as the nucleobase. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a CDP.

The molecule is an apo carotenoid triterpenoid that consists of 4,4'-diapolycopene in which one of the terminal methyl groups has been oxidised to the corresponding aldehyde. It is a carotenone and an apo carotenoid triterpenoid.

The molecule is a carbamate ester that consists of phenylmethylcarbamic acid bearing an additional (4-sulfamoylphenyl)oxy substituent at position 1. It has a role as a xenobiotic, an environmental contaminant and a herbicide. It is a sulfone, a member of benzenes, a monocarboxylic acid amide and a carbamate ester.

The molecule is a linear seventeen-membered polypeptide comprising the sequence Tyr-Ile-Val-Ala-Thr-Phe-Leu-Asn-Pro-Val-Lys-Cys-Asp-Arg. Corresponds to the P01372 and P09658 entries in the NCBI protein database. It has a role as a metabolite, an apoptosis inducer and an antineoplastic agent.
The molecule is a 2-amino-2-deoxy-alpha-D-glucopyranose in which the anomeric centre has alpha configuration. It is a conjugate base of an alpha-D-kanosamine(1+).

The molecule is a tetrapeptide composed of L-leucine, two L-valine units and two D-aspartic acid units joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-leucine, a L-valine and a D-aspartic acid.

The molecule is a beta-D-glucoside in which the anomeric position is substituted by a 4-(p-hydroxybenzoyl)oxy group and in which the hydroxy groups at positions 2 and 6 are replaced respectively by p-hydroxybenzyl and p-hydroxycyclohex-1-en-1-yl groups. Isolated from the leaves of Alvaradoa haitiensis, it exhibits cytotoxicity against human oral epidermoid carcinoma. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a beta-D-glucoside, a member of phenols, a cinnamate ester and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is a hydroxycalciol that consists of vitamin D3 (calciol) carrying additional hydroxy groups at positions 20, 24 and 26 (with S-configuration at position 20). It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a human metabolite, a rat metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a triol, a hydroxycalciol, a member of D3 vitamins and a tetrol.

The molecule is a fumarate salt prepared from tenofovir alafenamide by reaction of one equivalent of fumaric acid for each 1-methylpropyl group attached to the phosphorus. A prodrug for tenofovir, it is used in combination therapy for the treatment of HIV-1 infection as well as antiretroviral resistance monitoring. It has a role as an antiviral drug and a prodrug. It contains a tenofovir alafenamide(2+).

The molecule is the D-enantiomer of 4-phosphoglycolic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a glycolic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a D-glycerate 3-phosphate(2-).

The molecule is an aromatic ether that is the 2,4-dichlorophenoxy ester of N-(tert-butoxycarbonyl)-3,3-dimethylbutanamide. It has a role as an EC 1.14.18.1 (tyrosinase) inhibitor and an agrochemical. It is a nitrile, a dichlorobenzene, an aromatic ether and a member of benzamides.

The molecule is a monoterpenoid that is (E)-2-methylhex-3-ene substituted by a hydroxy group at position 1. It has been isolated from the essential oils of Lippia citriodora and Citrus aurantium var. deliciosa. It has a role as an antileishmanial agent, a plant metabolite and a volatile oil component. It is a primary alcohol and a monoterpenoid.

The molecule is a N-hexadecenoylsphinganine-1-phosphocholine in which the acyl group specified is (13Z)-docosenoyl. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and a rat metabolite. It derives from an erucic acid.

The molecule is a cadinane sesquiterpenoid that consists of 1,2,3,4,4a,5,6,7-octahydronaphthalene carrying three methyl substituents at positions 1, 4 and 4a as well as an isopropyl substituent at position 8. It has a role as a plant metabolite.
The molecule is a methylguanine in which the methyl group is located at position N-9. It has a role as an antimetabolite, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a quinolone that consists of 4-oxo-1,4-dihydroquinoline bearing carboxy, fluoro and 2-(piperazin-1-yl)pyrimidin-4-yl substituents at positions 1, 6 and 7 respectively.
