A synthetic antibacterial agent, it has been used for the treatment of urinary tract infections including pyelonephritis. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antiinfective agent and a DNA synthesis inhibitor. It is a N-arylpiperazine, a quinolone antibiotic, a monocarboxylic acid, a member of monofluorobenzenes, a tertiary amino compound and a quinolone antibiotic.
The molecule is a tripeptide composed of one 3-methylglycyl and two glycyl residues in a linear sequence. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (17Z,20Z,23Z,26Z,29Z)-dotriacontapentaenoic acid. It is a very long-chain fatty acyl-CoA and an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (17Z,20Z,23Z,26Z,29Z)-dotriacontapentaenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (17Z,20Z,23Z,26Z,29Z)-dotriacontapentaenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is the pentaanion of 1D-myo-inositol 2,3,4,5,6-pentakisphosphate arising from global deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is an inositol phosphate oxoanion and a myo-inositol pentakisphosphate(10-). It is a conjugate base of a 1D-myo-inositol 2,3,4,5,6-pentakisphosphate.

The molecule is a glycophytoceramide having an alpha-D-galactopyranosyl residue at the O-1 position and an octanoyl group attached to the nitrogen. It derives from an alpha-D-galactose and an octanoic acid.

The molecule is a dTDP-4-dehydro-6-deoxy-D-glucose(2-) in which the anomeric centre of the pyranose fragment has alpha-configuration. It is a conjugate base of a dTDP-4-dehydro-6-deoxy-alpha-D-glucose.

The molecule is a member of the class of 1,3,4-oxadiazoles that is obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2',5-dimethyl[1,1'-biphenyl]-4-carboxylic acid with the amino group of 3-cyano-N-methylaniline. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It is a nitrile, a member of biphenyls, a monocarboxylic acid amide, a member of 1,3,4-oxadiazoles and a secondary carboxamide.

The molecule is a member of the class of dithiolanes that is propane-1,3-dithiol in which both hydrogens attached to the carbon bearing hydroxy group have been replaced by hydroxy groups. It has a role as an antioxidant and a human metabolite. It derives from a hydride of a propane-1,2-diol.

The molecule is an acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of 3,8-didehydroaconitic acid. It derives from a 3,8-didehydroseryl-CoA and an aconitic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzophenones that is benzophenone in which one of the phenyl groups is substituted at position 4 by an ethyl group, while the other is substituted at positions 2 and 3 by thiophen-2-yl and ethyl groups, respectively. It has a role as a fungicide and a plant metabolite. It is a member of benzophenones and a member of thiophenes.

The molecule is a compound of copper and sulfate in which the ratio of copper (+2 oxidation state) to sulfate ions is 1:1. It has a role as an astringent, a sensitiser and a food colouring. It contains a copper(II) sulfate.

The molecule is a pyrimidone that is thymine in which the hydrogen at position 6 is substituted by a 2-hydroxyethyl group. It has a role as an antimetabolite, an antineoplastic agent and a DNA synthesis inhibitor. It derives from a thymine.

The molecule is an epoxide that is oxirane substituted by a (2E)-3,7-dimethylocta-2,6-dien-1-yl group and a formyl group at positions 2 and 3 respectively. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an enal, an epoxide and a monoterpenoid.

The molecule is a sialopentaosylceramide consisting of a alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->3)-beta-D-Gal-(1->3)-beta-D-GalNAc-(1->4)-[alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->8)-alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->8)-alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->3)]-beta-D-Gal-(1->4)-beta-D-Glucosyl unit attached to the primary hydroxy function of ceramide(d18:1/16:0). It has a role as a mouse metabolite. It derives from an octadecanoic acid.
The molecule is a 3-[alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->6)]-beta-D-glucosyl-1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at O-1 and O-2 are dodecanoyl. It has a role as an antigen.

The molecule is a monosaccharide derivative that consists of 4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde attached to a beta-D-glucopyranosyloxy residue at position 4. Isolated from the aerial parts of Piper sanguineispicum, it exhibits antileishmanial activity. It has a role as an antileishmanial agent and a plant metabolite. It is a member of phenols, a methoxybenzene, a beta-D-glucoside and a monosaccharide derivative.

The molecule is a member of the class of oxabicycloalkanes that is (4aS,7aR)-1,3a,4,5,6,7,7a-octahydrocyclopenta[c]furan substituted at positions 2 and 4 by hydroxy groups, position 5 by an acetamido group and position 1 by an oxo group. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite. It is a secondary alcohol, a cyclic ketone, a primary amino compound, an enol, an epoxide, a bridged compound, a monocarboxylic acid amide and a member of oxabicycloalkanes.

The molecule is a cholestanoid that is 5alpha-cholestane substituted by a beta-hydroxy group at position 3. It has been isolated from the mycelia of Cordyceps sinensis. It has a role as a fungal metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a 3beta-sterol, an oxysterol and a cholestanoid.

The molecule is a straight-chain saturated fatty acid that is tetracosane in which one of the terminal methyl groups has been oxidised to the corresponding carboxylic acid. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a very long-chain fatty acid, a straight-chain saturated fatty acid and a fatty acid 42:0.

The molecule is a quaternary ammonium salt that consists of choline having the sulfo group at the 3-position. It has a role as an animal metabolite, a plant metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It contains a cholinium sulfate(1-).

The molecule is a glycophytoceramide having an alpha-D-galactopyranosyl residue at the O-1 position and an icosanoyl group attached to the nitrogen. It derives from an alpha-D-galactose and an icosanoic acid.

The molecule is an organic anion that is the conjugate base of 5-(dihydroxymethyl)-2,3-dioxopent-1-en-4-one, obtained by deprotonation of one of the enolic hydroxy groups. It is a conjugate base of a 5-(dihydroxymethyl)-2,3-dioxopent-1-en-4-one.

The molecule is a dimethoxybenzene that is 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene substituted by acetyloxy groups at positions 2 and 4. It has been isolated from the leaves of Piper sanguineispicum. It has a role as an antiplasmodial drug and a plant metabolite. It is a member of acetophenones, a dimethoxybenzene and a member of phenols.

The molecule is trianion of 5-(2-phosphonoethyl)-3-methyl-4-thiouracil arising from deprotonation of carboxylic acid and phosphate functions. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a urate(3-).

The molecule is an organic disulfide that consists of two ethylenediamine units linked by a disulfide bridge. It has a role as a metabolite and an allergen. It derives from an ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid.

The molecule is a butan-4-olide having a 2-(p-tolylsulfonyloxy)ethyl group at the 3-position and two methyl substituents at position 5. It has a role as an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a herbicide.

The molecule is a 19-membered polypeptide comprising the sequence Glu-Ala-Ile-Val-His-Trp-Lys-Leu-Asn-Pro-Val-Thr-Met-Arg-Gln-Ile-Ile. Corresponds to the sequence of the myelin basic protein 83-99 (MBP83-99) immunodominant epitope with an Isoleucyl residue at position 76 replaced by Alanyl and with an N-methylleucine [(MeLeu)] substitution in place of Leucine at position 75.

The molecule is a hydrochloride obtained by combining the free base of malachite green cation with one molar equivalent of hydrogen chloride. It has a role as an antiseptic drug, an antibacterial agent and a dye. It contains a malachite green cation.

The molecule is a maleate salt obtained by combining benazeprilat with two molar equivalents of maleic acid. Used for treatment of hypertension and heart failure. It has a role as an EC 3.4.15.1 (peptidyl-dipeptidase A) inhibitor, an antihypertensive agent and a vasodilator agent. It contains a benazeprilat(2+).

The molecule is a cyclitol phosphate that consists of valiolone carrying an O-phospho substituent at position 6. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a valiolone.

The molecule is a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate that is AMP substituted at position N-9 by fluorine. It has a role as an EC 3.1.27.46 (ribosyldihydronicotinamide dinucleotide synthase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and an antimetabolite. It is an adenosine 5'-phosphate, a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate and an organofluorine compound.

The molecule is a ginsenoside found in Panax species that is dammarane which is substituted by hydroxy groups at the 3beta, 12beta and 20 pro-S positions, in which the hydroxy group at position 20 has been converted to its beta-D-xylopyranosyl-(1->6)-beta-D-glucopyranoside derivative, and in which a double bond has been introduced at the 24-25 position. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an apoptosis inducer, a plant metabolite, an antioxidant, a cardioprotective agent, an anti-inflammatory drug, a hepatoprotective agent, a neuroprotective agent, a hypoglycemic agent, an EC 3.6.3.9 (Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase) inhibitor, an anticoronaviral agent and an EC 3.7.3.8 (ATP synthase) inhibitor. It is a 12beta-hydroxy steroid, a disaccharide derivative, a ginsenoside, a tetracyclic triterpenoid, a 3beta-hydroxy steroid, a 14alpha-hydroxy steroid and a 20-hydroxy steroid.

The molecule is a peptide anion that is the conjugate base of gamma-Glu-Met, obtained by removal of protons from the two carboxy groups as well as protonation of the amino group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from an isocitrate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a gamma-Glu-Met.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid monoester that results from the formal condensation of one of the carboxy groups of glutaric acid with the hydroxy group of 17beta-hydroxy-3,5-didehydrotestosterone. It has a role as an androgen antagonist and an antineoplastic agent. It is a dicarboxylic acid monoester, a steroid ester, a 20-oxo steroid, a primary alpha-hydroxy ketone and a hemisuccinate.

The molecule is a carboxylic ester resulting from the formal condensation of (1S)-cyclohexanecarboxylic acid with the hydroxy group of 2-[bis(2-ethylpropyl)amino]prop-2-yn-1-ol. It has a role as an opioid analgesic, a mu-opioid receptor agonist and an antitussive. It is a tertiary amino compound, a carboxylic ester, a secondary alcohol and an acetylenic compound.
The molecule is a member of the class of hydroquinones that is p-cresol in which one of the methyl hydrogens has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It derives from a 4,6-dimethylphenol and a p-cresol.
The molecule is an amino cyclitol glycoside that consists of 2-deoxystreptamine having a beta-D-ribosaminyl residue attached at position 4. It derives from a streptamine.
The molecule is a diterpene that consists of hopane having an exocyclic double bond at position 16. It derives from a hydride of a hopane.
The molecule is an amino acid amide that is alanine in which the carboxy OH group has been replaced by NH2. It derives from a glycine and an alanine.

The molecule is a long-chain fatty acid that is icosane in which the hydrogens at position 16 have been replaced by an oxo group. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a human blood serum metabolite. It derives from a hydride of an icosane.

The molecule is an organic sodium salt resulting from the replacement of the proton from the carboxy group of 4-phenylbutyric acid by a sodium ion. It has a role as a human metabolite and a plant metabolite. It contains a 4-phenylbutyrate.
The molecule is an organoarsenic compound that consists of arsane bearing three chloro substituents. It has a role as a carcinogenic agent and a mutagen.

The molecule is a (5Z,8Z,14Z)-9,10-dihydroxyicosatrienoate obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group of (5Z,8Z,10R,12S,14Z)-9,10-dihydroxyicosa-5,8,12,14-tetraenoic acid; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of a (5Z,8Z,10R,12S,14Z)-9,10-dihydroxyicosatrienoic acid. It is an enantiomer of a (5Z,8Z,10S,12R,14Z)-9,10-dihydroxyicosatrienoate.

The molecule is an L-cysteine derivative that is the amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-cysteine with the amino group of 2-naphthylamine. It has a role as a chromogenic compound. It is a N-(2-naphthyl)carboxamide, an amino acid amide and a L-cysteine derivative.

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol 3-phosphate in which the acyl substituents at positions 1 and 2 are specified as oleoyl. It derives from an oleic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 1-oleoyl-2-(9Z)-octadecenoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate(2-).

The molecule is a polyprenol diphosphate compound having twelve prenyl units with undefined stereochemistry about the double bonds. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of 2-O-feruloylglucaric acid; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a glucarate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a 2-O-feruloylglucaric acid.

The molecule is a phosphatidylcholine 42:6 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are eicosanoyl and (4Z,7Z,10Z,13Z,16Z,19Z)-docosahexaenoyl respectively. It derives from an all-cis-docosa-4,7,10,13,16,19-hexaenoic acid and an icosanoic acid.
The molecule is a hydrate that is the monohydrate form of citric acid. It has a role as an antioxidant, a food acidity regulator and a buffer. It contains a citrate(1-).
The molecule is a 7alpha-hydroxy steroid, a cholestanoid and a 3beta-sterol. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a cephalosporin compound having (2-thienylacetyl)amino and methoxy side groups. It has a role as an antibacterial drug, an EC 3.5.2.6 (beta-lactamase) inhibitor and an antimicrobial agent.

The molecule is a hydrate that is the dihydrate form of fenoprofen sodium. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, it is used for the treatment of pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, dysmenorrhoea (painful periods), postoperative pain, and as an adjuvant to other treatments in patients with musculoskeletal disorders such as back pain, neck pain, shoulder pain, and knee pain. It has a role as a cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitor, a cyclooxygenase 1 inhibitor, a non-narcotic analgesic, an EC 1.14.99.1 (prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase) inhibitor, an antipyretic, an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a drug allergen. It contains a fenoprofen sodium (anhydrous).

The molecule is an amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of S-[(2E,6S)-farnesyl]-L-cysteine; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It is a tautomer of a S-[(2E,6S)-farnesyl]-L-cysteine.

The molecule is a glycopeptide that consists of the hexapeptide Ser-Ala-Asp-Asn-Ser-Tyr-Cl substituted at position 2 on each of the tyrosyl and seryl residues by (6R)-6-hydroxy-3,7-dimethyloctanoyl groups. It has a role as an antibacterial agent and a bacterial metabolite. It is a macrocycle, a heterodetic cyclic peptide, a polyketide, a polyphenol, an organochlorine compound and a glycopeptide.

The molecule is a bile acid taurine conjugate of ursodeoxycholic acid. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from an ursodeoxycholic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a tauroursodeoxycholate.

The molecule is an organic cation that is the conjugate acid of tropine, arising from protonation of the primary amino function. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation. It is a conjugate acid of a tropine.

The molecule is an amino disaccharide that consists of N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine having a 3,6-di-O-sulfo-beta-D-galactosyl residue attached at position 4. It has a role as an epitope and an antigen. It is an oligosaccharide sulfate and an amino disaccharide.

The molecule is an organic sodium salt that is the monosodium salt of ceftaroline fosamil. A prodrug for ceftaroline, it is used in combination therapy for the treatment of adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections caused or suspected to be due to susceptible strains of certain Gram-positive bacteria including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). It has a role as an antibacterial drug, an antimicrobial agent and a prodrug. It contains a ceftaroline fosamil(1-).

The molecule is an organic anion obtained by removal of the acidic proton from position 8 on the pteridine ring system of lumazine. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a cofactor. It derives from a hydride of a lumazine.

The molecule is zwitterionic form of 3-O-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)alanine arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group; major species at pH 7.3 It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a 3-O-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)lactic acid zwitterion and a D-tyrosine zwitterion.

The molecule is a 6-oxo monocarboxylic acid that is hex-2-enedioic acid substituted at positions 3 and 5 by hydroxy and amino groups respectively. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a mouse metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It is a 6-oxo monocarboxylic acid, a secondary alcohol and a primary amino compound. It derives from a (2E,4Z)-7-amino-8-hydroxyocta-2,4-dienoic acid.

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by global deprotonation of the triphosphate OH groups of guanosine 5'-(beta,gamma-imido)triphosphate. It is a conjugate base of a Gp[3]G(3-) and a Gp[3]G.

The molecule is a carboxylic ester obtained by the formal condensation of 2-chloro-4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid with tert-butyl alcohol. It has a role as an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a herbicide. It is a member of monochlorobenzenes, a carboxylic ester and an ether.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzodioxoles that is 1,3-dihydro-2H-benzofuran substituted by a formyl group at position 5. It has been isolated from Piper nigrum and exhibits antispasmodic activity. It has a role as an antispasmodic drug and a plant metabolite. It is a member of benzodioxoles and an aldehyde.

The molecule is a lignan with a dibenzocyclooctadiene skeleton isolated from Kadsura ananosma. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antifeedant. It is an acetate ester, an enoate ester, an organic heterotetracyclic compound, an oxacycle, a lignan and an aromatic ether.

The molecule is a biflavonoid that consists of two molecules of (S)-naringenin joined by a bond between positions C-5 and C-8' in one ring system, which is then linked to position O-3 of the other ring system. Isolated from Ginkgo biloba and Lotus edulis, it exhibits inhibitory activity against topoisomerase I and II. It has a role as an EC 5.99.1.2 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent, a plant metabolite and an antibacterial agent. It is a biflavonoid, a hydroxyflavanone, a methoxyflavanone, a secondary alpha-hydroxy ketone and a member of 4'-methoxyflavanones. It derives from a (S)-naringenin.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzamides obtained by formal condensation of one of the carboxy groups of 3-[(2,4-dimethylphenyl)diazenyl]-5-hydroxybenzoic acid with the phenolic hydroxy group of 1,3-dimethyl-5-oxo-1,5-dihydro-2H-pyrazol-4-yl]benzene. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a vascular endothelial growth factor receptor antagonist. It is a monocarboxylic acid, a pyrazolone, a member of azobenzenes, a biaryl and a member of benzoic acids.

The molecule is a tetrapeptide composed of L-tryptophan, two L-valine units and L-isoleucine joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-tryptophan, a L-valine and a L-isoleucine.

The molecule is a fluorinated steroid, an 11beta-hydroxy steroid, a 20-oxo steroid, a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid, a primary alpha-hydroxy ketone and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory drug.

The molecule is a member of the class of phenylacetaldehydes that is phenylacetaldehyde in which one of the hydrogens alpha- to the aldehyde carbonyl group has been replaced by an octyl group. It has a role as a human urinary metabolite and a rat metabolite.
The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups and protonation of the amino group of rifamycin SV. It is a conjugate base of a rifamycin SV.

The molecule is a member of the class of phenylhydroxylamines that is hydroxylamine in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by a 2-nitrophenyl group. It has a role as an EC 1.4.3.4 (monoamine oxidase) inhibitor and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It is a member of phenylhydroxylamines, a C-nitro compound and a secondary amino compound.

The molecule is a quinolone that is 1,4-dihydroquinoline which is substituted at positions 1, 3, and 6 by cyclopropylcarbonyl, carboxy, and 5-methoxy-2-oxo-1,2-dihydroquinolin-4-yl groups, respectively. It has a role as an antibacterial drug, an antiinfective agent, a DNA synthesis inhibitor, an EC 5.99.1.3 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor, an antimicrobial agent, a bacterial metabolite and an Escherichia coli metabolite. It is a quinolone antibiotic, a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, a N-acylpiperidine, a quinolinemonocarboxylic acid, a quinoline antibiotic, a quinolone, a member of cyclopropanes, a tertiary amino compound and an aromatic ether.

The molecule is a primary alcohol that is butane in which one of the methyl hydrogens at position 1 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hydride of a butane.

The molecule is an oligopeptide comprising glycyl, 3-(ethylamino)propyl, L-tryptophyl, L-seryl, D-tyrosyl, L-glutaminyl and L-phenylalanyl residues coupled in sequence with a sulfonyl group at the 3-position of the tyrosine residue. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is an aryl sulfate that is acetaminophen in which the phenolic hydrogen at position 4 has been replaced by a sulfo group. It has a role as a drug metabolite, a human urinary metabolite and a xenobiotic metabolite. It is an aryl sulfate, a member of phenols and a secondary carboxamide. It derives from an acetaminophen.

The molecule is a kaempferol O-glucuronide that consists of kaempferol attached to a beta-D-glucopyranuronic acid residue at position 3 via a glycosidic linkage. It has been isolated from the leaves and roots of Petrorhagia velutina. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a kaempferol O-glucuronide, a tetrahydroxyflavone and a monosaccharide derivative.

The molecule is a glycosylgalactose consisting of beta-D-glucopyranose and alpha-D-galactopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1->4) glycosidic bond. It derives from an alpha-D-galactose and a beta-D-glucose.

The molecule is an organic anion that is the conjugate base of 2,4-dihydroxy-7-oxo-3H-xanthen-3-one, obtained by deprotonation of one of the enolic hydroxy groups. It is a conjugate base of a 2,4-dihydroxy-7-oxo-3H-xanthen-3-one.

The molecule is a carbamate ester that is the methyl ester of 3-(pyridin-2-yl)-5-methoxypyridine-2-carboxylic acid. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, a molluscicide and an agrochemical. It is a member of pyridines, a monomethoxybenzene and a carbamate ester.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of (6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z,18Z)-tetracosapentaenoyl-CoA. It is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-), an (11Z)-Delta(11)-fatty acyl-CoA(4-) and a very long-chain acyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a (6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z,18Z)-tetracosapentaenoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a 2-(4-isopropyl-4-methyl-5-oxo-4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazol-2-yl)nicotinic acid that has S configuration. It is a conjugate acid of a (S)-imazapyr(1-). It is an enantiomer of a (R)-imazapyr.

The molecule is a 3beta-hydroxy steroid that consists of 5alpha-androstane bearing three hydroxy substituents at positions 17, 20 and 24. It has a role as an androgen, a human metabolite, a Daphnia magna metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a 3beta-hydroxy steroid, a 17alpha-hydroxy steroid, a 20-hydroxy steroid and a 24-hydroxy steroid.

The molecule is a peptide cation obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group and protonation of the amino groups of L-isoleucine, L-leucine, L-arginine, L-lysine, L-glutamine, L-phenylalanine, L-histidine, L-tyrosine, L-asparagine, L-leucine, L-valine, L-proline, L-methionine, L-lysine, L-arginine, L-lysine, L-phenylalanine, L-asparagine, L-leucine, L-valine, L-proline and L-isoleucine residues; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite. It is a conjugate acid of an Ile(5)-Pro(6)-Lys(7)-Phe(8)-Asn(9)-Leu(10)-Arg(11)-Ala(12)-amide.
The molecule is a dipeptide composed of L-aspartic acid and L-serine joined by a peptide linkage. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-aspartic acid and a L-serine.
The molecule is an amino disaccharide consisting of beta-D-galactose having a 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-beta-D-glucosyl residue attached at the 3-position. It has a role as an epitope and an antigen.

The molecule is a cationic sphingoid that is the conjugate acid of C20 phytosphingosine, obtained by protonation of the primary amino function; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate acid of a C20 phytosphingosine.

The molecule is a labdane diterpenoid that consists of 3,8-dimethyltrideca-2,6,10-trien-5-one bearing two hydroxy substituents at positions 7 and 9 as well as two methyl substituents at position 4. It has a role as an antifungal agent, a plant metabolite and an antibacterial agent.

The molecule is a 3-oxo-fatty acyl CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of 15-hydroxy-(5Z,8Z,11Z,13E)-icosatetraenoyl-CoA. It is a conjugate base of a 15-hydroxy-(5Z,8Z,11Z,13E)-icosatetraenoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of (13Z,16Z,19Z,22Z,25Z)-octacosapentaenoyl-CoA. It is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-), an ultra-long-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4-) and a 3-substituted propionyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a (13Z,16Z,19Z,22Z,25Z)-octacosapentaenoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a lignan that consists of 2,3-dimethylbutane substituted by a 4-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl group at position 1 and a 3,4-dimethoxyphenyl group at position 4. It has been isolated from the bark of Machilus robusta. It has a role as a plant metabolite.
The molecule is a tyrosinyl radical. It derives from a D-tyrosine. It is an enantiomer of a L-tyrosinyl radical.

The molecule is a primary aliphatic ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of one of the amino groups in ammonia. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a conjugate acid of an ethylamine.

The molecule is a thiazolidinemonocarboxylic acid that consists of beta-alanine bearing an N(alpha)-benzoyl group and having a 1,3-dimethylthiazolidine moiety attached to the alpha-nitrogen. It has a role as a hapten. It derives from a beta-alanine.

The molecule is a selenocysteine derivative that consists of glutathione bearing an additional selenium atom at position 1. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a L-glutamic acid.
The molecule is a semisynthetic, broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotic. It has a role as an antibacterial drug and an EC 3.5.2.6 (beta-lactamase) inhibitor. It derives from a penicillin G acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of quinolones that is 1-(tert-butyl)-2,3-dihydro-1H-indol-5-one substituted by a 4-hydroxy-6-oxo-2,3-dihydropyridin-1-yl group at position 2 and two hydroxy groups at positions 4 and 6 respectively. It is isolated from the culture broth of Streptomyces sp.TC-0378 and exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 and the acid fast bacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis MC 2 155. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antibacterial agent and a bacterial metabolite. It is a pyridone, a monohydroxyquinoline, a secondary alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, a cyclic ketone and a dihydropyridine.

The molecule is a lipid A oxoanion obtained via deprotonation of the carboxy and phosphate OH groups of galactosyl-(glucosyl)3-(heptosyl)3-4-phosphoheptosyl-(KDO)2-lipid A It is a conjugate base of a galactosyl-(glucosyl)3-(heptosyl)3-4-phosphoheptosyl-(KDO)2-lipid A.
The molecule is a tripeptide composed of L-glutamic acid, two L-cysteine units joined by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-glutamic acid and a L-cysteine.

The molecule is a diterpenoid of the class of daphnane-type terpenes. It has been isolated from the roots of Scorzonera judaica. It has a role as an antifeedant and a plant metabolite. It is a bridged compound, a cyclic ether, a lactol, a tertiary alcohol, a secondary alcohol and a diterpenoid.
The molecule is a monoterpene that consists of cyclohexa-1,3-diene bearing methyl and isopropyl substituents at positions 1 and 4 respectively. It has a role as a fragrance and a plant metabolite.
The molecule is an oxathiocane that is 1,3-oxathiane substituted by a methyl group at position 4. It has a role as a metabolite and a volatile oil component.
The molecule is a triglyceride formed by acylation of the three hydroxy groups of glycerol with palmitoleic acid. It derives from an oleic acid and a palmitoleic acid.

The molecule is a fatty acid ester obtained by the formal condensation of egonol with linoleic acid. It has been isolated from the fruits of Styrax agrestis and exhibits anti-inflammatory activity. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, a plant metabolite and a cyclooxygenase 1 inhibitor. It is a member of benzodioxoles, a fatty acid ester, an aromatic ether and a member of 1-benzofurans. It derives from a linoleic acid and an egonol.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid that is olean-12-ene substituted by an alpha-hydroxy group at position 3 and a carboxy group at position 28. It has been isolated from Juglans sinensis. It has a role as a plant metabolite, an anti-inflammatory agent and an antineoplastic agent. It is a hydroxy monocarboxylic acid and a pentacyclic triterpenoid. It derives from a hydride of an oleanane.

The molecule is a monohydroxybenzoic acid that is benzoic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 2 has been replaced by an azobenzen-1-yl group. It has a role as a bacterial xenobiotic metabolite and a fungal xenobiotic metabolite. It is a member of azobenzenes, a monohydroxybenzoic acid and a substituted aniline.

The molecule is an organic cation that is the conjugate acid of 5-O-demethylpikromycin, obtained by protonation of the tertiary amino group; major species at pH 7.3 It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation. It is a conjugate acid of a 5-O-demethylpikromycin.

The molecule is a 27-membered polypeptide comprising the sequence Ac-Asp-Arg-Glu-Asn-Pro-Val-Ala-Phe-Lys-Gln-Leu-Gly-Arg-Thr-Ile-Asn-Ile-NH2 with an acetyl group attached to the amino terminus. It has a role as a human metabolite and a rat metabolite.

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (10Z,13Z,16Z,19Z,22Z)-octacosapentaenoic acid. It is a very long-chain fatty acyl-CoA and an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (10Z,13Z,16Z,19Z,22Z)-octacosapentaenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (10Z,13Z,16Z,19Z,22Z)-octacosapentaenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is an amino trisaccharide consisting of beta-D-galactopyranose, 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-beta-D-glucopyranose and D-mannopyranose residues joined in sequence by (1->3) glycosidic bonds. It is a member of acetamides, an amino trisaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a polyene antibiotic that is TMC-1A in which the 2,4-dimethyloct-2-enoyl group has been replaced by an (E)-2,6-dimethyldeca-3,7-dienoyl group. It is produced by Streptomyces sp. A5908. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a cyclic ketone, a secondary alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, a polyketide, an enol, an enone, an olefinic compound, a polyene antibiotic, a dicarboxylic acid diamide and a secondary carboxamide.

The molecule is a piperidinecarboxylate ester that is methyl 4-piperideine-3-carboxylate substituted by a methoxycarbonyl group at position 1. It has been isolated from the plant species of the genus Piper and exhibits antispasmodic activity. It has a role as an antispasmodic drug, a muscarinic antagonist, a calcium channel blocker and a metabolite. It is a piperidinecarboxylate ester and a methyl ester.
The molecule is a sphingoid that is 4-dehydrohexadecasphingosine in which the terminal methyl group has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It derives from a 4-dehydrohexadecasphingosine.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of (21Z,24Z,27Z,30Z)-hexatriacontatetraenoyl-CoA. It is a conjugate base of a (21Z,24Z,27Z,30Z)-hexatriacontatetraenoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a sesquiterpenoid that is (+)-5-epi-aristolochene in which the hydrogen at position 2 has been replaced by an oxo group. It has a role as a plant metabolite, a volatile oil component and a bacterial xenobiotic metabolite. It is a member of peroxy compounds, an organic heterobicyclic compound and a sesquiterpenoid.
The molecule is a tripeptide composed of two L-glutamic acid units and an L-aspartic acid joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite.

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (23Z,26Z,29Z,32Z)-octatriacontatetraenoic acid. It is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA and an ultra-long-chain fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (23Z,26Z,29Z,32Z)-octatriacontatetraenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (23Z,26Z,29Z,32Z)-octatriacontatetraenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 5-formamido-1-(5-phospho-D-ribosyl)imidazole-4-carboxamide. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a human metabolite. It derives from a 5-formamidino-1-(5-phospho-beta-D-ribosyl)imidazole-4-carboxamide(2-).

The molecule is a member of the class of chloroethenes that is ethene in which both hydrogens are replaced by chlorines. It has a role as an inhalation anaesthetic, a refrigerant and a carcinogenic agent.

The molecule is a member of the class of tetracenomycins that is 8-demethyltetracenomycin C in which the hydroxy group at position 12 has been converted to its methyl ether and in which the carboxy group at position 9 has undergone formal condensation with the anomeric hydroxy group of D-mannose to give the corresponding glycoside. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite, an antimicrobial agent and an EC 5.99.1.3 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor. It is an alpha-D-glucoside, an enol ether, an enone, an aromatic ketone, a monosaccharide derivative, a polyketide, a tertiary alcohol, a tetracenomycin, a methyl ester and a secondary alcohol.

The molecule is a phenolate anion obtained by deprotonation of the 2- and 7-hydroxy groups of norsolorinic acid. It is the major microspecies at pH 7.3 (according to Marvin v 6.2.0.). It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a norsolorinate(1-).

The molecule is a macrolide that is isolated from the marine sponge Aplysinopsis digitata and exhibits cytotoxicity against P-388 murine leukemia cells. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an animal metabolite and a marine metabolite. It is a macrolide, a secondary alcohol, a cyclic ketone, a member of thiocarbamides and an epoxide.

The molecule is a nicotinamide dinucleotide that is NADP(+) in which the anomeric centre of the ribosyldihydronicotinamide moiety has alpha- rather than beta-configuration. It derives from an alpha-NADP and a nicotinic acid D-ribonucleotide.
The molecule is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid that is heptadecanoic acid substituted by an oxo group at position 2. It derives from a heptadecanoic acid.

The molecule is a triacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at positions 1, 2 and 3 are specified as lauroyl, palmitoyl and stearoyl respectively. It has a role as an EC 3.5.1.98 (histone deacetylase) inhibitor and a human blood serum metabolite. It derives from a dodecanoic acid, a hexadecanoic acid and an octadecanoic acid.

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol 3-phosphate(2-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 1-oleoyl-2-docosanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate. It is a conjugate base of a 1-oleoyl-2-docosanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate.
The molecule is a methoxybenzoic acid in which the methoxy group is located at position 2. It has a role as an antiinfective agent, an antibacterial drug and a drug allergen.

The molecule is a steroidal acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of 9alpha-hydroxy-3-oxo-23,24-bisnorchola-1,4-dien-22-oic acid. It derives from a 9alpha-hydroxy-3-oxo-23,24-bisnorchola-1,4-dien-22-oic acid.

The molecule is a 19-HEPE that consists of 5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z-icosatetraenoic acid in which the 19-hydroxy group has S-configuration. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a human xenobiotic metabolite.
The molecule is a member of the class of 1,2-benziodoxoles carrying an oxo substituent at position 3. It has a role as an EC 4.6.1.2 (guanylate cyclase) inhibitor and an antiglaucoma drug.

The molecule is a L-lysine derivative in which the epsilon nitrogen of lysine carries an N(6)-adenylyl group. It has a role as a Mycoplasma genitalium metabolite and a bacterial metabolite. It is a member of pyrimidines, a N-glycosyl compound, a L-lysine derivative and a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid.
The molecule is a nitrogen oxoacid of formula H2NSO. It has a role as an EC 3.5.1.4 (amidase) inhibitor, an EC 6.1.1.1 (cytochrome c oxidase) inhibitor and a reagent.

The molecule is a branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of the linear sequence beta-D-GalNAc-(1->4)-beta-D-Gal-(1->3)-beta-D-Glc having an N-acetyl-alpha-neuraminyl residue attached to the galactose via an alpha-(2->6) linkage and a beta-D-galactosyl residue attached at position 3 linked to the reducing end glucose. It has a role as an epitope.
The molecule is an omega-amino fatty acid that is nonanoic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 9 has been replaced by an amino group. It derives from a nonanoic acid.

The molecule is a medium-chain fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of dodecanoic (lauric) acid. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a straight-chain saturated fatty acid anion, a medium-chain fatty acid anion and a fatty acid anion 12:0. It is a conjugate base of a dodecanoic acid.

The molecule is a hydroxybenzo[c]phenanthrene that is benzo[c]phenanthrene in which the hydrogen at position 2 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It has a role as an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic metabolite.
The molecule is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid anion. It derives from an octanoate. It is a conjugate base of a 3-oxopropanoic acid and a 3-oxobutanoic acid.

The molecule is a tertiary amine that consists of pentadecane substituted by a methyl group at position 15 and a (2-aminoethyl) group at positions 30 and 31 respectively. It has a role as an antifungal agrochemical.

The molecule is a 3-oxo-fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of 3-oxotetracosanoic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a 3-oxotetracosanoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 3-oxotetracosanoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is a gallate ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of gallic acid with the (3S)-hydroxy group of (+)-catechin. It has a role as an antioxidant and a metabolite. It is a catechin, a gallate ester and a polyphenol. It derives from a (+)-catechin and a gallic acid.
The molecule is an alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of aspartic acid. It has a role as a fundamental metabolite. It is a conjugate base of an aspartate(1-) and an aspartate.

The molecule is a member of the class of pyrimidines that is pyrimidine which is substituted at positions 2,4 and 6 by (1-hydroxypropan-2-yl)nitrilo, pyridin-3-yl and trifluoromethyl groups respectively. It is an aromatic amine, a secondary amino compound, a tertiary alcohol, a member of (trifluoromethyl)benzenes, a member of pyridines and a member of pyrimidines.
The molecule is a quaternary ammonium ion that consists of 3-phenoxypyridine bearing three N-methyl substituents. It has a role as an epitope, a hapten and an allergen.
The molecule is a dTDP-sugar having 4,6-dideoxy-alpha-D-glucose as the sugar component. It derives from a dTDP-D-glucose and an alpha-D-glucose.

The molecule is an acyl-CoA(4-) oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of (2S,9R)-3-oxooctanoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a (R)-pantothenate(1-).

The molecule is a quaternary ammonium salt that has tetradecyltrimethylammonium as the cation. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.8 (cholinesterase) inhibitor, a potassium channel blocker and a surfactant. It is a bromide salt and a quaternary ammonium salt. It contains a tetradecyltrimethylammonium ion.

The molecule is a heteropentacyclic compound that consists of 1alpha,2beta,3beta,4beta,5alpha-hexahydroxyepimino[2',3':6,7]-oxireno[1'',2'':8,9]furan substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1 and 5 alpha respectively, a methyl group at position 2 beta and benzoyloxy groups at positions 3 and 7. Isolated from the leaves of Albizia chinensis, it exhibits inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase. It has a role as an EC 2.7.7.49 (RNA-directed DNA polymerase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a bridged compound, a cyclic ether, an epoxide, a lactol, a benzoate ester, a diol and a heteropentacyclic compound.

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 5-epi-valiolone 7-phosphate; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a fungal metabolite. It derives from a valienone.

The molecule is a carbamate ester that is the N-butyl ester of 2-iodopropionic acid. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, an acaricide and an agrochemical. It is an organoiodine compound and a carbamate ester.

The molecule is a trihydroxyanthraquinone that is 9,10-anthraquinone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1, 3 and 8 and a methyl group at position 6. It has been isolated from the roots of Rubia yunnanensis. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a cyclitol phosphate that is 3-amino-1D-myo-inositol carrying an additional phospho substituent at position 6. It has a role as a human metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a myo-inositol.

The molecule is a pyridinemonocarboxylate that results from the removal of a proton from the carboxylic acid group of nicotinic acid. It has a role as an algal metabolite, a human xenobiotic metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from a nicotinate. It is a conjugate base of a nicotinic acid.

The molecule is an apo carotenoid triterpenoid compound arising from oxidative degradation of the beta,beta-carotene skeleton at the 8'-position. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a marine xenobiotic metabolite. It is an enal and an apo carotenoid triterpenoid.

The molecule is a member of the class of oxazolines that is 1,3-oxazolidine substituted by an ethyl group at position 2. It has been isolated from Penicillium species and Aspergillus niger. It has a role as a metabolite and an Aspergillus metabolite.

The molecule is a 3-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (3R,8Z,11Z,14Z,17Z)-3-hydroxytetracosatetraenoic acid. It is a (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA, a 3-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA and an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA. It is a conjugate acid of a (3R,8Z,11Z,14Z,17Z)-3-hydroxytetracosatetraenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is an omega-amino acid anion that is the conjugate base of 6-aminohexanoic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group. It derives from a hexanoate. It is a conjugate base of a 6-aminohexanoic acid zwitterion and a 6-ammoniohexanoate(1-).

The molecule is a member of the class of 1,3-oxazoles that is 5-({4'-[2-chloroethyl]biphenyl-4-yl}methyl)-1,3-oxazole-4-carboxylic acid in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen has been replaced by an N-acetyl-O-benzyl-L-threonyl group. It is a potent inhibitor of peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma and exhibits anti-diabetic activity. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.35/PPA2 (sterol O-acyltransferase) inhibitor and a hypoglycemic agent. It is a member of 1,3-oxazoles, a monocarboxylic acid amide, a member of biphenyls, a member of monochlorobenzenes and a carboxylic ester.

The molecule is a C20-gibberellin, initially identified in Gibberella fujikuroi. It differs from gibberellin A1 in the absence of OH groups at C-3 and -7 and the presence of an alpha-OH group at C-9 (all gibbane numbering).

The molecule is a tricarboxylic acid trianion obtained by deprotonation of the three carboxy groups of (2R)-dihomocitric acid; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a homoisocitrate(3-). It is a conjugate base of a (2R)-dihomocitric acid.

The molecule is a branched tetrasaccharide consisting of alpha-L-rhamnose having an alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->3)-beta-D-galactosyl moiety attached at the 2-position and an alpha-L-fucose residue attached at the 4-position.

The molecule is a polyprenylhydroquinone in which the polyprenyl substituent is decaprenyl at C-2; methoxy and methyl groups are also present at positions 6 and 3 respectively. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite.

The molecule is a member of the class of dihydrochalcones that is (S)-dihydrochalcone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 4 and 2', methoxy group at position 6' and prenyl group at position 3 respectively. It has been isolated from the buds of Cleistocalyx operculatus. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an aromatic ether, a member of dihydrochalcones, a secondary alcohol and a polyphenol.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid saponin isolated from the aerial parts of Dianthus versicolor. It has been shown to exhibit cytotoxic activity against human cancer cell lines. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a carboxylic ester, a hydroxy monocarboxylic acid, a pentacyclic triterpenoid and a triterpenoid saponin. It derives from a 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid and a gypsogenic acid.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid of the class of cucurbitane glycosides isolated from Machilus yaoshansis. It has been shown to exhibit inhibitory activity against nitric oxide production. It has a role as an EC 1.14.13.39 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a tetrol, a cyclic terpene ketone, a pentacyclic triterpenoid and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is a pyrrolidinecarboxylic acid that is (1R,2S)-hexahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole-1-carboxylic acid substituted by an oxo group at position 5. It has been isolated from the culture broth of Streptomyces sp.TC-0347 and exhibits inhibitory activity against chymotrypsin. It has a role as a metabolite, an antimicrobial agent and an EC 3.4.21.1 (chymotrypsin) inhibitor. It is a member of pyrrolidines, a monocarboxylic acid and a cyclic ketone.

The molecule is a D-galactopyranose 6-phosphate in which the anomeric centre has beta-configuration. It derives from a beta-D-galactose. It is a conjugate acid of a beta-D-galactofuranose 6-phosphate(2-).

The molecule is a member of the class of quinazolines that is 4-(pyridin-2-yl)quinazoline in which one of the hydrogens at position 6 has been replaced by an N-{3-[2-methoxyethyl]carbamoyl}amino group. It is a potent and selective inhibitor of mitogen-activated protein kinase p38alpha (MAPK14, MAP2K7). It has a role as an EC 2.7.11.24 (mitogen-activated protein kinase) inhibitor. It is a member of quinazolines, a secondary carboxamide, a member of pyridines and an aromatic amine.

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and sulfonate OH groups of 5-amino-6-formyl-2-(4,6-disulfophenyl)-3-hydroxy-4-methylpyridine-5'-phosphate. It derives from a pyridinium ion.

The molecule is a member of the class of indoles that is 3-cyanoindole in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite and a marine xenobiotic metabolite. It is a nitrile, a member of phenols and a member of indoles.

The molecule is an inositol phosphomannosylinositol phosphophytoceramide(2-) having a tetracosanoyl group amide-linked to a C18 phytosphingosine base, with hydroxylation at C-2 of the very-long-chain fatty acid. Major species at pH 7.3 It is a conjugate base of an Ins-1-P-6-Man-beta1-2-Ins-1-P-Cer(t18:0/2-OH-24:0).

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid that consists of hexanoic acid bearing two amino substituents at positions 2 and 6. It has a role as a Daphnia magna metabolite, a human urinary metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hexanoic acid.

The molecule is a 2-acyl-1-alkyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine in which the alkyl and the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as hexadecyl and glutaryl respectively. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a tetrapeptide composed of L-asparagine, L-glutamine, L-proline and L-serine joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-asparagine, a L-glutamine, a L-proline and a L-serine.

The molecule is a fatty nitrile that is nonadec-9-enal in which the hydrogen at position 10 has been replaced by an amino group. It is found in the oil palm, Elaeis guineensis and in fried potato chips.

The molecule is an organic heteroheptacyclic compound isolated from the marine sponge Plakinastrella clathrata and has been shown to exhibit antineoplastic activity. It has a role as a metabolite, an animal metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is an epoxide, a member of indoles, an organic heteroheptacyclic compound, a tertiary alcohol and a secondary alcohol.

The molecule is an arenesulfonate that is benzenesulfonic acid substituted by a cyano group at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite and a dye. It is an arenesulfonate, a nitrile and a member of benzenes.

The molecule is a butenolide that consists of (3S)-but-2-en-4-olide bearing hydroxy and hydroxymethyl substituents at positions 3 and 5 respectively. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite, a marine metabolite and a bacterial xenobiotic metabolite. It is a butenolide, a primary alcohol and a secondary allylic alcohol.

The molecule is a phosphatidate(2-) obtained by deprotonation of both phosphate OH groups of dimyristoylphosphatidic acid; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a tetradecanoate. It is a conjugate base of a dimyristoylphosphatidic acid.

The molecule is a sesquiterpene glycoside that consists of 2alpha,3beta-dihydroxy-4,6-dideoxy-beta-D-glucopyranose attached to a 10-hydroxy-9-oxo-9,10-dihydroanthracen-7-yl group at position 1 via a glycosidic linkage. Isolated from the whole plant of Scutellaria barbata and other species of genus Scutellaria, it exhibits antineoplastic activity against human cancer cells. It has a role as an apoptosis inducer, an antileishmanial agent, an EC 5.99.1.2 (DNA topoisomerase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a benzoate ester, a bridged compound, a cyclic acetal, a dihydroagarofuran sesquiterpenoid, a lactol, a secondary alcohol, a beta-D-glucoside and a sesquiterpene glycoside.

The molecule is a member of the class of cinnamamides that is trans-cinnamamide in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen has been replaced by a 6-aminohexyl group while another hydrogen at position 4 on the benzene ring has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It has a role as an Arabidopsis thaliana metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a secondary carboxamide, a member of phenols and a member of cinnamamides. It derives from a trans-cinnamamide.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide that is 7H-purin-6-amine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the amino group has been replaced by an aminocarbonyl group. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a member of purines and a monocarboxylic acid amide.

The molecule is a dTDP-sugar having alpha-L-threo-hex-4-ulose as the sugar component. It derives from an alpha-L-threo-hex-4-ulopyranose. It is a conjugate acid of a dTDP-alpha-L-threo-hex-4-ulose(2-).

The molecule is a polysaccharide derivative comprised of an alpha-D-mannosyl residue glycosidically linked to a 5-aminopentyl group and which carries at O-2 an alpha-L-rhamnosyl-(1->3)-[alpha-L-rhamnosyl-(1->3)-beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)]-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl trisaccharide unit. It is a polysaccharide derivative, a tetrasaccharide derivative and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is an L-tyrosine derivative that is L-tyrosine in which the hydrogen at position 4 on the phenyl ring has been replaced by a methyl group. It is a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid and a L-tyrosine derivative.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the secondary amino function of (S)-orciprenaline. It is a conjugate acid of a (S)-orciprenaline. It is an enantiomer of a (R)-orciprenaline(1+).

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 3-(2-hydroxyethoxy)benzoic acid with the amino group of propylamine. It has a role as an antiglaucoma drug, an antihypertensive agent and an environmental contaminant. It is a monocarboxylic acid amide, a secondary alcohol and a member of benzophenones.

The molecule is a quaternary ammonium salt that is the bromide salt of triethylammonium 3,6-bis(dimethylamino)pyridine N-oxide. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It contains a triethylammonium 3,6-bis(dimethylamino)pyridinium-1-carboxylate.

The molecule is an N-acylglycine in which the acyl group is specified as (12E)-3,12-dibromododec-12-enoyl. It has a role as a marine xenobiotic metabolite and a marine xenobiotic metabolite. It is an organobromine compound, a monocarboxylic acid amide and a secondary carboxamide.

The molecule is a C20 hydroxy fatty acid having (5S)-, (6R)- and (18R)-hydroxy groups as well as (7E)- (9E)-, (11Z)- and (14Z)-double bonds. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a lipoxin, a long-chain fatty acid and a hydroxy polyunsaturated fatty acid.

The molecule is a cephalosporin compound having methoxy and [(2Z)-2-(2-amino-1,3-thiazol-4-yl)-2-(methoxyimino)acetyl]amino side groups located at positions 3 and 7 respectively. It has a role as an antibacterial drug.

The molecule is an aminoglycoside antibiotic that is 3,8-dimethylnonacosane which carries a 2-amino-4-O-methyl-alpha-L-rhamnosyl residue at position 9 via a glycosidic linkage. It has a role as a metabolite and an antibacterial agent. It is an amino sugar, an organic heterobicyclic compound, a primary alcohol, a secondary alcohol, a monosaccharide derivative and an aminoglycoside antibiotic.
The molecule is an organic potassium salt that is the dipotassium salt of L-tartaric acid. It has a role as a food acidity regulator and a buffer. It contains a L-tartrate(2-).
The molecule is a compound of beryllium (+2 oxidation state) and sulfate in which the ratio of beryllium (in +2 oxidation state) to sulfate ions is 1:1. It contains a beryllium sulfate.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid that is olean-12-ene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 28, an oxo group at position 21 and a carboxy group at position 24. It has been isolated from the leaves of Rosa laevigata. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a pentacyclic triterpenoid, a cyclic terpene ketone, a diol and a monocarboxylic acid. It derives from a hydride of an oleanane.

The molecule is an O-acylcarnitine having (3Z)-7-hydroxyhept-3-enoyl as the acyl substituent. It has a role as a metabolite. It is an ammonium betaine, a carboxylic ester and an O-(hydroxyalkyl)carnitine. It derives from a carnitine.
The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that is glycolic acid in which one of the hydroxy hydrogens has been replaced by a phenyl group. It derives from a glycolic acid.

The molecule is a tetrapeptide comprising L-alpha-glutamyl, N(6)-L-lysyl, L-valyl and D-alanyl residues coupled in sequence with the C-terminus being connected to methyl 3-carboxypropionate via an amide bond. It has a role as a peptide hormone.
The molecule is a wax ester obtained by the formal condensation of palmityl alcohol with oleic acid. It derives from an oleic acid and a hexadecan-1-ol.

The molecule is a glycopeptide that consists of the linear hexapeptide Lys-Gly-Lys-Gly-Lys-Gly-Glu-Asn-(prolylglycyl)-Phe-Val-Ala-Asp-Pro-Arg-Thr-Cys in which the amino terminus has been glycosylated at position 2 by an alpha-D-galactopyranosyl-(1->4)-[beta-D-xylopyranosyl-(1->3)]-N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminyl disaccharide unit. It is isolated from the culture broth of Streptomyces sp.TC-0365 and exhibits potent activity against the multi-drug resistant P388/ADR tumor cells. It has a role as a metabolite, an antimicrobial agent and an antineoplastic agent.

The molecule is a methanesulfonate salt prepared from (R,S)-tosufloxacin by reaction of one molecule of tosufloxacin for every two molecules of methane sulfonic acid. It contains a (R,S)-tosufloxacin(2+). It is an enantiomer of a (S,R)-tosufloxacin methanesulfonate.

The molecule is a glycosylglycerol derivative in which an alpha-D-glucuronic acid residue and an alpha-L-rhamnosyl group are linked respectively (1->3) and (2->6) to the glycerol core. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a hopanoid that consists of hopane substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 7, 22 and 23 respectively. It has been isolated from Hypocrella species. It has a role as a fungal metabolite.

The molecule is a triacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as oleoyl while that at position 3 is specifed as linoleoyl. It has a role as a human blood serum metabolite. It derives from an oleic acid and a linoleic acid.

The molecule is an aryl sulfate that is 4-acetoxyphenyl hydrogen substituted by a sulfooxy group. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite and a drug metabolite. It derives from a p-acetophenol.

The molecule is a furofuran that consists of tetrahydro-1H,3H-furo[3,4-c]furan substituted by 2-hydroxy-5-methoxyphenyl groups at positions 1 and 4 respectively. Isolated from the stems of Sinocalamus affinis, it exhibits inhibitory activity against lipoxygenase. It has a role as a metabolite and an EC 1.13.11.34 (arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase) inhibitor. It is a furofuran, a polyphenol and an aromatic ether.

The molecule is a docosanoid that consists of (8E,10Z,13Z,15E,19Z)-docosapentaenoic acid carrying two hydroxy substituents at positions 7 and 16. An intermediate of specialised proresolving mediators It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It is a docosanoid, a diol and a hydroxy polyunsaturated fatty acid.

The molecule is a berberine alkaloid that consists of (S)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline bearing hydroxy and methoxy substituents at positions 6 and 9 respectively as well as methyl, methoxy and 7-hydroxy-8,9-dimethoxy-3-oxo-10H-benzo[c]pyrrolo[1',2':5,6]pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidine-10-yl groups at position 1. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, a plant metabolite, an antioxidant, an antileishmanial agent, an antineoplastic agent, an apoptosis inducer, an antibacterial agent, an antiviral agent, an anticoronaviral agent, an antiinflammatory agent, an EC 1.14.13.39 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor and an angiogenesis modulating agent. The molecule is a 1,3-thiazole that is 4,5-dihydro-1,3-thiazol-2(3H)-one substituted by a carboxy group at position 4 and a 6-hydroxybenzothiazol-2-yl moiety at position 5. The molecule is a carotenoid ether that is spirilloxanthin carrying two methoxy substituents at positions 2 and 2'. It has a role as an algal metabolite, a marine xenobiotic metabolite and a bacterial metabolite. It derives from a spirilloxanthin.

The molecule is an aromatic amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 4-({1-[4-(2,4-dimethoxyphenyl)piperazin-1-yl]ethyl}amino)benzoic acid with the amino group of 3-phenoxyaniline. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It is a N-arylpiperazine, a N-alkylpiperazine, an aromatic ether, an aromatic amide and a secondary carboxamide.

The molecule is an organosulfinate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of 2-(hydroxyethyl)sulfonic acid, obtained by deprotonation of one of the sulfinic acid groups. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from a 1-ethanolamine(1-).

The molecule is a benzoate ester obtained by the formal condensation of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid with propanol. It has been isolated from Pisonia aculeata and exhibits antitubercular activity. It has a role as an antitubercular agent, a plant metabolite and an antimicrobial agent. It derives from a 4-hydroxybenzoic acid and a propan-1-ol.
The molecule is a member of the class of benzamides that is benzamide substituted by an octyloxy group at position 2. It has a role as a metabolite and an anti-inflammatory agent.

The molecule is a flavonoid oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the 7-hydroxy group of apigenin. It is the major microspecies at pH 7.3 (according to Marvin v 6.2.0.). It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, an antioxidant and a metabolite. It is a conjugate base of an apigenin.

The molecule is an organic cation that is phenoxazin-7-ium substituted by amino group at position 3, methyl group at position 2 and a diethylamino group at position 4. The chloride salt is the histological dye 'methyl green'
The molecule is a lathyrane diterpenoid isolated from the roots of Euphorbia micractina. It is an enoate ester, a member of phenols and a lathyrane diterpenoid.

The molecule is a steroid lactone that consists of 5alpha-pregnane substituted by an oxo group at position 3, methyl groups at positions 6 and 17 and a (2E)-4-methoxy-4-oxobut-2-enoyl moiety at position 20. Isolated from Hainan soft coral Dendronephthya studeri, it exhibits cytotoxicity against human oral epidermoid carcinoma. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a delta-lactone, a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid, a member of tetracyclic triterpenoids, a methyl ester, a primary alcohol and a steroid lactone.

The molecule is an L-lysine derivative obtained by formal condensation of the side-chain carboxy group of L-lysine with the phenolic hydroxy group of 2-{4-[(2Z)-3-amino-2-hydroxyprop-2-enoyl]phenoxy}acetic acid. It has a role as a metabolite and an antibacterial agent. It is a member of furans, a monocarboxylic acid amide, a phenoxyacetate ester, a L-lysine derivative and a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid.
The molecule is an N-hydroxy-alpha-amino acid having a 9-thiaoctyl substituent at the 2-position. It derives from a dihomomethionine.
The molecule is a purine ribonucleoside 5'-triphosphate that is GTP substituted at position O(2) by an oxo group. It derives from a guanosine 5'-monophosphate and an ATP.

The molecule is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid that is pyruvic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens has been replaced by a 5,6-dihydro-4H-pyran-2(3H)-ylidene group. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid, an epoxide and a secondary alpha-hydroxy ketone. It derives from a pyruvic acid.

The molecule is a linear mannotriose consisting of three D-mannosyl residues linked sequentially alpha(1->2) and beta(1->3), with an additional D-mannosyl residue also linked alpha(1->6) to the mannose at the reducing end.

The molecule is a member of the class of pyrazoles that is 1H-pyrazole which is substituted at positions 2, 3 and 5 by trifluoromethyl, phenylcarbamoyl, and difluorophenyl groups, respectively. It has a role as an EC 1.14.13.39 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor. It is a member of pyrazoles, a secondary carboxamide, a tertiary carboxamide, an organofluorine compound and a biaryl.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that is 2-(4-{[5-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)thiophen-2-yl]methylsulfanyl}phenyl)acetic acid in which the thiophene ring has been substituted at position 5 by a p-(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group. It is an inhibitor of retinoic acid receptor beta and exhibits antitumour activity against several cancer cell lines, including human melanoma cells. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an apoptosis inducer and an EC 1.6.3.9 [retinoic acid receptor beta (RARbeta)] antagonist. It is a member of thiophenes, an aryl sulfide, a monocarboxylic acid, an aromatic ether and a member of (trifluoromethyl)benzenes.

The molecule is a sulfoglycolipid in which alpha,alpha-trehalose, sulfated at the 2'-position, is acylated at the 2-position with palmitic acid, and at the 3-position with (2E,4S,6S)-2,4,6-trimethyltetracos-2-enoic acid. It derives from an alpha,alpha-trehalose.

The molecule is a leukotriene anion that is the conjugate base of (12R)-hydroxy-10,11-dihydroleukotriene E4 arising from deprotonation of both carboxylic acid functions and protonation of the glutamyl alpha-amino group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite. It derives from an icosanoid LTC4(1-). It is a conjugate base of a (12R)-hydroxy-10,11-dihydroleukotriene E4.

The molecule is a benzothiazine that consists of phenanthridine bearing two additional methyl substituents at positions 2 and 3. It has a role as an anti-estrogen, an EC 1.4.99.1 (prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent, an antibacterial agent, an antifungal agent, an apoptosis inducer, an anticoagulant, an angiogenesis modulating agent, an analgesic, an antipyretic, a xenobiotic, a marine metabolite and a drug allergen.

The molecule is an anthracycline antibiotic that is 13-deoxydaunorubicin in which the hydroxy group at position 4 of the tetracyclic ring system has been converted to its methyl ester and the carboxy group attached to position 9 has been converted into the corresponding alpha,alpha-dimethyl derivative. It derives from a daunorubicin.

The molecule is a carbotricyclic compound that is 1,2,3a,4,5,6,7-octahydrocyclopenta[c]furan substituted by methyl groups at positions 1, 4, 6 and 8; hydroxy groups at positions 1, 2, 5 and 9; an ethyl group at position 3; oxo groups at positions 4 and 7; a (hydroxy)butanoyl group at position 6; and a beta-hydroxybutyryl group at position 3. It has been isolated from the fungus Aspergillus niger ATCC 1015. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite. It is a carbotricyclic compound, a cyclic ketone, a diol, a secondary alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, a primary alpha-hydroxy ketone and a beta-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is a carboxylic ester resulting from the formal condensation of methyl (2S)-2-aminohexanoate with the carboxy group of N,N'-dinitropenta-2,4-dienamide. It has a role as an EC 3.5.1.98 (histone deacetylase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It is a C-nitro compound, a primary carboxamide, a secondary amino compound and a carboxylic ester.

The molecule is a disaccharide derivative that consists of alpha-L-arabinopyranose and 6-O-cyano-alpha-D-glucopyranoside residues joined in sequence by a (1->2) glycosidic bond. It derives from an alpha-L-arabinopyranose and a 6-O-cyano-alpha-D-glucose.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid monoanion that results from the removal of a proton from one of the carboxy groups of 2-(2-hydroxyethoxy)furoic acid. It derives from a furancarboxylate and a dihydrogenfuranate.
The molecule is a cyclic ether that consists of two oxolane rings joined by an oxygen bridge. It has a role as a non-polar solvent and a metabolite.

The molecule is a straight-chain saturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of behenic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a long-chain fatty acid anion, a straight-chain saturated fatty acid anion and a fatty acid anion 20:0. It is a conjugate base of a docosanoic acid.

The molecule is an amino octasaccharide comprising two D-GlcNS(6S) residues, one D-GlcA residue, three D-GlcNS(6S) residues, a single D-GlcA residue and two D-GlcA residues (one of which is at the reducing end) all linked sequentially 1->4, with the GlcNAc residues being connected via glycosidic linkages to 2-nitrophenol and the non-reducing-end glucuronic acid residue also carrying a 4-nitrophenyl substituent. It is an amino oligosaccharide, a carbohydrate acid derivative and an oligosaccharide sulfate.
The molecule is a phosphatidylcholine 40:1 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are eicosanoyl and oleoyl respectively. It derives from an icosanoic acid and an oleic acid.

The molecule is an aldonolactone obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of D-arabinonic acid with the 1-hydroxy group of L-arabino-furanose. It has a role as a metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is an organic sodium salt that is the monosodium salt of lomitapide. Used for treatment of hepatic encephalopathy and hyperammonaemia in patients with liver cirrhosis. It has a role as a prodrug, a hepatoprotective agent and a glutamine antagonist. It contains a lomitapide(1-).

The molecule is an L-proline derivative that is the ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-proline with the 3'-hydroxy group of AMP. It has a role as a Mycoplasma genitalium metabolite and a Mycoplasma pneumoniae metabolite. It is an adenosine 5'-phosphate, a L-proline derivative, an alpha-amino acid ester and a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate. It derives from an adenosine 5'-monophosphate.

The molecule is a dipeptide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of N-(3,5-difluorophenyl)-L-alaninamide with the amino group of L-valyl-D-tert-butyl ester. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent and a bacterial metabolite.

The molecule is a branched amino octasaccharide comprising a linear trisaccharide of beta-D-mannose, N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine and N-acetyl-alpha-D-galactosamine residues linked sequentially (1->4) and (1->6), to the mannosyl residue of which are also linked (1->3) and (1->4) two further beta-D-mannosyl-(1->4)-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannosyl tetrasaccharide units. It has a role as an epitope. It is an amino octasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.
The molecule is a hydrate that is the dihydrate form of vanadic acid. It has a role as an oxidising agent, a poison and a carcinogenic agent. It contains a vanadate(2-).

The molecule is a ceramide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of tricosanoic acid with the amino group of 14-methylhexadecasphingosine. It is a metabolite of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. It has a role as a Caenorhabditis elegans metabolite. It derives from a 14-methylhexadecasphingosine and a tricosanoic acid.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid anion that results from the removal of a proton from the carboxylic acid group of (R)-pantothenic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a pantoate. It is a conjugate base of a (R)-pantoic acid.

The molecule is a UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-alanine in which the muramoyl fragment has alpha-configuration at its anomeric centre. It derives from an UDP-alpha-D-MurNAc-L-Ala and an alpha-D-alanine. It is a conjugate acid of an UDP-2,6-diacetamido-3-amino-2,3,4,6-tetradeoxy-alpha-D-glucopyranose(3-).

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of ent-kaur-16-en-19-oic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an EC 2.5.1.58 (protein farnesyltransferase) inhibitor. It derives from a kaur-16-ene-19-oate.

The molecule is a quercetin O-glucoside that is the 2'',3''-dihydro derivative of myricetin 3-O-(6-deoxy-L-malonyl)-beta-D-glucopyranoside. Isolated from Pisonia aculeata and Myrica rubra, it exhibits antineoplastic activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a beta-D-glucoside, a carboxylic ester, a monosaccharide derivative, a polyphenol, a quercetin O-glucoside and a dimethoxyflavone.

The molecule is a cholesterol ester obtained by the formal condensation of cholesterol with linoleic acid. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It derives from a linoleic acid.
The molecule is an organic disulfide that results from the formal oxidative dimerisation of 2,4-dimethyldodecane-1-thiol. It has a role as a metabolite and an allergen.

The molecule is the (S)-enantiomer of laudanine. It has a role as an EC 2.1.1.70 [3',4'-methylenedioxytyramine oxidase (quinone)] inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It derives from a (S)-nandinine. It is a conjugate base of a (S)-laudanine(1+).
The molecule is an N-acyl-15-methylhexadecasphing-4-enine in which the acyl group has 29 carbons and 0 double bonds and is 2-hydroxylated. It derives from a 15-methylhexadecasphing-4-enine.

The molecule is a member of the class of chromenes that is (3S)-chromene which is substituted by methoxy groups at positions 6 and 7, cyclopropylmethyl group at position 2, an amino group at position 5, and a [4-amino-5-(hydroxymethyl)pyrimidin-2-yl]methyl group at position 3. It has been found to inhibit the growth of several human cancer cell lines including A-549 lung carcinoma cells, HT-29 colon adenocarcinoma cells, SK-OV-3 ovarian cancer cells, U87 glioblastoma cells, and PC-3 prostate cancer cells. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an apoptosis inducer and an EC 1.5.1.3 [dihydroorotate oxidase (fumarate)] inhibitor. It is a member of pyrimidines, a primary amino compound, a secondary amino compound, a polyether, a member of chromenes and a member of cyclopropanes.

The molecule is a thienopyridine that consists of 4,5,6,7-tetrahydrothieno[3,2-c]pyridine bearing an additional phenyl substituent at position 1. It has a role as a P2Y12 receptor antagonist and an anticoagulant.

The molecule is a steroid acid that consists of 5alpha-cholestan-26-oic acid bearing oxo substituents at positions 3 and 7 as well as methyl and vinyl substituents at position 4. An intermediate in the biosynthesis of ergosterol by Candida albicans It has a role as a Candida albicans metabolite. It is an enone, a 3-oxo-Delta(1) steroid, a 7-oxo steroid, a steroid acid, a polyketide and a monocarboxylic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzamides obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of salicylic acid with one of the amino groups of aniline. It has a role as an EC 2.3.1.48 (histone acetyltransferase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and an apoptosis inducer. It derives from a salicylanilide and a salicylic acid.

The molecule is an N(2)-acylglutamine resulting from the formal condensation of the amino group of L-glutamic acid with the carboxy group of 4-indoleacetic acid. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a human urinary metabolite. It derives from a 4-indolylacetic acid.

The molecule is a trisaccharide consisting of two beta-D-glucopyranose residues and an L-arabinofuranose residue joined in sequence by (1->2) glycosidic bonds. It derives from a beta-D-Glcp-(1->2)-beta-D-Glcp and a L-arabinofuranose.

The molecule is a glycosylgalactose consisting of beta-L-fucopyranose and D-galactopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1->3) glycosidic bond. It derives from a beta-L-fucose and a D-galactopyranose.

The molecule is a polyprenyl glucuronic acid that is 3-deoxy-D-manno-octulosonic acid attached to a undecaprenyl group via a glycosyl phosphate linkage. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranosonic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 3-deoxy-D-manno-octulosonate-1-phosphate-1-undecaprenol(2-).

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol 3-phosphate(2-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 1-oleoyl-2-arachidonoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate. It is a conjugate base of a 1-oleoyl-2-arachidonoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate.

The molecule is a 2-monoglyceride resulting from the condensation of the carboxy group of prostaglandin F2alpha with the 2-hydroxy group of glycerol. It has a role as an antiglaucoma drug, an antihypertensive agent and a vasodilator agent. It derives from a prostaglandin F2alpha.
The molecule is a glycosylfucose consisting of an alpha-L-rhamnosyl residue attached at the 3-position to beta-D-galactose. It has a role as an epitope and an antigen.

The molecule is the conjugate base of ammonia; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a cofactor. It is an inorganic molecular entity, a monoatomic nitrogen and a monovalent inorganic anion.

The molecule is a branched octasaccharide comprising eight D-arabinofuranose units, in an assembly consisting of two arabinose residues linked alpha(1->5) with beta-arabinosyl-(1->2)-alpha-arabinosyl and alpha-arabinosyl-(1->3)-beta-arabinosyl tetrasaccharide units linked to respectively the 3- and 5-positions of the residue distal from the reducing-end residue.

The molecule is a linear amino tetrasaccharide comprising an N-acetylglucosamine residue, two galactose residues and one glucose residue (at the reducing end) in a (1->4), (1->3), (1->4) sequence. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a member of the class of 2-benzofurans that is 1,3-dihydro-2H-benzo[f]furan substituted by an oxo group at position 3. It has been isolated from Penicillium species and Aspergillus niger.
