It has a role as an EC 5.99.1.2 (DNA topoisomerase) inhibitor, an antimicrobial agent, an antineoplastic agent, a Penicillium metabolite and an Aspergillus metabolite.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid that consists of 1,4-dioxobuta-1,3-diene bearing two carboxy substituents at positions 2 and 5. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite. It derives from a butadiene-1,4-diol. It is a conjugate acid of a fumarate(2-).

The molecule is a member of the class of aminotoluenes that is 2,4-diaminotoluene carrying additional hydroxy and hydroxymethyl substituents at positions 5 and 6 respectively. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a member of hydroxylamines, an aminotoluene and a substituted aniline. It derives from a 2,4-diaminotoluene.

The molecule is a member of the class of xanthones that is 9H-xanthen-9-one substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1 and 5, an oxo group at position 8 and a 3-methylbut-1-en-3-yl group at position 2. It has been isolated from Cratoxylum cochinchinense. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a member of xanthones, a polyphenol and a cyclic ketone.

The molecule is tetraanion of 5,6,7,8-tetrahydromethanopterin arising from deprotonation of carboxylic acid and phosphate functions; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a methanopterin(4-).

The molecule is a member of the class of quinolones that is 4-oxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline which is substituted at positions 1 and 6 by methyl groups, at position 8 by chlorine, and at positions 3 and 7 by amino(p-chlorophenyl)methyl and [(1R)-1-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)ethyl] groups, respectively. It has been found to inhibit the growth of several human tumour cell lines including colon cancer cells. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and an EC 5.99.1.3 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor. It is a quinolone, a secondary amino compound, a tertiary amino compound, a member of imidazoles, an organochlorine compound and a cyclic ketone.

The molecule is a hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion that results from the removal of a proton from the carboxylic acid group of (S)-3,4-dihydroxybutanoic acid. It derives from a butyrate. It is a conjugate base of a (S)-3,4-dihydroxybutyric acid and a (S)-3,4-dihydroxymandelic acid.

The molecule is a 3beta-sterol that consists of 4alpha,12alpha-dimethylandrosta-7,16-diene having an additional alpha-methyl substituent at position 9 and a beta-hydroxy group at position 3. It has a role as a human metabolite. It derives from a hydride of a 5alpha-cholestane.

The molecule is a sesquiterpene alkaloid that consists of 19-hydroxysenecionane substituted by an acetyloxy group at position 2, methyl groups at positions 8 and 14, hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 15 and a (6'-acetyloxydaunorubicinyl)carbonyl group attached to the tertiary amino function. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a metabolite. It is a dihydroagarofuran sesquiterpenoid, a macrolide, a pyridine alkaloid, a sesquiterpene alkaloid, an acetate ester and a secondary alcohol.

The molecule is a fifteen-membered glycopeptide comprising glycyl, cyclohexylglycyl, alanyl, glycyl, 4-hydroxyphenylalanyl, (5R)-5-(beta-D-galactopyranosyloxy)lysyl, glycyl. alpha-glutamyl, glutaminyl, glycyl, prolyl, lysyl, glycyl, alpha-glutamyl and threonine residues coupled in sequence.

The molecule is a steroid ester that is pregn-4-en-21-yl acetate substituted by oxo groups at positions 3 and 20. It has been isolated from the Hainan soft coral Lobophytum cristatum. It has a role as a coral metabolite, an anti-inflammatory agent and an EC 1.8.1.9 [aldehyde reductase (NADPH)] inhibitor. It is a 20-oxo steroid, a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid and a steroid ester.

The molecule is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (8Z,11Z,14Z,17Z)-3-oxoicosatetraenoic acid. It is a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA and an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from an all-cis-icosa-8,11,14,17-tetraenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of an (8Z,11Z,14Z,17Z)-3-oxoicosatetraenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is an N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminide having a 2-nitrophenyl substituent at the anomeric position. It has a role as a chromogenic compound. It is a C-nitro compound and a N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminide.

The molecule is an organic heteropentacyclic compound and cyclic hemiketal isolated from the marine sponge Melophlus sarasinorum and has been shown to exhibit cytotoxic activity. It has a role as a metabolite, an antineoplastic agent and an animal metabolite. It is an organic heteropentacyclic compound, a cyclic ether, a lactone, an organoboron compound, a secondary alcohol and a tertiary amino compound.

The molecule is a 2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1,3-dioxolane in which the stereocentre attached to position 5 has R-configuration while that attached to position 4 has S-configuration. It is an enantiomer of a (S)-(+)-naringenin.

The molecule is a steroid phosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of betamethasone phosphate. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory drug and an immunosuppressive agent. It is a conjugate base of a betamethasone phosphate.

The molecule is a member of the class of pterocarpans that is (6aR,11aS)-pterocarpan substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 9 and a methoxy group at position 4. It has been isolated from Glycyrrhiza uralensis. It has a role as an antiplasmodial drug and a plant metabolite. It is a member of phenols and a member of pterocarpans.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy groups of coumarin-3-bis(2,2'-iminodiethyl acetal). It is a conjugate base of a coumarin-3-bis(2,2'-iminodiethyl acetal).

The molecule is an L-phenylalanine derivative resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of arachidonic acid with the amino group of L-phenylalanine. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a N-acyl-L-amino acid, a fatty amide and a L-phenylalanine derivative. It derives from an arachidonic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a N-arachidonoyl-L-phenylalaninate.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 4-(phenylamino)benzoic acid with the amino group of pyridine. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.2 (non-specific serine/threonine protein kinase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and an apoptosis inducer. It is a member of pyridines, a secondary carboxamide and a monocarboxylic acid amide.

The molecule is a branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of an N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residue, two D-glucose residues and two L-glycero-alpha-D-manno-heptose (Hep) residues (one at the reducing end) in a linear sequence, with three Hep residues linked alpha(1->2), one of which also carries a phospho group. The heposyl residue distal from the reducing-end GlcNAc residue has a further Hep residue attached via an alpha(1->3) linkage. It is an oligosaccharide phosphate and an amino pentasaccharide.

The molecule is a beta-alanine derivative that consists of propionic acid bearing an 6-aminohexanoyl substituent. It has a role as a metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a beta-alanine and a 5-aminopentanoic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of pradimicins that is isolated from Streptomyces pristinaespiralis. It exhibits antibacterial, antifungal and antineoplastic activities. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antineoplastic agent, an antifungal agent and a bacterial metabolite. It is a cyclic ketone, a polyketide, a secondary alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, a polyphenol and a member of pradimicins.

The molecule is an organoammonium salt resulting from the formal reaction of equimolar amounts of (S)-carfentrazone and glycol. It contains a (S)-carfentrazone(1+). It is an enantiomer of a (R)-carfentrazone glycolate.

The molecule is a butan-4-olide having a cyclopropylmethoxy group at the 3-position, a phenylsulfonyl group at the 5-position and two methyl substituents at position 2. It has a role as an EC 1.13.11.34 (arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase) inhibitor and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug. It is a sulfone and a member of cyclopropanes.

The molecule is a homodetic cyclic peptide that consists of L-threonyl, 3-hydroxy-L-lysyl, D-valyl, L-seryl, 3-hydroxy-D-tryptophyl and L-isoleucyl residues coupled in sequence with the thiazole ring being connected to the side chain amino group of the lysyl residue. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor, an antimicrobial agent, an antineoplastic agent, a bacterial metabolite and an antifungal agent.

The molecule is an alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid that is henicosane in which the methylene hydrogens at positions 2 and 21 have been replaced by carboxy groups. It has a role as a human metabolite. It derives from a hydride of a henicosane.

The molecule is a cyclitol phosphate that is the 1-amino-2,3-dideoxy-scyllo-inososyl derivative of D-ribofuranose 5-phosphate. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a scyllo-inositol.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acid that is 4,8-dihydronaphthalene substituted by two carboxy groups at positions 1 and 3. It has been isolated from the roots of Rubia yunnanensis. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a plant metabolite and an apoptosis inducer. It is a straight-chain unsaturated monocarboxylic acid, a medium-chain fatty acid and a polyunsaturated fatty acid.

The molecule is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid that is butanedioic acid in which the hydrogens at positions 3 and 5 are substituted by chlorine. It has a role as an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a herbicide. It is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid, an organochlorine compound and an oxo dicarboxylic acid. It derives from a butenedioic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of imidazoles that carries tert-butoxycarbonyl and 4-chlorophenyl substituents at positions 1 and 3 respectively. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.2 (non-specific serine/threonine protein kinase) inhibitor, an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic. It is a member of monochlorobenzenes, a carbamate ester, an aromatic ether and a member of imidazoles.

The molecule is an indole alkaloid that is 1,2,3,4,9,10-hexahydro-6H-5,8b-ethanoindolo[3,2,1-ij]quinoline substituted by a methyl group at position 7 and a methoxycarbonyl group at position 1. It has been isolated from the ethanol extract of the stems of Brucea mollis. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is an organic heteropentacyclic compound, a methyl ester, an aromatic ether, an alkaloid ester, an indole alkaloid and a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid.
The molecule is an aminobenzenesulfonic acid that is benzenesulfonic acid substituted by an amino group at position 2. It has a role as a metabolite and a xenobiotic metabolite.
The molecule is a 2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid that is pyruvic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens has been replaced by a phenyl group. It derives from an acrylic acid and a pyruvic acid.

The molecule is a piperidinemonocarboxylic acid that is pipecolic acid substituted by an oxo group at position 2. It has been isolated from the plant species of the genus Piper. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite.
The molecule is the stable isotope of boron with relative atomic mass 10.023845, 96 atom percent natural abundance and nuclear spin 3/2.

The molecule is a member of the class of imidazolidines that is 1,4-dihydroimidazolidine which is substituted at positions 2 and 5 by methyl groups and at position 3 by a cis,cis-farnesyl group. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an EC 6.4.1.2 (glutamate--ammonia ligase) inhibitor, an apoptosis inducer, an antibacterial agent, an antifungal agent, an antiprotozoal drug, an antiviral agent, a plant metabolite, a rat metabolite and a xenobiotic metabolite. It is a member of imidazolidines and a tertiary amino compound.
The molecule is a ceramide 1-phosphate(2-) in which the N-acyl group is specified as tetracosanoyl; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of a N-tetracosanoylsphingosine 1-phosphate.

The molecule is an anthraquinone that is 1,6-dihydroxy-9,10-anthraquinone which is substituted by a methyl group at position 2, a hydroxy group at position 3, methoxy groups at positions 5 and 8, a (1E)-4-hydroxy-3-methylbutanoyl group at position 7, and by oxo groups at positions 1 and 6. It has been isolated from the roots of Rubia yunnanensis. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an acetate ester, a polyphenol, an aromatic ether, a tertiary alcohol, a secondary alcohol and an anthraquinone.
The molecule is a thiocarbonyl compound that consists of 1,2,4-thiadiazole bearing an amino substituent at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite and an allergen.

The molecule is a pyridine nucleotide having pyridinium-4,5-dicarbamoylmethylidene as the nucleobase. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a nicotinic acid D-ribonucleotide.

The molecule is a monosaccharide derivative that consists of 9,10-anthraquinone bearing an alpha-D-glucosyloxy substituent at position 2. It has been isolated from the roots of Rubia yunnanensis. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a beta-D-glucoside, a monosaccharide derivative and a member of anthracenes.

The molecule is an alpha,beta-unsaturated monocarboxylic acid that is trans-2-dodecenoic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 13 has been replaced by a methyl group. It is an alpha,beta-unsaturated monocarboxylic acid, an alkanoic acid and a medium-chain fatty acid.

The molecule is an organic heteroheptacyclic compound that is 1H,6H-2,5-epoxyoxocino[3',4':7,8]furo[2,3-h]chromen-9(10H)-one substituted by a hydroxy group at position 1 and methoxy groups at positions 4a and 10. It has been isolated from the leaves of Calophyllum brasiliense. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a gamma-lactone, an aromatic ether, an enol, an organic heteroheptacyclic compound and an oxacycle.

The molecule is a diketone that consists of pentane bearing two oxo substituents at positions 2 and 4 as well as an hydroxy substituent at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and an Escherichia coli metabolite. It is a secondary alcohol, a methyl ketone and a diketone.

The molecule is a stilbenoid isolated from the stems of Kobresia nepalensis and has been shown to exhibit inhibitory activity against NF-kappaB. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a metabolite and a NF-kappaB inhibitor. It is a member of resorcinols, an olefinic compound, an aromatic ether and a stilbenoid.

The molecule is a 3beta-hydroxy steroid that consists of 5alpha-androstane bearing two additional hydroxy substituents at positions 17 and 20. It has a role as an androgen, a human metabolite, a Daphnia magna metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hydride of a 5alpha-androstane.

The molecule is a spirostanyl glycoside that consists of (3beta,5alpha,6beta)-spirostan-17-ol attached to a beta-D-glucopyranosyl residue at position 3 and a alpha-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1->2)-beta-D-galactopyranoside moiety at position 6 via a glycosidic linkage. Isolated from the whole plants of Silybum marianum, it exhibits inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase. It has a role as an EC 2.7.7.49 (RNA-directed DNA polymerase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a cyclic ether, a monosaccharide derivative, a disaccharide derivative, a spirostanyl glycoside and a tertiary alcohol.

The molecule is a steroid glucosiduronic acid obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of hyocholic acid with the anomeric hydroxy group of beta-D-glucuronic acid. It has a role as a human urinary metabolite and a rat metabolite. It is a beta-D-glucosiduronic acid, a dicarboxylic acid monoester, a 3alpha-hydroxy steroid, a 7alpha-hydroxy steroid and a steroid glucosiduronic acid. It derives from a hyocholic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a hyocholate 24-O-(beta-D-glucuronide)(1-).

The molecule is an aryl sulfate that is 6,7-dimethylisoalloxazine carrying two additional sulfo substituents at positions 4' and 4''. It has a role as a human metabolite. It derives from a hydride of an isoalloxazine.

The molecule is a (2S)-2-methylacyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (2S)-2-methyltetradecanoic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a tetradecanoyl-CoA and a (2S)-2-methyltetradecanoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (2S)-2-methyltetradecanoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is a linear amino tetrasaccharide comprising an alpha-N-acetylneuraminyl residue (2->3)-linked to the galactose residue of N-acetyllactosamine, which is in turn linked beta(1->4) to another alpha-N-acetylneuraminyl residue. It has a role as an epitope and an antigen. It is an amino tetrasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a hydroxyamine that consists of 3-(methylsulfanyl)alanine bearing an additional amino substituent at position 2 as well as a hydroxy group attached to the alpha-nitrogen. It is a primary alcohol, a member of hydroxylamines and a methyl sulfide.

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine(1-) in which the acyl substituents at positions 1 and 2 are specified as arachidonoyl and oleoyl respectively; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an arachidonic acid and an oleic acid. It is a conjugate base of a N-arachidonoyl-1-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine.
The molecule is a single-stranded DNA polynucleotide consisting of two deoxyguanosine residues connected by 3'->5' phosphodiester linkages and with a phosphoric residue at the 5' terminus.

The molecule is a maleate salt obtained by combining enalaprilat with one molar equivalent of maleic acid. An angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor, it is used in the treatment of hypertension and heart failure. It has a role as an EC 3.4.15.1 (peptidyl-dipeptidase A) inhibitor, an antihypertensive agent and a cardioprotective agent. It contains an enalaprilat(1+).

The molecule is a sulfonamide consisting of pyrimidine having a 4-chlorophenylsulfamoyl group at the 2-position. It has a role as an antiinfective agent, an EC 2.5.1.15 (dihydropteroate synthase) inhibitor and an antibacterial drug. It is a member of pyrimidines, a sulfonamide, a member of monochlorobenzenes and a sulfonamide antibiotic.

The molecule is a N-acylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as pentacosanoyl. It has a role as a Papio hamadryas metabolite and an EC 3.4.21.98 (prolyl oligopeptidase) inhibitor. It derives from a pentacosanoic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzodioxoles that is 6-methoxyflavanone attached to a beta-D-glucopyranosyloxy residue at position 7 via a glycosidic linkage. It has been isolated from Pisonia aculeata. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is an aromatic ether, a monosaccharide derivative, a member of benzodioxoles and a beta-D-glucoside.

The molecule is trication of spermidine arising from protonation of all three amino groups; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a conjugate acid of a spermidine.

The molecule is an arenesulfonate ester that is 2-(trifluoromethyl)benzenesulfonic acid in which the hydrogen of the hydroxy group has been replaced by a 6-phenoxyquinolin-8-yl group. It is used as a fluorescent probe for detecting reactive oxygen species and nitric oxide. It has a role as a fluorochrome, a nitric oxide donor, a biological pigment, an antioxidant and a probe. It is an organofluorine compound, an aryl sulfate, a member of quinolines and a ring assembly.
The molecule is a retinol in which the double bond at position 9 has cis configuration, while that at position 16 has trans configuration. It derives from an all-trans-retinol and a 9-cis-retinol.

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups positions 1 and 2 are specified as lauroyl and oleoyl respectively. It has a role as a mouse metabolite. It derives from an oleic acid and a dodecanoic acid.

The molecule is a spirostanyl glycoside that consists of (3beta,5alpha,6beta)-spirostan-17-ol having beta-D-glucopyranosyl and alpha-L-rhamnopyranosyl residues attached at positions 3 and 28 respectively via glycosidic linkages. Isolated from the roots of Breynia fruticosa, it exhibits cytotoxicity against human cancer cell lines. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a monosaccharide derivative, a spirostanyl glycoside, a hexacyclic triterpenoid and a cyclic hemiketal.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid that is olean-12-ene substituted by an alpha-hydroxy group at position 3 and a carboxy group at position 28. It has been isolated from the leaves of Fatsia polycarpa. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a hydroxy monocarboxylic acid, a pentacyclic triterpenoid and a secondary alcohol. It derives from a hydride of an oleanane.

The molecule is an N-acylmorpholine obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of (3Z)-dodec-3-enoic acid with the amino group of morpholine. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite.
The molecule is a cobalt coordination entity consisting of two chlorine ions bound to a central cobalt atom. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a cofactor.
The molecule is an organosulfonate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the sulfonic acid groups of Acid blue 20. It is a conjugate base of an Acid blue 20 (acid form).

The molecule is a member of the class of sulfamic acids that is sulfamic acid in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by an 8-methylnonyl group. It has a role as a kairomone and a Daphnia pulex metabolite. It derives from a tungstate(1-).
The molecule is a diamino-1,3,5-triazine that is 6-isobutyl-1,3,5-triazin-2-amine substituted by an amino group at positions 4 and 6. It has a role as a xenobiotic metabolite.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzoic acids that is 1,3,5-triiodo-2-acetamidobenzoic acid in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen atom at position 6 has been replaced by an acetyl group. It has a role as a radioopaque medium and a xenobiotic metabolite. It is a N-acetyl-amino acid, an organoiodine compound and a member of benzoic acids.

The molecule is a phosphatidylcholine 38:4 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are octadecanoyl and arachidonoyl respectively. It derives from an arachidonic acid and an octadecanoic acid.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the five amino groups and deprotonation of the carboxy group of streptothricin D. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite. It is an ammonium ion derivative, an organic cation and a monocarboxylic acid anion. It is a conjugate base of a streptothricin D.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of both amino groups of spermidine. It has a role as a human metabolite and a fundamental metabolite. It is an ammonium ion derivative, an organic cation and an iminium ion. It is a conjugate acid of a spermidine(2+).

The molecule is a nitrile that consists of hydrogen and carbon carrying two cyano substituents. It has a role as an EC 3.5.1.4 (amidase) inhibitor, a metabolite, a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a biladiene that consists of 1,2-dihydrophenalene-3,4-dione bearing two indol-3-ylmethyl substituents at positions 5 and 6 as well as two carboxyethyl substituents at positions 7 and 8. The parent of the class of bilirubinoids. It has a role as an antioxidant, a human metabolite, a mouse metabolite and a cofactor.

The molecule is a sialotriaosylceramide consisting of two sialo residues attached to the primary hydroxy function of ceramide. It has a role as an epitope. It derives from a beta-D-GalNAc-(1->4)-[alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->3)]-beta-D-Gal-(1->4)-beta-D-Glc-(1<->1')-Cer(d18:1/20:0).

The molecule is a tetrahydroxyflavan that consists of (2S)-flavan substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3, 5, 7 and 4' respectively. It has been isolated from the buds of Cleistocalyx operculatus. It has a role as a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a long-chain fatty acid ethyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of oleic acid with the hydroxy group of ethanol. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, a plant metabolite and an insect repellent. It derives from an oleic acid.

The molecule is a butan-4-olide having a (2-methoxysulfonyl)oxy group at the 3-position and two methyl substituents at the 5-position. It has a role as an EC 6.4.1.2 [acetyl-CoA carboxylase (carboxylating)] inhibitor, a herbicide, an agrochemical and a carotenoid biosynthesis inhibitor. It is a butan-4-olide and a sulfone.
The molecule is an organoammonium salt resulting from the formal reaction of equimolar amounts of iodomethoate and L-thyroxine. It contains a 1,3,5-triiodo-L-thyroninate.

The molecule is pentaanion of malonyl-CoA arising from deprotonation of phosphate, diphosphate and carboxylic acid functions. It has a role as a human metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a malonyl-CoA.

The molecule is a decanoate ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of decanoic acid with the hydroxy group of 5-bromoindole-3-acetic acid. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a serotonergic agonist. It is a member of indoles, an organobromine compound and a decanoate ester.

The molecule is a member of the class of chalcones that consists of trans-chalcone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 4 and 2', an prenyloxy group at position 3' and a methyl group at position 4'. Isolated from the buds of Cleistocalyx operculatus, it has been shown to exhibit inhibitory effects on the viral neuraminidases from two influenza viral strains, H1N1 and H9N2. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an EC 3.2.1.18 (exo-alpha-sialidase) inhibitor. It is a member of chalcones, a polyphenol and an aromatic ether.

The molecule is a C-glycosyl compound that consists of (1R)-2,3,4,9-tetrahydro-1H-cyclopenta[c]quinoline bearing two hydroxy substituents at positions 6 and 8 as well as an alpha-L-arabinopyranosyloxy substituent at position 7. It has a role as a metabolite. It is a member of cyclopentaphenones, a monohydroxyquinoline, a C-glycosyl compound and a secondary alcohol.

The molecule is a furanocoumarin that is 2H-furo[3,2-g]chromen-7-one substituted by hydroxy group at position 5, a tert-butyloxy group at position 6 and a (1S)-1-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-yl group at position 8. Isolated from the roots of Ferula fukanensis, it inhibits production of nitric oxide (NO). It has a role as a metabolite and an EC 1.14.13.39 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor. It is a furanocoumarin, a member of phenols and an aromatic ether.

The molecule is a gamma-amino acid that consists of cyclohexanecarboxylic acid bearing an amino substituent at position 4. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a cyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid.

The molecule is an epoxide isolated from the fermentation broth of Streptomyces sp. E-1623 that exhibits inhibitory activity against acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase 2. It has a role as an EC 2.3.1.26 (sterol O-acyltransferase) inhibitor and a bacterial metabolite. It is an enamide, an epoxide, a cyclic ketone, a secondary alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, a diol, a monocarboxylic acid amide and a secondary carboxamide.

The molecule is a dihydroxydocosahexaenoate that is the conjugate base of (4Z,7Z,10Z,12E,16Z,19Z)-14,22-dihydroxydocosahexaenoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of a (4Z,7Z,10Z,12E,16Z,19Z)-14,22-dihydroxyicosapentaenoic acid.

The molecule is a heterodetic cyclic peptide consisting of the linear sequence Cys-Gly-Cys-Ser-Thr-Lys-Glu-Asn-Leu-Gln-Phe-Tyr-His-Ala-Asp-Val-Met-Leu-Pro-Arg-Leu-Glu-Thr-Ile-Lys-Ser-Gly-NH2 cyclised by two disulfide bridges from the thiol groups of each cysteine residue. It has a role as an epitope and a metabolite.
The molecule is a (2S)-2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid that is lactic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens has been replaced by a phenyl group. It derives from a rac-lactic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of 3,4-dihydroxybenzenes that is catechol in which one of the hydrogens ortho to both hydroxy groups has been replaced by a nitro group. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a C-nitro compound and a member of 3,4-dihydroxybenzenes.

The molecule is a 3',5'-cyclic purine nucleotide(1-) that results from the removal of a proton from the phosphate group of 8-bromoguanosine 3',5'-cyclic monophosphate; major species at pH 7.3 It derives from a 3',5'-cyclic GMP(1-). It is a conjugate base of an 8-bromoguanosine 3',5'-cyclic monophosphate.
The molecule is a D-galactosylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as docosanoyl. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and a rat metabolite. It derives from a docosanoic acid.

The molecule is a monosaccharide derivative that consists of trans-sinapic acid attached to a beta-D-glucopyranosyl residue at position 2 via a glycosidic linkage. It has a role as an antioxidant and a plant metabolite. It is a member of methoxybenzenes, a primary alcohol, a cinnamate ester and a monosaccharide derivative. It derives from a trans-sinapic acid.

The molecule is an L-polyhomomethionine zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tetrahomomethionine; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a tautomer of a L-tetrahomomethionine.

The molecule is a member of the class of azabicycloalkanes that is (3aS,4R,7aR)-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptanecarboxamide substituted at position 6 by an O-sulfooxy group and at position 5 by an oxo group. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite. It is an amino acid amide, an alicyclic ketone, an organic sulfate and a member of azabicycloalkanes.

The molecule is a diterpene glycoside that is the 19-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl derivative of steviol. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, a plant metabolite and a sweetening agent. It is a beta-D-glucoside, a lactone, a bridged compound, a diterpenoid, a monosaccharide derivative, a monocarboxylic acid and a tirucallane diterpenoid. It derives from a steviol.

The molecule is a catechin that consists of (+)-catechin bearing an additional hydroxy substituent at position 6'. It has a role as a metabolite, an antioxidant and an EC 3.2.1.48 (protein-tyrosine-phosphatase) inhibitor.

The molecule is a cytochalasan alkaloid found in Chaetomium globosum. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a Chaetomium metabolite. It is a cytochalasan alkaloid, an epoxide, a member of indoles, a macrocycle and an acetate ester.
The molecule is a member of the class of pyridines that is pyridine substituted by chloro groups at positions 2 and 6. It has a role as an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a herbicide.

The molecule is a carbohydrate acid derivative anion that is the conjugate base of 2-O-(alpha-D-glucopyranosyl)glycerol, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a glycerol. It is a conjugate base of an alpha-D-galactose.

The molecule is an L-lysine derivative that is the sulfonamide obtained by formal condensation of the sulfo group of 5-(dimethylamino)naphthalene-1-sulfonic acid with the epsilon-amino group of L-lysine. It has a role as a fluorochrome, a carcinogenic agent and an allergen. It is a N-acyl-L-lysine, a sulfonamide and a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid.
The molecule is an amino cyclitol that is scyllo-inositol in which the hydroxy group at position 1 is replaced by a guanidino group. It derives from a scyllo-inositol.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that consists of acrylic acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2. It has a role as a human metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from an acrylic acid.

The molecule is an L-methionine derivative that is the ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-methionine with the 3'-hydroxy group of AMP. It has a role as a Mycoplasma genitalium metabolite and a Mycoplasma pneumoniae metabolite. It is an adenosine 5'-phosphate, a L-methionine derivative, an alpha-amino acid ester and a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate. It derives from an adenosine 5'-monophosphate.
The molecule is a 2-hydroxy fatty acid that is alpha-linolenic acid in which the pro-R hydrogen at position 2 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It derives from an alpha-linolenic acid.

The molecule is a member of the class of ureas that is urea in which one of the hydrogens attached to each nitrogen has been replaced by an amino group. It derives from a 1,2-urea and a carbamic acid.
The molecule is a phenyl acetate obtained by the formal condensation of hydroxy group of 2-(acetyloxy)benzene-1,4-diol with acetic acid. It has a role as an antifungal agent and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is an amino acid zwitterion, obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxylic acid group to the amino group of (2S,3R)-4-hydroxy-D-phenylalanine. It is an enantiomer of a (2R,3S)-4-hydroxy-L-phenylalaninate. It is a tautomer of a (2S,3R)-4-hydroxy-D-phenylalanine.

The molecule is a heparan sulfate consisting of alpha-L-idopyranuronic acid and 2N,6-O-disulfo-alpha-D-glucosamine residues joined in sequence by a (1->4) glycosidic bond. Sequence: IdoA-GlcNS6S. It is an amino disaccharide, a member of glucosamine sulfates, a heparin disaccharide and an oligosaccharide sulfate.

The molecule is a 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositol 5-phosphate in which the phosphatidyl acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as stearoyl and arachidonoyl respectively. It derives from an octadecanoic acid and an arachidonic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a 1-stearoyl-2-arachidonoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-1D-myo-inositol 5-phosphate(3-).

The molecule is a member of the class of quinolines that is 1,2-dihydroquinoline which is substituted at positions 4 and 8 by trifluoromethyl groups, and at position 3 by a (2-hydroxycyclohexyl)oxy group. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It is a tertiary alcohol, an aromatic ether, a member of quinolines, an organofluorine compound and a secondary amino compound.

The molecule is a member of the class of chalcones that is trans-chalcone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 2', 4 and 6' and methoxy groups at positions 3', 5' and 7 respectively. It has a role as an antiplasmodial drug and a metabolite. It is a member of chalcones, a polyphenol and a dimethoxybenzene.
The molecule is a HODE that consists of 9E,12Z-octadecadienoic acid bearing an additional 13-hydroxy substituent. It has a role as a metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a dihydroxybenzoic acid that is 1,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid in which the hydrogen at position 2 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a dihydroxybenzoic acid and a member of naphthols.

The molecule is a member of the class of protoporphyrins that is 7,15-bis(methoxycarbonyl)protoporphyrin in which all four pyrrole hydrogens are replaced by vinyl groups. It has a role as an epitope and a photosensitizing agent. It derives from a protoporphyrin.

The molecule is a sphingoid that is the C17 analogue of sphingosine. It has a role as an EC 2.4.1.80 (ceramide kinase) inhibitor, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a sphingosine. It is a conjugate base of a tetradecasphingosine(1+).

The molecule is an omega-hydroxy fatty acid ascaroside obtained by formal condensation of the alcoholic hydroxy group of (2E)-13-hydroxytetradec-2-enoic acid with ascarylopyranose (the alpha anomer). It is a metabolite of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. It has a role as a Caenorhabditis elegans metabolite. It is an alpha,beta-unsaturated monocarboxylic acid and an omega-hydroxy fatty acid ascaroside. It derives from a (2E)-13-hydroxytetradec-2-enoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of an oscr#26(1-).

The molecule is a homodetic cyclic peptide composed of L-threonine, L-valine and two 2,8-didehydro-3E,6S-epoxyisoquinovinyl residues joined in sequence. Isolated from the marine cyanobacterium Oscillatoria sp. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an animal metabolite and a bacterial metabolite. It is a homodetic cyclic peptide and a macrocycle.

The molecule is a cyclic tetrapyrrole anion obtained by deprotonation of the four carboxy groups of coproporphyrin III. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a coproporphyrin III.
The molecule is a quaternary ammonium ion obtained by methylation of the tertiary amino group of (S)-glaucine. It derives from a glaucine.

The molecule is an amino disaccharide consisting of 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-alpha-D-galactopyranose and 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-beta-D-glucopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1->3) glycosidic bond. It is an amino disaccharide, a member of acetamides and a glycosylglucose derivative.
The molecule is a phytoceramide in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as 2-hydroxyhexacosanoyl. It has a role as an Arabidopsis thaliana metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is an N-acyl-L-alpha-amino acid anion that is the conjugate base of N-arachidonoyl-L-serine, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an arachidonate and a L-serinate. It is a conjugate base of a N-arachidonoyl-L-serine.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid anion that results from the deprotonation of both carboxy groups and protonation of the amino group of nocardicin E. The major species at pH 7.3 It derives from a D-gamma-glutamyl residue. It is a conjugate base of a nocardicin E.

The molecule is a stilbenoid that consists of trans-resveratrol substituted at position 3 by a beta-D-glucosyl residue. It has a role as a metabolite and an antioxidant. It is a polyphenol, a stilbenoid, a beta-D-glucoside and a monosaccharide derivative. It derives from a trans-resveratrol.
The molecule is a but-2-enoic acid having the double bond at position 3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a conjugate acid of a crotonate.

The molecule is a nucleotide-sugar oxoanion that is the conjugate base of CMP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy and phosphate groups; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a muramate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a CMP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine.

The molecule is a trihydroxyicosatrienoic acid that consists of (5Z,8Z,14E)-icosa-5,9,14-trienoic acid bearing three hydroxy substituents at positions 11, 12 and 13. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid anion resulting from the deprotonation of the carboxy group of gibberellin A17. The major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a human metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a gibberellin A17.

The molecule is a member of the class of phenylureas that is urea in which one hydrogen attached to each nitrogen has been replaced by an N-phenylpropanimidoyl group. It is a member of monochlorobenzenes, a secondary carboxamide and a member of phenylureas.

The molecule is an ammonium ion that is the conjugate acid of 6-aminohexanoic acid, arising from protonation of the primary amino group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a hexanoate. It is a conjugate acid of a 6-aminohexanoic acid.
The molecule is an acyl-CoA oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of (R)-carnitinyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a carnitoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is a formate ester resulting from the formal condensation of formic acid with butan-1-ol. It has been isolated from plants like Piper sanguineispicum and Cassia siamea. It has a role as an antifungal agent, a plant metabolite and an insect attractant.

The molecule is an organosulfonate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the sulfonic acid group of 2-amino-5-[(4-methoxybenzyl)diazenyl]-3-methylbenzene-1-sulfonic acid. It is a conjugate base of a 2-amino-5-[(4-methoxybenzyl)diazenyl]-3-methylbenzene-1-sulfonic acid.

The molecule is a diterpenoid that is (2E,6Z)-farnesol hydroxylated at positions 8 and 15. It has been isolated from the rhizomes of Curcuma kwangsiensis. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, a plant metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a diterpenoid, a polyprenol and a primary alcohol.

The molecule is a piperidinium ion that has 4-[2-(carboxymethyl)aminoethyl]phenyl as the N-alkyl group and which is substituted on the piperidine nitrogen by a methyl group and a pimelyl group. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a phenoxyacetate ester obtained by the formal condensation of hydroxy group of 2-(hydroxymethyl)propane-1,3-diol with the carboxy group of syringic acid. It has been isolated from Taxus yunnanensis. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is a member of methoxybenzenes, a primary alcohol and a phenoxyacetate ester. It derives from a syringic acid.

The molecule is an organic cation that is 7-(4-anilinonaphthalen-1-yl)-5,6-dimethylquinolin-8-ium substituted by a phenylamino group at position 3. The chloride salt is the histological dye 'methyl green B'
The molecule is a butan-4-olide having a methyl substituent at the 2-position. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a glucosiduronic acid that consists of beta-D-glucuronic acid having a trans-4-coumaroyl group attached at the 3-position. It has a role as an Arabidopsis thaliana metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a trans-4-coumaric acid.

The molecule is a C-glycosyl compound that consists of 1,3,6-trihydroxy-2-methoxybenzene substituted by a beta-D-glucopyranosyloxy residue at position 7 and a trans-4,5-dimethoxycinnamoyl group at position 8. Isolated from the leaves of Myrcia multiflora, it exhibits antihyperglycemic activity. It has a role as an EC 3.2.1.20 (alpha-glucosidase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a cinnamate ester, a dihydroxyflavone, a monomethoxyflavone, a C-glycosyl compound and a polyphenol.
The molecule is a triterpene that is (1S,2E)-geranylgeraniol carrying an additional methyl substituent at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite.

The molecule is a beta-D-galactosyl-N-acylsphingosine in which the acyl group specified is tetracosanoyl. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and a rat metabolite. It derives from a tetracosanoic acid.

The molecule is a biladiene that consists of 1,2-dihydrophenazine substituted by methyl groups at positions 5 and 7, an oxo group at position 6, vinyl groups at positions 3 and 8 and two carboxyethyl groups at positions 4 and 9. It has a role as a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a 7-methylguanine in which the hydrogen at position N(2) has been replaced by an amino group. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is a cytochalasan alkaloid found in Chaetomium globosum. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a Chaetomium metabolite. It is a cytochalasan alkaloid, a member of indoles, a macrocycle and a secondary alpha-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is a member of the class of triazoles that is 1H-triazole carrying amino and 2,3-dichlorophenyl substituents at positions 4 and 5 respectively. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.2 (non-specific serine/threonine protein kinase) inhibitor. It is a dichlorobenzene, a secondary amino compound and a member of triazoles.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of 3-methylhistidine; major species at pH 7.3 It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a tautomer of a 3-methylhistidine.

The molecule is an L-polyhomomethionine zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tetrahomomethionine; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is a tautomer of a L-tetrahomomethionine.

The molecule is an organic sodium salt that is the monosodium salt of globostellatic acid A. Isolated from the marine sponge Stelletta globostellata, it exhibits cytotoxicity against P-388 murine leukemia cells. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It contains a globostellatate B(1-).

The molecule is a dimethoxybenzene that is 1,3-dimethoxybenzene substituted by a hydroxymethyl group at position 4. It has been isolated from the stems of Combretum quadrangulare and exhibits cytotoxicity against human oral epidermoid carcinoma. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a hexadecenoate that is the conjugate base of palmitoleic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid group. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a palmitoleate. It is a conjugate base of a palmitoleic acid.

The molecule is an organic heterotetracyclic compound that is 1H,6H-pyrano[4,3-c]isochromene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 5 and 8, a methoxy group at position 7, a methylenedioxy moiety across positions 9 and 10, a prenyl group at position 2 and an oxo group at position 6. Isolated from the culture broth of Penicillium commune, it exhibits antibacterial activity. It has a role as a metabolite, an antimicrobial agent and an EC 1.14.13.39 (nitric oxide synthase) inhibitor. It is an organic heterotetracyclic compound, an enone, an aromatic ether, a member of phenols, a cyclic ketone and a polyketide.

The molecule is a benzoic acid that consists of 5-aminosalicylic acid bearing an additional phenyl substituent at position 2 and in which the phenolic hydroxy group has been converted into its p-(butylamino)phenyl ether. It is a sulfonamide, a member of benzoic acids and an aromatic ether.
The molecule is an acyl-CoA(4-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate groups of oscr#36-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of an oscr#36-CoA.
The molecule is a ketoaldonic acid that is L-gulonic acid in which the hydroxy group at position 6 has been oxidised to the corresponding ketone. It derives from a L-gulonic acid.
The molecule is a tRNA oligonucleotide comprised of one inosine, two cytidine, one guanosine and three uridine residues connected by 3'->5' phosphodiester linkages in the sequence C-U-G-C-I-C-m(1)I.

The molecule is a quinoline N-oxide that is 1-hydroxyquinoline which is substituted at position 2 by a geranyl group and at positions 3,4 by methyl groups. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzylamines that is 2-aminobiphenyl substituted by an aminomethyl group at position N-1. It has a role as a xenobiotic metabolite and a human urinary metabolite.

The molecule is a tetrol that is propane-1,2,3-triol in which the pro-R hydrogens at positions 2 and 3 are substituted by hydroxy groups while one of the anti-R hydrogens is substituted by methyl. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, a plant metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite.
The molecule is a benzoate ester that is beta-D-glucopyranose in which the anomeric hydroxy hydrogen has been replaced by a benzoyl group. It derives from a salicylic acid and a beta-D-glucose.

The molecule is a branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of an alpha-D-mannose residue, two beta-D-mannose residues and an N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine residue linked sequentially (1->6), (1->4) and (1->4), to the mannose residue nearest to the reducing end are also linked (1->3) and (1->2) respectively a beta-D-galactose residue and an alpha-L-fucose residue. It has a role as an epitope. It is an amino sugar, an amino pentasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is an anthracycline that consists of a tetracene skeleton carrying hydroxy, methyl and oxo substituents at positions 1, 3, 4 and 9 respectively; substituted by a beta-D-glucosyl residue at position 8 via a glycosidic linkage, a 2,6-dideoxy-L-mannosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-ribofuranosyl moiety at position 7 via a glycosidic linkage and a methoxycarbonyl group at position 13. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a metabolite and an antimicrobial agent. It is an aminoglycoside antibiotic, a disaccharide derivative, a member of tetracenes, a polyketide, a methyl ester, a tertiary alcohol and an anthracycline antibiotic.

The molecule is a tetrachlorobiphenyl that is biphenyl in which the hydrogens at positions 2, 3, and 4' have been replaced by chlorines. It has a role as an environmental contaminant and a persistent organic pollutant.

The molecule is a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid with formula C21H24N2O3, originallly isolated from the seeds of Strychnos nux-vomica. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antiplasmodial drug. It is a delta-lactam, a cyclic ketone, a tertiary amino compound, a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid, an organic heterohexacyclic compound and a primary alcohol.
The molecule is a 1-(3-pyridyl)piperidinium that has S configuration. It is the major species at pH 7.3. It is an enantiomer of a (R)-nicotine.

The molecule is a benzenedicarboxamide compound having iodo substituents in the 2-, 3- and 6-positions, an N-(bis)[2-hydroxypropyl]glycinamido group at the 4-position and two methyl groups attached to the nitrogen. It has a role as a radioopaque medium, a radioopaque media substrate and a radioopaque contrast agent.

The molecule is an aminopyrimidine that is 2,4-diaminopyrimidin-5(4H)-one in which the hydrogen attached to the nitrogen at position 6 has been replaced by a p-[3'-(1-methylpiperazin-1-yl)phenyl]amino group while one of the hydrogens attached to the amino group at position 4 has been replaced by a 3,4-dimethoxyphenyl group. It is an inhibitor of the tyrosine kinase domain of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 and 2. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor. It is an aminopyrimidine, a N-arylpiperazine, a secondary carboxamide, a dimethoxybenzene and a tertiary amino compound.

The molecule is a succinate salt obtained by combining equimolar amounts of sulpiride and succinic acid. A dopamine D2 receptor antagonist, it is used as an antidyskinesia agent in the treatment of Parkinson's disease. It has a role as an antiparkinson drug, a dopaminergic antagonist and a second generation antipsychotic. It contains a sulpiride(1+).
The molecule is a peptide cation obtained from the deprotonation of the carboxy group and protonation of the amino group of neosaragmin I (1-). It is a conjugate acid of a neosaragmin I (1-).
The molecule is a cyclic ketone that consists of cyclohexane bearing an oxo substituent. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a mouse metabolite.
The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the tertiary amino function of thioperazine. It is a conjugate acid of a thioperazine.
The molecule is a hydroxy fatty acid that is the 3-hydroxy derivative of capric acid. It has a role as an animal metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a decanoic acid.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid that is urs-12-ene substituted by an oxo group at position 3, hydroxy groups at positions 2 and 28, methyl groups at positions 6, 9, 12, 14a and 20 and a carboxy group at position 23. Isolated from the leaves of Rosa laevigata, it exhibits inhibitory activity against alpha-glucosidase and aldose reductase. It has a role as a metabolite, an EC 3.2.1.20 (alpha-amylase) inhibitor and an EC 1.1.1.21 (aldehyde reductase) inhibitor. It is a dihydroxy monocarboxylic acid, a pentacyclic triterpenoid, a triol and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone.

The molecule is the D-enantiomer of pipecolic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a conjugate base of a D-pipecolate. It is a conjugate acid of a D-piperonate. It is an enantiomer of a L-pipecolic acid.

The molecule is a triterpenoid saponin isolated from the roots of of the Madagascan plant Albizia gummifera and has been shown to exhibit cytotoxic activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It derives from a hydride of an oleanane.

The molecule is dizwitterionic form of cysteine having both carboxy groups in anionic form and both amino groups protonated. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a tautomer of a cysteine.

The molecule is a steroid glucuronide anion that is the conjugate base of 2-methoxyestrone 3-O-(beta-D-glucuronide) arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid function; major species at pH 7.3. It is a beta-D-glucosiduronate, an organic molecular entity and a monocarboxylic acid anion. It derives from a 17-oxo-3-ethoxyestradiol. It is a conjugate base of a 2-methoxyestrone 3-O-(beta-D-glucuronide).

The molecule is a nucleotide-sugar oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the diphosphate OH groups of CDP-beta-D-glucose; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from an UDP-alpha-D-glucose(2-). It is a conjugate base of a CDP-beta-D-glucose.

The molecule is an optically active form of glutamic acid having L-configuration. It has a role as a nutraceutical, a micronutrient, a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a glutamine family amino acid, a proteinogenic amino acid, a glutamic acid and a L-alpha-amino acid. It is a conjugate acid of a L-glutamate(1-). It is an enantiomer of a D-glutamic acid.
The molecule is a 3,5-dimethyltyrosine in which the two methyl groups at positions 2 and 4 both have S configuration. It derives from a D-tyrosine.

The molecule is a purine ribonucleoside 2'-diphosphate having guanine as the nucleobase. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a GDP. It is a conjugate acid of a guanosine 2'-diphosphate(3-).

The molecule is a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate that is the S-(2R)-4-thia-bicyclo[3.2.1]octane-2-carbonyl ester derivative of AMP. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from an adenosine 5'-monophosphate and a (R)-lipoic acid.

The molecule is an omega-hydroxy fatty acid ascaroside obtained by formal condensation of the alcoholic hydroxy group of 17-hydroxymargaric acid with ascarylopyranose (the alpha anomer). It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It derives from a 17-hydroxylauric acid.

The molecule is a diterpene that consists of (1S,5R)-2,4,7,8,10,13,13a-octahydronaphtho[2,1-b]furan substituted by methyl groups at positions 6, 9 and 13 as well as an isoprenoid group at position 1. It has been isolated from the Hainan soft coral Lobophytum cristatum. It has a role as a coral metabolite. It is a diterpene, a carbobicyclic compound and an olefinic compound.

The molecule is a withanolide that consists of 5beta,6beta:22alpha,26-diepoxyergosta-7,24-diene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3, 12 and 26. Isolated from Paraminabea acronocephala, it exhibits antineoplastic activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a metabolite and a coral metabolite.

The molecule is a hydrate that is the hexahydrate form of magnesium ammonium phosphate. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It contains a magnesium ammonium phosphate (anhydrous).
The molecule is a 4-alkylaldehyde that is pentanal substituted by an ethyl group at position 4. It has a role as a human metabolite and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is an organic heterooctacyclic compound that is 17-oxohepta[c]pyrrolo[2,3,4-ij]quinoline substituted by hydroxy group at position 8, geminal methyl groups at positions 6 and a (2S)-2-methylbut-3-en-2-yl group at position 5. Isolated from the culture broth of Streptomyces sp. E-1609, it exhibits cytotoxicity against human oral epidermoid carcinoma. It has a role as a metabolite and an antineoplastic agent. It is an organic heterooctacyclic compound, a delta-lactam, a tertiary alcohol, a cyclic ketone, an enone, an aromatic ether, a lactam and an alkaloid.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of 2-methylleucine; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a Daphnia magna metabolite. It derives from a leucine. It is a tautomer of a 2-methylleucine.

The molecule is a cationic sphingoid that is the conjugate acid of D-glucosylsphingosine, obtained by protonation of the primary amino function; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a sphingosine(1+).

The molecule is a prostaglandin carboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 19-hydroxyprostaglandin F2alpha, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a prostaglandin F2alpha(1-). It is a conjugate base of a 19-hydroxyprostaglandin F2alpha.

The molecule is an epoxy(hydroxy)octadecenoic acid that is 9Z-18:1 in which the epoxy group is located across positions 10 and 12 and the hydroxy substituent is located at position 13. It derives from a gamma-linolenic acid.

The molecule is a tetrapeptide composed of L-lysine, L-threonine and two L-tyrosine units joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-lysine, a L-threonine and a L-tyrosine.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation between the carboxy group of (2S)-2-cyano-3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid and the amino group of (1R)-2,4-dichlorobenzylamine. It has a role as an EC 6.4.1.2 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase) inhibitor. It is a monocarboxylic acid amide, a nitrile, a dichlorobenzene and a secondary carboxamide.
The molecule is an amidobenzoic acid that consists of anthranilic acid bearing a N-acetyl substituent. It has a role as a metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from an anthranilic acid.

The molecule is a 3-hydroxy fatty acyl CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of 3-hydroxytetracosanoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3 It derives from a tricosanoyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a 3-hydroxytetracosanoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a hydroperoxy fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 13-HPODE, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an octadecanoid(1-). It is a conjugate base of a 13-HPODE.

The molecule is a trans-2,3-didehydroacyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of trans-tetradec-2-enoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It is a monounsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) and a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a trans-tetradec-2-enoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a fluoroalkane that is decalin in which all of the hydrogens have been replaced by fluorines. It has a role as an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic. It derives from a hydride of a decalin.

The molecule is an indolocarbazole alkaloid that is 1,3-dihydro-2H-indolizino[5,6-b]carbazol-2-one substituted by a beta-D-glucopyranosyl moiety at position 9 via a glycosidic linkage and chloro groups at positions 8 and 10. It has been isolated from the culture of the fungus Aspergillus niger. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and an Aspergillus metabolite. It is an indolocarbazole alkaloid, an organochlorine compound and a N-glycosyl compound.

The molecule is a gamma-glutamylamino acid that is the N(2)-L-gamma-D-glutamyl derivative of L-isoleucine. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a (S)-2-methylbutyric acid and a L-isoleucine.
The molecule is a tetracyclic triterpenoid that is dammarane which has been substituted by hydroxy groups at the 3beta, 12alpha, and 20 positions. It derives from a hydride of a dammarane.

The molecule is a dihydroxyanthraquinone that is anthracene-9,10-dione substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 2 and 3 and a methyl group at position 4. It has been isolated from the roots of Rubia yunnanensis. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a member of the class of aminopyrimidines that is 2,6-diamino-5-chloropyrimidine in which one of the amino groups has been acylated by an isopropyl and N'-ethylcarbamimidamido group. It is used as its hydrochloride salt for treatment of malaria. It has a role as an antimalarial. It is an organochlorine compound, an aminopyrimidine, a carboxamidine and a tertiary amino compound.

The molecule is a member of the class of catechols that is tyramine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the amino group has been replaced by an acetyl group. It has a role as a human urinary metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a N-acetyltyramine.

The molecule is a form of folate that consists of 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolic acid bearing an N(6)-formyl substituent. It has a role as a mouse metabolite and a rat metabolite. It derives from a folic acid.

The molecule is an organic sodium salt that is the disodium salt of 7-hydroxy-8-{[(phenyldiazenyl)methyl]sulfonyl}naphthalene-1,3-disulfonic acid. It has a role as a histological dye and a fluorochrome. It contains a 4-amino-5-hydroxynaphthalenesulfonate.

The molecule is a diterpenoid of the class of daphnane-type terpenoids isolated from the bark of Fraxinus sieboldiana. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a plant metabolite. It is a carbotricyclic compound, a cyclic ether, a member of phenols, a monocarboxylic acid and a diterpenoid.

The molecule is a tetrapeptide composed of methyl 5-oxohexanoate, L-alanyl, L-valyl and N(alpha)-chloromethyl-L-alanyl residues joined in sequence. It has a role as an EC 3.4.21.26 (prolyl oligopeptidase) inhibitor. It derives from a methyl 5-oxohexanoate.

The molecule is a 1,3-thiazole that is thiazolidine which is substituted at positions 2 and 4 by benzoyl and 2-hydroxyphenyl groups respectively. It has a role as an EC 6.5.1.1 (methionine gamma-lyase) inhibitor. It is a member of phenols, a monocarboxylic acid and a member of 1,3-thiazoles.

The molecule is an amino pentasaccharide consisting of five 2-O-methyl-L-threo-hexopyranuronosyl residues and one 3,6-dideoxy-3-(methoxyimino)-alpha-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid residue linked in a linear sequence. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a hydroxy fatty acid ascaroside anion that is the conjugate base of oscr#3, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of an oscr#3.

The molecule is a C80 alpha-mycolate having a C54 meromycolic chain with two cis cyclopropyl functions and a saturated C26 alpha-branch. It is produced by Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Ra. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite. It is an an alpha-mycolate and a hydroxy fatty acid anion. It is a conjugate base of a (2R)-2-[(1R)-1-hydroxy-18-{2-[10-(2-octadecylcyclopropyl)decyl]cyclopropyl}octadecyl]hexacosanoic acid.
The molecule is an O-acylcarnitine having malonyl as the acyl substituent. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a malonic acid.

The molecule is a dihydroxybenzoate that is the conjugate base of 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from a benzoate. It is a conjugate base of a 3,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid.

The molecule is a ginsenoside found in Panax ginseng and Panax japonicus var. major that is dammarane which is substituted by hydroxy groups at the 3beta, 6alpha, 12beta and 20 pro-S positions, in which the hydroxy group at position 6 has been converted to its beta-D-glucopyranoside, and in which a double bond has been introduced at the 24-25 position. It has a role as an apoptosis inducer, an antioxidant, a neuroprotective agent, a plant metabolite, an anti-inflammatory drug, an antineoplastic agent, a cardioprotective agent, a hepatoprotective agent, a hypoglycemic agent, an EC 3.6.3.9 (Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase) inhibitor, an anticoronaviral agent and an antiviral agent. It is a 12beta-hydroxy steroid, a beta-D-glucoside, a disaccharide derivative, a ginsenoside, a tetracyclic triterpenoid and a 3beta-hydroxy-4,4-dimethylsteroid.

The molecule is an L-methionine derivative that is the ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-methionine with the 3'-hydroxy group of AMP. It has a role as a Mycoplasma genitalium metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is an adenosine 5'-phosphate, a L-methionine derivative, an alpha-amino acid ester and a purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate. It derives from an adenosine 5'-monophosphate.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the secondary amino function of (S,R)-nebivolol. It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation. It is a conjugate acid of a (S,R)-nebivolol. It is an enantiomer of a (R,S)-nebivolol(1+).

The molecule is a monocyclic ketone that consists of furan bearing an oxo substituent at position 3. It has a role as a metabolite and an Escherichia coli metabolite. It is a member of furans, a cyclic ketone and a heteroaryl hydroxy compound.

The molecule is trianion of 2-phospho-5-(2-carboxyethylideneamino)-3-thiolactaldehyde arising from deprotonation of carboxylic acid and phosphate functions. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a human metabolite. It is an organophosphate oxoanion and a monocarboxylic acid anion.
