The molecule is a phytoceramide in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as octadecanoyl (stearoyl). It has a role as an EC 3.6.3.9 (Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase) inhibitor, a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite.

The molecule is a dihydroagarofuran sesquiterpenoid that consists of dihydro-beta-agarofuran substituted by acetoxy groups at positions 1 and 6, benzoyloxy groups at positions 2 and 9 and methyl groups at positions 4a and 8 (the 1beta,4alpha,5alpha,6alpha stereoisomer). Isolated from Celastrus orbiculatus, it exhibits inhibitory activity against acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase 2. It has a role as an EC 2.3.1.26 (sterol O-acyltransferase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is an acetate ester, a bridged compound, a benzoate ester, a cyclic ether, a dihydroagarofuran sesquiterpenoid and an organic heterotricyclic compound.

The molecule is a sphingoid obtained by formal oxidation of the 3-hydroxy group and reduction of the carboxy function of C20 sphingosine. It has a role as an EC 1.4.3.4 (monoamine oxidase) inhibitor, a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a C20 sphingosine.
The molecule is a sphingomyelin d18:1 in which the N-acyl group and sphingoid base are specified as hexadecanoyl (palmitoyl) and sphingosine respectively. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a synthetic 19-membered cyclodepsipeptide that is isolated from the fermentation broth of Streptomyces sp.MK732-AF486 and exhibits potent antitumour activity against several human tumour cell lines. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antineoplastic agent and a bacterial metabolite. It is a macrocycle, a member of formamides, a heterodetic cyclic peptide, a cyclodepsipeptide and an organobromine compound.

The molecule is a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid with formula C23H29NO5, originally isolated from the seeds of Strychnos nux-vomica. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antifeedant. It is a delta-lactam, a tertiary amino compound, a secondary alcohol, a methyl ester, a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid, an organic heteropentacyclic compound and an aromatic ether.
The molecule is a dipeptide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-asparagine with the amino group of L-tyrosine. It derives from a L-asparagine and a L-tyrosine.

The molecule is a branched amino oligosaccharide that is an undecasaccharide derivative in which two pentasaccharide branches, each formed from beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannose and beta-D-galactosyl-(1->3)-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannose units linked (1->3) and (1->6) respectively, are linked (1->3) and (1->6) to the mannose residue of a trisaccharide chain consisting of mannose residues all linked beta(1->4) with an N-acetylglucosamine residue at the reducing end. It has a role as an epitope. It is an amino oligosaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a C-glycosyl compound that consists of apigenin substituted by beta-D-glucopyranosyl and alpha-L-arabinofuranosyl residues at positions 6 and 8 respectively. It has been isolated from the leaves of Mimosa diplotricha. It has a role as an antiplasmodial drug, a metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a trihydroxyflavone and a C-glycosyl compound.

The molecule is a limonoid that is the 1,2-diacetyl derivative of trichagmalin C. It has been isolated from Trichilia connaroides. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an acetate ester, a bridged compound, a member of furans, a limonoid, a methyl ester and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone. It derives from a tiglic acid and a trichagmalin C.

The molecule is a member of the class of imidazolones that is 1,5-dihydroimidazol-4-one which is substituted at positions 2 and 5 by methyl groups, at position 3 by an isopropyl group, and at position 6 by a (2-methoxy-2-methylbenzoyl)nitrilo group. It has a role as a herbicide, an environmental contaminant and a xenobiotic. It is a member of benzoic acids, a member of benzamides, a methyl ester and a member of imidazolones.

The molecule is a 3beta-hydroxy steroid that consists of androsta-1,4-diene bearing three hydroxy substituents at positions 3beta, 8alpha and 17. It has a role as an androgen, a human metabolite, a Daphnia magna metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a 3beta-hydroxy steroid, a 17alpha-hydroxy steroid, an androstanoid and a C21-steroid.

The molecule is a member of the class of quinazolines that is 1-methylquinazoline which is substituted at positions 2, 3 and 6 by p-chlorobenzamido, bromoamino and (2-hydroxyethoxy)nitrilo groups respectively. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.2 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor. It is a member of quinazolines, a secondary amino compound, a hydroxamic acid ester, an organofluorine compound, a member of monochlorobenzenes and a member of bromobenzenes.

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the tertiary amino function of N-octanoyl-(1R,2S)-2-(3,4-methylenedioxyphenyl)cyclopropanecarboxamide. It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation. It is a conjugate acid of a N-octanoyl-(1R,2S)-2-(3,4-methylenedioxyphenyl)cyclopropanecarboxamide.

The molecule is a pentacyclic triterpenoid with formula C30H42O5, originally isolated from Tripterygium hypoglaucum. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent and a plant metabolite. It is a pentacyclic triterpenoid, a monocarboxylic acid and a member of catechols.

The molecule is a cinnamate ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of trans-ferulic acid with the 5-hydroxy group of quinic acid. It has a role as an antioxidant and a plant metabolite. It derives from a ferulic acid and a quinic acid.

The molecule is a dicarboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of 4-hydroxy-2,5-dioxopentanedioic acid; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a human metabolite. It derives from a valerate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a 4-hydroxy-2,5-dioxopentanedioic acid.

The molecule is a tricarboxylic acid that consists of succinic acid bearing three additional methyl substituents at positions 2,3 and 4. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a succinic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a homoisocitrate(3-).

The molecule is a monohydroxyquinoline that is quinoline substituted by a hydroxy group at position 6. It has been isolated from the bark of Cryptocarya chartacea and exhibits inhibitory activity against HIV-1 integrase. It has a role as an anti-HIV agent, a plant metabolite and an EC 5.99.1.3 [DNA topoisomerase (ATP-hydrolysing)] inhibitor.
The molecule is a ceramide phosphoethanolamine (35:1) in which the acyl and sphingoid base specified are icosanoyl and sphingosine respectively. It derives from an icosanoic acid.

The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and phospho group of 4-nitrophenyl phosphate. It derives from a phenyl phosphate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a 4-nitrophenyl phosphate.

The molecule is a polycyclic cage that consists of hexacyclic fused-ring system bearing hydroxy, methoxy and 2-[(3S)-5-hydroxy-1-methylpyrrolidin-3-yl]carbonyl substituents. It has been isolated from Streptomyces sp. TC-0378. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an antineoplastic agent, a bacterial metabolite and a marine metabolite. It is a cyclic ether, a cyclic ketone, a polycyclic cage, a member of resorcinols, a monocarboxylic acid amide, a methyl ester and a tertiary alcohol.

The molecule is zwitterionic form of (2S,3R)-3-hydroxy-L-leucine having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite. It is a tautomer of a (2S,3R)-3-hydroxy-L-leucine.

The molecule is a quercetin O-glucoside that consists of quercetin attached to beta-D-glucopyranosyl residues at positions 3 and 7 respectively via glycosidic linkages and a alpha-L-[6''-p-coumaroyl-beta-D-xylopyranosyl-(1->2)]-rhamnopyranosyl residue at position 4' via a glycosidic linkage. Isolated from the aerial parts of Delphinium staphisagria, it exhibits trypanocidal activity. It has a role as a metabolite and a trypanocidal drug. It is an alpha-L-rhamnoside, a cinnamate ester, a disaccharide derivative, a trihydroxyflavone and a quercetin O-glucoside.
The molecule is a dipeptide formed from L-serine and L-proline residues. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-serine and a L-proline.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that consists of propionic acid bearing cyclopropyl and (2E)-3-[4-(7-chloroquinolin-6-yl)buta-1,3-dien-1-yl]phenyl substituents at position 3 as well as a {2-[(1S)-1-hydroxy-2-methylpropyl]cyclopropyl}sulfanyl group at position 2. It has a role as an antiglaucoma drug, an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor and an antineoplastic agent. It is a member of quinolines, a monocarboxylic acid, a sulfoxide, a tertiary alcohol, a secondary alcohol, a cyclic ether and a chloronaphthalene.

The molecule is a glycosylgalactose consisting of alpha-D-glucopyranose and D-galactopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1->4) glycosidic bond. It derives from an alpha-D-glucose and a beta-D-galactose.

The molecule is an amino disaccharide that consists of N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosamine having a 6-O-sulfo-beta-D-galactosyl residue attached at position 4. It has a role as an epitope and an antigen. It is an oligosaccharide sulfate, an amino disaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a trans,trans-2,3,4,5-tetradehydroacyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of (2E,4Z)-deca-2,4-dienoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It is an acyl-CoA(4-) and a medium-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a (2E,4Z)-deca-2,4-dienoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2-(3-ethoxy-4-hydroxyphenyl)hexadecanoic acid with the amino group of 3-chloro-4-(trifluoromethyl)aniline. It has a role as an EC 1.6.5.2 [monoamine oxidase (H(2)O(2) oxidizing)] inhibitor and an antiparkinson drug. It is a member of monochlorobenzenes, a monocarboxylic acid amide, an aromatic ether, a secondary carboxamide and a member of (trifluoromethyl)benzenes.

The molecule is a cyclohexenecarbaldehyde that is cyclohex-1-ene-1-carbaldehyde substituted by a hydroxy group at position 5. It has been isolated from the essential oils of Pimpinella anisum and Zingiber officinale. It has a role as an antifeedant, a plant metabolite and an insect attractant.

The molecule is dianion of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine 1-phosphate arising from deprotonation of both OH groups of the phosphate. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It is an organophosphate oxoanion and a monosaccharide 1-phosphate(2-). It derives from a D-glucopyranose 6-phosphate(2-).

The molecule is a member of the class of naphthoquinones that is 1,4-naphthoquinone in which one hydrogen at position 2 and one hydrogen attached to the carbon bearing the oxo group are replaced by methyl groups while a sulfonic acid group is attached to the other carbon. It has a role as an EC 3.6.3.9 (Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase) inhibitor. It is a member of 1,4-naphthoquinones, a sulfone and a cyclic ketone.

The molecule is a member of the class of 2-pyranones that is 5,6-dihydro-2H-pyran-2-one substituted by a hydroxy group at position 4 and a (3R,5S,6R,7R,8S)-3,5,6,7,8-pentahydroxytridecyl moiety at position 6. It has been isolated from Cryptocarya species. It has a role as a metabolite and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is an amino oligosaccharide that is a tridecasaccharide derivative in which two pentasaccharide branches, each formed from alpha-L-fucosyl-(1->2)-beta-D-galactosyl-(1->3)-N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannose, are linked (1->3) and (1->6) to the mannose residue of a trisaccharide chain consisting of mannose and two N-acetylglucosamine residues all linked beta(1->4) with a beta-configuration of the anomeric carbon of the N-acetylglucosamine residue at the reducing end. It has a role as an epitope. It is an amino oligosaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a bisindole alkaloid that is isolated from the marine sponge Plakinastrella clathrata and exhibits anti-HIV activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a metabolite and an anti-HIV-1 agent.

The molecule is a chlorocarboxylic acid that is acrylic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 3 has been replaced by chlorine. It has a role as an EC 4.2.1.50 (prolyl oligopeptidase) inhibitor, a human xenobiotic metabolite and a bacterial xenobiotic metabolite. It is a chlorocarboxylic acid and an alpha,beta-unsaturated monocarboxylic acid.

The molecule is an alicyclic ketone that consists of cyclohexanone bearing a 2-methylthiophenoyl substituent at position 5. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a volatile oil component. It is a member of thiophenes, an alicyclic ketone and an olefinic compound.

The molecule is a member of the class of 1,3-oxazoles that is 5-(4-isopropylphenyl)-2-{[4-(morpholin-4-ylmethyl)phenyl]carbamoyl}oxazole carrying additional hydroxy and 2,4-dihydroxy-6-(propan-2-yl)phenyl substituents at positions 4 and 7 respectively. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, a vascular endothelial growth factor receptor antagonist and an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor. It is a member of 1,3-oxazoles, a member of morpholines, a secondary amino compound, a tertiary carboxamide, a member of resorcinols and a dihydroxybenzene.

The molecule is a bile acid glycine conjugate in which the glycoxy group at position 3 has been esterified with one of the carboxy groups of acetic acid. It derives from an allocholic acid and an acetic acid.
The molecule is an epsilon-amino acid that is butyric acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 4 has been replaced by an amino group. It derives from a butyric acid.

The molecule is a 3',5'-cyclic purine nucleotide(1-) that results from the removal of a proton from the phosphate group of 3',5'-cyclic GMP; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as a human metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a 3',5'-cyclic GMP(1-). It is a conjugate base of a 3',5'-cyclic GMP.

The molecule is a branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of D-galactose at the reducing end with an alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->3)-[beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)]-N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-(1->2)-alpha-D-mannosyl moiety attached at the 3-position. It has a role as an epitope.
The molecule is a tripeptide composed of L-alanine, glycine and L-tyrosine joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite.

The molecule is a twelve-membered branched glucosamine oligosaccharide made up from four glucose, two Kdo and two glucosamine residues with the central one being phosphorylated at position 7. Corresponds to the core oligosaccharide of Neisseria meningitidis. It is an amino octasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a branched amino nonasaccharide comprised of an alpha-D-mannosyl residue, two N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl residues, three beta-D-galactose residues and one N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosamine residue linked sequentially (1->6), (1->4), (1->3), (1->3), (1->4) and (1->4), to the beta-D-galactose residue nearest to the reducing end are also linked (1->2) and (1->3) respectively an alpha-L-fucosyl residue and an N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-(1->2)-[N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminyl-(1->3)]-alpha-D-mannosyl tetrasaccharide unit. It has a role as an epitope. It is an amino nonasaccharide and a glucosamine oligosaccharide.

The molecule is a steroid sulfate that is (24S)-24-hydroxycholesterol in which all four hydroxy hydrogens have been replaced by sulfo groups. It has a role as a human xenobiotic metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a (24S)-24-hydroxycholesterol.
The molecule is a UDP-D-galactofuranose in which the anomeric centre of the galactofuranose fragment has alpha-configuration. It is a conjugate acid of an UDP-alpha-D-galactofuranose(2-).

The molecule is a 2-acyl-1-alkyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine in which the alkyl and the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as hexadecyl and butanoyl respectively. It has a role as an epitope. It derives from a butyric acid.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid that consists of 5-(4-hydroxyphenyl)pentanoic acid in which one of the hydrogens at position 2 has been replaced by a 3,3-dimethyloxiran-2-yl group. It is an ether, an oxirane and a monocarboxylic acid.
The molecule is a fluoride salt with K(+) as the counterion. It has a role as an EC 1.8.1.12 (citrate synthase) inhibitor, a food acidity regulator and a poison. It contains a potassium.
The molecule is an N-acyl-L-homoserine resulting from the formal condensation of hexanoic acid (caproic acid) with amino group of L-homoserine. It derives from a hexanoic acid.
The molecule is a 2-hydroxymyristic acid in which the chiral centre has S configuration. It is a conjugate acid of a (S)-2-hydroxyoctanoate.

The molecule is a secondary amino compound that is N-hydroxyacetamide in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen has been replaced by a 2-{[(1E)-3-methyl-1H-indol-2-yl]methyl}ethyl group. It is an inhibitor of histone deacetylase and induces apoptosis in human cancer cells. It has a role as an EC 3.5.1.98 (histone deacetylase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and an apoptosis inducer. It is a member of indoles, a secondary amino compound, a monocarboxylic acid amide and a hydroxamic acid.

The molecule is an ethyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of vanillic acid with ethanol. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an antibacterial agent. It derives from a vanillic acid.

The molecule is a monoterpenoid that consists of (+)-pantothenic acid having an alpha-L-rhamnosyl residue attached at position C-2. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a human xenobiotic metabolite. It is a monoterpenoid, a monosaccharide derivative, an aldehyde and a glycoside.

The molecule is a 2-pyranone in which the hydrogens at positions 4, 5 and 6 of 2H-pyran-2-one are replaced by hydroxy, methyl and heptadecyl groups respectively. It is a member of 2-pyranones, an enol and a heteroaryl hydroxy compound.
The molecule is an N-acyl-4-hydroxy-15-methylhexadecasphinganine-1-phosphocholine in which the acyl group has 29 carbons and 0 double bonds. It derives from a 15-methylhexadecaphytosphingosine.

The molecule is a dihydrolipoic acid that consists of octanoic acid bearing two (R)-sulfanyl substituents at positions 3 and 8. It has a role as an antioxidant, a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite.
The molecule is a disaccharide derivative that consists of 6-sulfated beta-D-glucose having an alpha-L-sulfated sulfogalactosyl residue attached at position 4. It has a role as an epitope.
The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of the secondary amino function of (R)-tetrindole. It is a conjugate acid of a (R)-tetrindole. It is an enantiomer of a (S)-tetrindole(1+).

The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups positions 1 and 2 are specified as alpha-linolenoyl and (8Z,11Z,14Z)-icosatrienoyl respectively. It has a role as a human blood serum metabolite. It derives from an all-cis-icosa-8,11,14-trienoic acid and an alpha-linolenic acid.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid that consists of propionic acid bearing a single amino substituent at position 2. It has a role as a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a propionic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a L-2-aminopropionate. It is a tautomer of a L-alanine zwitterion.
The molecule is a dipeptide composed of glycine and L-histidine joined by a peptide linkage. It has a role as a metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite.

The molecule is an N-acyl-L-alpha-amino acid anion that is the conjugate base of N-[15(S)-hydroperoxy-(5Z,8Z,11Z,13E)]-icosatetraenoyl-L-alanine, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It is a N-acyl-L-alpha-amino acid anion and a N-(fatty acyl)-L-alpha-amino acid anion. It derives from a 15(S)-HPETE(1-). It is a conjugate base of a N-[15(S)-hydroperoxy-(5Z,8Z,11Z,13E)-icosatetraenoyl]-L-alanine.
The molecule is a diterpenyl phosphate that is the O-diphospho derivative of (+)-kolavenol It derives from a (+)-kolavenol. It is an enantiomer of a (-)-kolavenyl diphosphate.

The molecule is a tetrachlorobiphenyl that is biphenyl in which the hydrogens at positions 2 and 5 have been replaced by chlorines. It has a role as an environmental contaminant, a xenobiotic and a herbicide.

The molecule is a tripeptide composed of L-phenylalanine, L-alanyl and L-aspartic acid joined in sequence by peptide linkages. It has a role as a metabolite. It derives from a L-phenylalanine, a L-alanine and a L-aspartic acid.

The molecule is a straight-chain saturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of dotriacontanoic acid (melissic acid), obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a plant metabolite. It is a very long-chain fatty acid anion, a straight-chain saturated fatty acid anion and an ultra-long-chain fatty acid anion. It derives from a hexatriacontanoate. It is a conjugate base of a dotriacontanoic acid.
The molecule is the hydrochloride salt of cyclizine. It has a role as an antipruritic drug, a H1-receptor antagonist and an antitussive. It contains a cyclizine.
The molecule is an organic thiophosphate and an organothiophosphate insecticide. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor, an acaricide and an agrochemical.

The molecule is a flavanone glycoside that consists of naringenin substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 5, 2' and 4', a methyl group at position 6 and a trans-4 coumaryloxy residue at position 8. Isolated from the leaves of Myrcia multiflora, it exhibits inhibitory activity against alpha-glucosidase and aldose reductase. It has a role as an EC 3.2.1.20 (alpha-amylase) inhibitor, an EC 1.1.1.21 (aldehyde reductase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a cinnamate ester, a dihydroxyflavanone, a flavanone glycoside, a monosaccharide derivative and a member of 4'-hydroxyflavanones. It derives from a trans-4-coumaric acid.

The molecule is a long-chain fatty acid that consists of (9Z)-octadecenoic acid having an alpha-linolenoyloxy group at position 2 and a beta-D-glucopyranosyloxy group at position 18. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a monounsaturated fatty acid, a long-chain fatty acid and a monosaccharide derivative.

The molecule is a nucleoside analogue in which the purine fragment has been modified by replacement of one hydrogen at position 2 on the adenine ring by a hydroxy group and by substitution at positions N-6 and C-8 on the guanine ring. It derives from an adenosine.

The molecule is a member of the class of 1,4-naphthoquinones that is 1,4-naphthoquinone in which one of the hydrogens at position 2 has been replaced by an oxo group. It derives from a 1,4-naphthoquinone.

The molecule is a benzoate ester obtained by the formal condensation of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid with ethanol. It has been isolated from Pisonia aculeata and exhibits antitubercular activity. It has a role as an antitubercular agent, a plant metabolite and an EC 3.6.3.10 (H(+)/K(+)-exchanging ATPase) inhibitor. It derives from a 4-hydroxybenzoic acid.

The molecule is a steroid alkaloid that consists of 5alpha-androstane having acetoxy groups at the 3beta and 17 positions, an oxo group at position 16 and a morpholinoethyl side chain at the 20beta position. It has a role as an antidiarrhoeal drug and a muscarinic antagonist. It is a quaternary ammonium ion, a steroid alkaloid, a tertiary alcohol, an acetate ester and a member of morpholines.

The molecule is an acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of 3-hydroxy-3-phenylpropanoic acid. It derives from a 3-hydroxy-3-phenylpropionic acid and a propionyl-CoA.

The molecule is a diterpene glycoside that consists of 13,20-epoxylimenic acid attached to a beta-D-glucopyranosyl residue at position 16 via a glycosidic linkage. Isolated from the aerial parts of Inula hupehensis it exhibits antineoplastic activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a cyclic ether, a bridged compound, a diterpenoid, a secondary alcohol, an acetate ester, a beta-D-glucoside and a diterpene glycoside. It derives from a limenene.

The molecule is a beta-D-glucoside in which a 2-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)acetyl group and a beta-D-glucopyranosyloxy residue are attached at positions 1 and 6 respectively of phloroglucinol. It has been isolated from the aerial parts of Vicia faba and exhibits inhibitory activity against alpha-amylase. It has a role as an EC 3.2.1.1 (alpha-amylase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a member of catechols, a monosaccharide derivative, a beta-D-glucoside and a polyphenol.

The molecule is a member of the class of benzophenones that is 2,3-dihydroxybenzophenone substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 5 and 6, a methyl group at position 4', a prenyl group at position 3' and a (1E)-3-methylbut-1-en-1-yl group at position 7. Isolated from Chaetomium brasiliense it exhibits cytotoxic activity against human tumor cells. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a Chaetomium metabolite. It is a member of resorcinols, a benzenetriol, a polyketide, a cyclic ketone, a polyphenol, an aromatic ether and a member of benzophenones.

The molecule is a member of the class of xanthones that is 2H-xanthene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1, 3, 6 and 8, a (E)-4-[(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)methylidene]cyclopenta-2,5-dien-1-ylidene group at position 2, an oxo group at position 9 and a 7,4'-dihydroxyflavanone moiety at position 10. Isolated from Garcinia vieillardii, it exhibits antioxidant activity. It has a role as a metabolite and an antioxidant. It is a polyphenol, a cyclic ketone, a member of xanthones and a tetrahydroxyflavone.
The molecule is a member of indoles, a member of maleimides and a member of 2,1-benzoxazoles. It has a role as an EC 3.4.23.46 (memapsin 2) inhibitor.
The molecule is a metal acetate salt having thallium(1+) as the counterion. It has a role as an allergen and a miotic. It contains a thallium(1+).

The molecule is a lignan that consists of (+)-lariciresinol substituted by an alpha-L-arabinopyranosyl moiety at position 4 via a glycosidic linkage. It has been isolated from the roots and stems of Sinocalamus affinis. It has a role as a plant metabolite, an antioxidant and an anti-inflammatory agent. It is a member of benzodioxoles, a furofuran, a primary alcohol, a secondary alcohol, a lignan and a glycosyloxyisoflavan. It derives from a (+)-lariciresinol.

The molecule is a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid with formula C21H24N2O3, isolated from several species of Tabernaemontana. It has a role as an EC 3.1.1.7 (acetylcholinesterase) inhibitor and a plant metabolite. It is a methyl ketone, an organic heteropentacyclic compound, a primary alcohol, a tertiary amino compound, a monoterpenoid indole alkaloid and an acetate ester.

The molecule is a hexaric acid anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy groups of 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an Escherichia coli metabolite and a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite. It derives from a D-gluconate(2-). It is a conjugate base of a 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid zwitterion that is tryptophan in which a proton has been transferred from the carboxy group to the amino group. It is the major species at pH 7.3. It is a tautomer of a tryptophan.

The molecule is an alpha-amino-acid anion obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of aspartic acid. It has a role as a fundamental metabolite. It derives from a propionate. It is a conjugate base of an aspartate(1-) and an aspartate.

The molecule is a glycosyloxyflavone that consists of kaempferol attached to a alpha-L-rhamnopyranosyl(1->2)-beta-D-glucopyranoside moiety at position 3 via a glycosidic linkage. Isolated from the aerial parts of Vicia faba and Lotus edulis, it exhibits inhibitory activity against topoisomerase I. It has a role as an EC 5.99.1.2 (DNA topoisomerase) inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a disaccharide derivative, a dihydroxyflavone and a glycosyloxyflavone. It derives from a kaempferol.

The molecule is an organic disulfide isolated from the culture broth of Streptomyces sp. A-235 that exhibits inhibitory activity against acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase 2. It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an EC 2.3.1.26 (sterol O-acyltransferase) inhibitor and a bacterial metabolite. It is an organic heteropentacyclic compound, an oxacycle, a cyclic ketone, a primary alcohol, an organosulfur heterocyclic compound, a tertiary amino compound and an organic disulfide.

The molecule is a 3-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (R)-3-hydroxytetracosanoic acid. It is a (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA, a 3-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA and an ultra-long-chain fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (R)-3-hydroxylignoceric acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (R)-3-hydroxylignocenoyl-CoA(4-).

The molecule is a hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion that results from the removal of a proton from the carboxylic acid group of glyceric acid. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a human metabolite. It derives from a propionate. It is a conjugate base of a glycerol.

The molecule is a branched amino hexasaccharide comprising alpha-D-galactose at the reducing end with an N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminyl-(1->3)-[beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)]-[beta-D-xylosyl-(1->2)]-beta-D-mannosyl moiety attached via a (1->6)-linkage and an L-fucosyl residue attached via a (1->3)-linkage. It has a role as an epitope.

The molecule is a monocarboxylic acid amide formed between N(alpha)-[4-guanidinoethyl]-L-leucyl-D-valine and 2-aminoacetic acid. It derives from an alicyclic carboxylic acid, a D-valine derivative and a guanidine.

The molecule is a fluorinated steroid, an 11beta-hydroxy steroid, a 20-oxo steroid, a 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid, a primary alpha-hydroxy ketone and a tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory drug.
The molecule is a hydrate that is the hexahydrate form of manganese(II) sulfate. It has a role as a nutraceutical and a mordant. It contains a manganese(II) sulfate (anhydrous).

The molecule is a biflavonoid isolated from the stem bark of Morus nigra and has been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory activity. It has a role as an anti-inflammatory agent, a plant metabolite and a NF-kappaB inhibitor. It is a biflavonoid, a hydroxyflavone and a ring assembly.
The molecule is a tripeptide composed of L-leucine, L-tyrosine and 4-methylumbelliferylglycine residues joined in sequence. It has a role as a chromogenic compound.
The molecule is a butan-4-olide having an (sulfomethyl)oxy group at the 3-position and two methyl substituents at the 5-position. It derives from a methanesulfonic acid.
The molecule is a 2-coumaric acid in which the double bond has Z configuration. It derives from an acrylic acid.

The molecule is a 3-chloroalanine that has R at the chiral carbon. It has a role as an EC 1.4.3.4 (diaminopropionate ammonia-lyase) inhibitor, a bacterial metabolite and a marine metabolite. It is a L-threonine derivative, a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid and a 3-chloroalanine. It is an enantiomer of a 3-chloro-D-alanine.

The molecule is a monomethoxyflavone that is the 4'-methoxy derivative of quercetin. It has been isolated from Combretum quadrangulare and Zanthoxylum piperitum. It has a role as an antiplasmodial drug, an antineoplastic agent, a plant metabolite and a radical scavenger. It is a trihydroxyflavone and a monomethoxyflavone. It derives from a quercetin.
The molecule is a sulfur oxoanion. It is a conjugate base of an trithionic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a trioxidosulfate(2-) and a trithiocarbonate(3-).

The molecule is an organic cation obtained by protonation of all five amino groups of N(4)-aminopropylspermidine. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a eukaryotic metabolite. It is an ammonium ion derivative and an organic cation. It is a conjugate acid of a N(4)-ammoniopropylspermidine.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acid that is octadecanoic acid with triple bonds at positions 13 and 16, and a furan-2-yl group substituted at position 5. It has a role as an apoptosis inducer and a plant metabolite. It is a monocarboxylic acid, a polyunsaturated fatty acid and a member of furans.
The molecule is an amino disaccharide consisting of two 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-D-galactopyranose residues joined by a (1->6) glycosidic bond. It is an amino disaccharide and a member of acetamides.

The molecule is a triol that consists of propane-1,2,3-triol bearing two 2-hydroxyethyl substituents at position 1 and one hydroxyethyl substituent at position 4. It has a role as an epitope. It derives from a hydride of a propane.

The molecule is a member of the class of oxazolidinones isolated from the marine sponge Petrosia. It has been shown to exhibit cytotoxicity against human tumour cells. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent, an animal metabolite and a marine metabolite. It is a member of benzyl alcohols, an ether, a lactam and an oxazolidinone.

The molecule is a methyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of indole-3-acetic acid with methanol. It has a role as an Arabidopsis thaliana metabolite and a plant metabolite. It derives from an indole-3-acetic acid.

The molecule is a dioxo monocarboxylic acid that consists of glutaramic acid bearing an oxo substituent at position 2 as well as an amino substituent at position 5. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a glutaramic acid.
The molecule is an ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of both amino groups of (R,S)-nebivolol. It derives from a levobunolol(1+). It is a conjugate acid of a (R,S)-nebivolol.

The molecule is a hydroxycalciol that consists of vitamin D3 (calciol) carrying additional hydroxy groups at positions 20 and 24 as well as an oxo group at position 1. An intermediate in the synthesis of calcitriol It has a role as a human metabolite, a rat metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a triol, a member of oxolanes, a cyclic ether, a hydroxycalciol and a diol.

The molecule is a diterpene glycoside that consists of (2E,6E)-farnesyllinalool attached to two beta-D-glucopyranosyloxy groups at positions 13 and 20. Isolated from the aerial parts of Ajuga bracteosa, it exhibits antileishmanial activity. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a plant metabolite. It is a disaccharide derivative, a diterpene glycoside and a macrocyclic lactone.

The molecule is an alpha-amino acid anion that is the conjugate base of glutamine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group. It has a role as a fundamental metabolite. It derives from a glutarate(1-). It is a conjugate base of a glutamine and a glutamine zwitterion.

The molecule is a 2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid that is lactic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens at position 3 has been replaced by an imidazol-4-yl group. It has a role as a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a member of imidazoles and a 2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid. It derives from a rac-lactic acid.

The molecule is a pyridone that is pyridine-2,5-dione substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 6 and a (1S,4R,5S)-1,4,5-trimethylcyclohexyl group at position 3. It has been isolated from Aspergillus niger ATCC 1015. It has a role as an Aspergillus metabolite. It is a member of pyridones and a dihydroxypyridine.
The molecule is an organic triphosphate formed by condensation between the gamma-phospho group of 2'-deoxyadenosine 5'-triphosphate and ethanol. It derives from a dTTP and an ethanol.

The molecule is a 3-oxo-fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (15Z)-3-oxotetracosenoic acid. It is an unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA and a 3-oxo-fatty acyl-CoA. It derives from a (15Z)-3-oxotetracosenoic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a (15Z)-3-oxotetracosenoyl-CoA(4-).
The molecule is a sulfonamide consisting of cyclohexane having an N-sulfonylamino group. It has a role as a human metabolite and a mouse metabolite.
The molecule is an anionic C3 cyanine-type compound having indoleinine and dihydropyrano[3,2-g]quinoline substituents at either end. It has a role as a fluorochrome.

The molecule is a 4-hydroxy-2-(propan-2-yl)cyclohexanol in which the stereocentre at position 4 has R configuration, while that at position 2 has S configuration. It is an enantiomer of a (+)-(2S,4R)-myristic acid.

The molecule is a nitrile that consists of N,N-dimethylformamide bearing an additional (6-chloropyridin-3-yl)methyl substituent at position 1 as well as a cyano group at position 2. It has a role as a metabolite and an environmental contaminant. It derives from a N,N-dimethylformamide.
The molecule is a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as palmitoyl. It has a role as a mouse metabolite. It derives from a hexadecanoic acid.

The molecule is a straight chain alkane containing 19 carbon atoms. It has been isolated from the essential oils of several plants including Sideritis diphylla and Zanthoxylum piperitum. It has a role as an antibacterial agent, a volatile oil component and a plant metabolite.

The molecule is a ceramide phosphoinositol compound having a hexacosanoyl group amide-linked to a C20 phytosphingosine base, with no hydroxylation at C-4 of the long-chain base or on the very-long-chain fatty acid.

The molecule is a 2-hydroxy fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 2-hydroxydecanoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an algal metabolite and a marine xenobiotic metabolite. It derives from a decanoate. It is a conjugate base of a 2-hydroxydecanoic acid.

The molecule is a 19-membered cyclodepsipeptide isolated from the culture broth of Penicillium sp. It exhibits potent inhibitory activity against chymotrypsin (EC 3.4.21.1) and trypsin (EC 3.4.21.4). It has a role as an antimicrobial agent, an EC 3.4.21.1 (chymotrypsin) inhibitor and an EC 3.4.21.4 (trypsin) inhibitor. It is a macrocycle and a cyclodepsipeptide.
The molecule is a sulfur hydride. It is a conjugate base of an trithionic acid. It is a conjugate acid of a trianion(2-).

The molecule is a secondary carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2-hydroxy-3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid with the amino group of 4-(trifluoromethyl)aniline in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen has been replaced by a cyano group while the other hydrogen has been replaced by a p-[sulfonyl(phenyl)methyl]amino group. It is an organofluorine compound, a nitrile, a sulfone and a secondary carboxamide.

The molecule is a polyunsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4-) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of (13Z,16Z)-docosadienoyl-CoA. It is an (11Z)-Delta(11)-fatty acyl-CoA(4-) and a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4-). It is a conjugate base of a (13Z,16Z)-docosadienoyl-CoA.
The molecule is a dipeptide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-threonine with the amino group of L-isoleucine. It derives from a L-threonine and a L-isoleucine.
The molecule is a beta-D-galactoside that is the 2-aminoethyl glycoside of beta-D-glucuronic acid. It has a role as an epitope and a mouse metabolite. It derives from a beta-D-glucuronic acid.

The molecule is a 15-HPETE(1-) that is the conjugate base of 15(S)-HPETE, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from an all-cis-icosa-8,11,14-trienoate. It is a conjugate base of a 15(S)-HPETE.

The molecule is a tricyclic diterpenoid isolated from the stem bark of Fraxinus sieboldiana. It has a role as a plant metabolite and an anti-inflammatory agent. It is a cyclic terpene ketone, a member of phenols, an aromatic ether and a tricyclic diterpenoid.
The molecule is an organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of 6-hydro-beta-NADP; major species at pH 7.3. It derives from a beta-NAD(+).

The molecule is a phenolate anion that is the conjugate base of L-ascorbic acid, obtained by deprotonation of one of the two hydroxy groups at position 3; major species at pH 7.3. It has a role as an antioxidant and a plant metabolite. It derives from a L-arabinonate. It is a conjugate base of a L-ascorbic acid.

The molecule is a 2,3-trans-enoyl CoA(4-) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of trans-2-icosenoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3. It is a conjugate base of a trans-2-icosenoyl-CoA.

The molecule is a cinnamate ester obtained by the formal condensation of hydroxy group of 4-hydroxycinnamic acid with methoxyacetic acid. It has been isolated from Pisonia aculeata and Piper nigrum. It has a role as an antifeedant, a plant metabolite and an antifungal agent. It derives from a 4-hydroxycinnamic acid and a methoxyacetic acid.

The molecule is a hydrochloride obtained by combining equimolar amounts of metoclopramide and hydrogen chloride. It has a role as an antiemetic, a gastrointestinal drug, a dopaminergic antagonist and a serotonergic agonist. It contains a metoclopramide(2+).

The molecule is a member of the class of 2,6-diaminopurines that is 2,6-diamino-9H-purine carrying additional piperidin-4-yl and (morpholin-4-ylmethyl)nitrilo groups at positions 5 and 8 respectively. It has a role as an EC 2.7.10.1 (receptor protein-tyrosine kinase) inhibitor. It is a member of morpholines, a secondary amino compound, a tertiary amino compound, a member of piperidines and a member of 2,6-diaminopurines.
The molecule is an L-leucine derivative that is the methyl ester of (3S)-3-methyl-L-leucine. It has a role as a metabolite and a bacterial metabolite.

The molecule is a member of the class of thiazolidinones that is N-acetyl-D-threonyl-L-cysteinamide in which one of the hydrogens attached to the sulfur has been replaced by an (R)-1,5-dihydroxy-3-methylpentan-2-yl group. It has a role as a bacterial metabolite and an antifungal agent. It is a L-cysteine derivative, a non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid, a secondary alcohol, a diol, a member of acetamides and a thiazolidinone.
